<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:anmext}
A function $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ is a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine
extractor if, for every affine source $X$ of dimension at least $k$ and
every affine map $T:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^n$ with no fixed points,
\[
 (F(X),F(T(X)))\approx_\varepsilon(U_m,F(T(X))).
\]
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{intro:linear}\label{thm:affine-linear}
For every constant $0<\rho\le1$, there are constants
$c_\rho,e_\rho>0$ and an explicit family
$\mathsf{anmExt}_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{m_n}$ with output length $m_n\ge c_\rho n$
and the following property for all sufficiently large $n$.
For every affine source $X$ with $H_\infty(X)\ge\rho n$ and every affine
map $T$ with $T(x)\ne x$ for all $x\in\mathsf{Supp}(X)$,
\[
 (\mathsf{anmExt}_n(X),\mathsf{anmExt}_n(T(X)))
 \approx_{2^{-e_\rho n}}(U_{m_n},\mathsf{anmExt}_n(T(X))).
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{intro:sublinear}\label{thm:affine-sublinear}
For every fixed $0<\eta<1$ and integer $h\ge1$, there is a constant
$C_{\eta,h}>0$ and a uniformly polynomial-time computable family
$\mathsf{anmExt}_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{m_n}$ with
$m_n\ge\lfloor n^{1-\eta}\rfloor$ and the following property for all
sufficiently large $n$. For every affine source $X$ of entropy at least
\[
 k=\left\lceil\frac{C_{\eta,h}n}{\log n}\right\rceil
\]
and affine maps $T_1,\ldots,T_h$ with no fixed point on $\mathsf{Supp}(X)$,
\[
 \bigl(\mathsf{anmExt}_n(X),(\mathsf{anmExt}_n(T_j(X)))_{j\in[h]}\bigr)
 \approx_{2^{-n^{1-\eta}}}
 \bigl(U_{m_n},(\mathsf{anmExt}_n(T_j(X)))_{j\in[h]}\bigr).
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:directional-intro}
A function $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ is a $(k,\varepsilon)$ directional
affine extractor if, for every affine source $X$ of dimension at least
$k$ and every nonzero $a\in\mathsf{F}_2^n$,
\[
 (F(X),F(X+a))\approx_\varepsilon(U_m,F(X+a)).
\]
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:directional-hardness-intro}
Let $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ have directional derivative bias at most
$\beta$ at entropy $k$. If $1\le q<n$ and $2q-n\ge k$, then every size-$s$ weakly
read-once linear branching program $P$ satisfies
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{x\sim U_n}(-1)^{f(x)+P(x)}\right|
 \le\sqrt{2s\bigl(\beta+2^{-(n-q)}\bigr)}.
\]
Consequently, if $F$ is a $(k,\varepsilon)$ directional affine
extractor and $k\le n-2$, each nonzero output parity of $F$ has
correlation at most
$\sqrt{2s(2\varepsilon+2^{-\lfloor(n-k)/2\rfloor})}$ with $P$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{intro:weak}\label{thm:affine-hardness-intro}
Let $1\le k<n$, and let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable
affine extractor. For every $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^m\setminus\{0\}$ and every
size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program $P$,
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{x\sim U_n}(-1)^{\langle u,F(x)\rangle+P(x)}\right|
 \le\sqrt{2s\bigl(2\varepsilon+2^{-(n-k)}\bigr)}.
\]
If $k\le n-2$, $\varepsilon\le1/2$, and $R\sim U_t$ is independent
of $X\sim U_n$, then, for every $t\ge0$ and every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program $P$ on $(X,R)$,
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{X,R}(-1)^{\langle u,F(X)\rangle+P(X,R)}\right|
 \le\sqrt{2s\left(2\varepsilon+
 (1-2\varepsilon)2^{-(n-k-1)}\right)}.
\]
In both statements, non-malleability against globally fixed-point-free
affine involutions suffices; an involution is a map $T$ satisfying
$T(T(x))=x$ for every $x$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{intro:hardness}\label{cor:exponential-average-hardness}
There are constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and an explicit Boolean function family
$f_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every
weakly read-once linear branching program $P$ of size at most $2^{c_1n}$
satisfies
\[
 \mathbf{Pr}[P(U_n)=f_n(U_n)]\le\frac12+2^{-c_2n}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{intro:quadratic-adaptivity}
There is an absolute constant $C>0$ with the following
properties for all sufficiently large $n$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every fixed $0<\eta<1$, there is an explicit non-malleable
affine extractor $F_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{m_n}$ with output length
$m_n=\lceil n^{1-\eta}\rceil$, error $\varepsilon_n\le2^{-n^{1-\eta}}$,
and entropy threshold
\[
 k_n=\left\lceil\frac{Cn\log\log n}{\log n}\right\rceil.
\]
Every nonzero output parity $f_n$ satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 n^{1-\eta}-1&\le D_2(f_n)\le D_2(F_n)\le n^{1-\eta+o(1)},\\
 D_2^{\mathrm{obl}}(f_n)&\ge n-k_n+1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
\item For every fixed $a,e>0$, there is an explicit non-malleable
affine extractor $G_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{\lceil a\log n\rceil}$
with entropy threshold
$k_n=\lceil Cn\log\log\log n/\log\log n\rceil$
and error at most $n^{-e}$, such that every nonzero output parity $g_n$
satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Omega(\log n)&\le D_2(g_n)\le D_2(G_n)\le(\log n)^{1+o(1)},\\
 D_2^{\mathrm{obl}}(g_n)&\ge n-k_n+1=n-o(n).
 \end{aligned}
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{intro:fixed-degree-depth}
Fix $0<\rho\le1$ and an integer $h\ge1$. For all sufficiently large
$n$, every integer $m\ge1$ and real $E\ge1$ with
$m+E\le c_{\rho,h}n$, for a sufficiently small constant
$c_{\rho,h}>0$, admit an explicit $m$-bit non-malleable affine
extractor $F_h$ at entropy $\lceil\rho n\rceil$, with error at most
$2^{-E}$ against $h$ affine tamperings, such that
\[
 D_2(F_h)\le O_{\rho,h}(m+E+\log n).
\]
Suppose, in addition, that the parameters satisfy the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item Entropy rate: $\rho<1/2$.
\item Query degree and number of tamperings: $r\ge2$ is fixed and
$h\ge\max\{1,2^{r-2}-1\}$.
\item Output length and error exponent: $m\le E$ and $E\ge\log n$.
\end{itemize}
Then every nonzero output parity $f$ satisfies
\[
 \frac{E}{2^{r-2}}-O_r(1)
 \le D_r(f)\le D_r(F_h)\le O_{\rho,h}(E).
\]
Thus both $D_r(f)$ and $D_r(F_h)$ are $\Theta_{\rho,h,r}(E)$.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{intro:local-depth}
The following statements hold for growing locality $\ell$.
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Sumset extractors.}
Fix $0<\delta<1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. There are an explicit
Boolean family $S_n$, independent of $\ell$, and a constant
$c_\delta>0$ such that, for $\ell\le n^{1-\delta}$, every non-oblivious
$\ell$-local tree $T$ of depth at most $c_\delta(n/\ell)\log\ell$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Corr}(S_n,T)\le2\varepsilon(1+o(1)).
\]
In particular, $\operatorname{LDT}_\ell(S_n)
=\Omega_\delta((n/\ell)\log\ell)$.
\item \emph{Directional affine extractors.}
Fix $0<\rho<1/2$ and $a>0$. Suppose $F_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{m_n}$
is a directional affine extractor at dimension $\lceil\rho n\rceil$
with error at most $2^{-an}$. There is $C_\rho>0$ such that,
for $\ell\le n/(C_\rho\log n)$, every nonzero output parity $f_n$
and every non-oblivious $\ell$-local tree $T$ of depth at most
\[
 \left\lfloor\frac{n}{4\ell}\frac{\log\ell}{\log\log\ell}\right\rfloor
\]
satisfy $\operatorname{Corr}(f_n,T)\le2^{-\Omega(n/\sqrt\ell)}$.
Consequently,
$\operatorname{LDT}_\ell(f_n)
=\Omega((n/\ell)\log\ell/\log\log\ell)$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:lifting-intro}
There are constants $c,C>0$ and a deterministic polynomial-time
construction of unsatisfiable CNFs $\Psi_m$ on
$N=\Theta(m\log m)$ variables, of polynomial size and width
$O(\log m)$, such that every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ refutation
of $\Psi_m$ of depth $d$ and size $S$ satisfies
\[
 d\left(\log S+C\frac{N}{\log N}\right)\ge cN^2.
\]
In particular, for every fixed $a>0$, refutations of depth at most $aN$
have size $2^{\Omega_a(N)}$. The same conclusion applies to top-regular
and bottom-regular refutations.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{intro:quadratic}
For every sufficiently large $N$, there is a uniformly polynomial-time
constructible, polynomial-size unsatisfiable CNF $\Psi_N$ on exactly
$N$ variables with a polynomial-size ordinary-resolution refutation,
such that every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ refutation of size $S$
and resolution depth $d$ satisfies
\[
                         d\log(2S)=\Omega(N^2).
\]
All variables, including padding variables, are counted.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{pre:entropy}
If $V$ has a range of size at most $2^b$, then
\[
 \widetilde{H}_\infty(X\mid Z,V)\ge\widetilde{H}_\infty(X\mid Z)-b.
\]
Moreover, if $\widetilde{H}_\infty(X\mid Z)\ge k+q$, then
\[
 \mathbf{Pr}_z[H_\infty(X\mid Z=z)<k]\le2^{-q}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For the first assertion, write
\[
 2^{-\widetilde{H}_\infty(X\mid Z,V)}
 =\sum_{z,v}\max_x\mathbf{Pr}[X=x,Z=z,V=v]
 \le 2^b\sum_z\max_x\mathbf{Pr}[X=x,Z=z]
 =2^b 2^{-\widetilde{H}_\infty(X\mid Z)}.
\]
The second assertion is Markov's inequality applied to
$\max_x\mathbf{Pr}[X=x\mid Z]$, whose expectation is at most $2^{-k-q}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
A function $L:\{0,1\}^N\times\{0,1\}^d\to\{0,1\}^r$ is a strong $(k,\epsilon)$
seeded extractor if, for every $X$ with $H_\infty(X)\ge k$ and independent
uniform $Y\in\{0,1\}^d$,
\[
 (L(X,Y),Y)\approx_\epsilon(U_r,Y).
\]
We call $L$ a \emph{linear seeded extractor} if $L(\cdot,y)$ is linear
for every fixed seed $y$, as in~\cite{Li11b,LZdir}.
No linearity in the seed is required.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{pre:merge}
Suppose $(A,A')\perp(Y,Y')\mid Z$ and
\[
 (Y,Y',Z)\approx_\delta(U_d,Y',Z).
\]
Let $L:\{0,1\}^N\times\{0,1\}^d\to\{0,1\}^r$ be a strong
$(k,\epsilon)$ extractor. If
\[
 \widetilde{H}_\infty(A\mid Z)\ge k+r+\log(1/\epsilon),
\]
then
\[
 (L(A,Y),L(A',Y'),Y,Y',Z)
 \approx_{\delta+2\epsilon}
 (U_r,L(A',Y'),Y,Y',Z).
\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
First suppose $Y$ is uniform independently of $(Y',Z)$, retaining the given
conditional law of $(A,A')$. Fix $Z,Y'$ and the output $L(A',Y')$.
Independence and \Cref{pre:entropy} give average remaining entropy of
$A$ at least $k+\log(1/\epsilon)$. The seed $Y$ remains independent
uniform, so the average-case strong-extractor guarantee gives error at most $2\epsilon$.

For the general seed law, fix $(y,y',z)$ and use the law of $(A,A')$ given
$Z=z$. The distance of $(L(A,y),L(A',y'))$ from $(U_r,L(A',y'))$ is
a function of $(y,y',z)$ taking values in $[0,1]$.
Changing the marginal of $(Y,Y',Z)$ to $(U_d,Y',Z)$ changes its expectation
by at most $\delta$. Conditional independence ensures that this conditional law remains
unchanged. This proves the assertion, including the
retention of both seeds. This is the $t=1$ case of
the independence-merging lemma in~\cite[Lemma 3.26]{CL22}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{pre:fibers-sections}
Let $A=x_0+V$ be an affine subspace and let $J$ be an affine map.
\begin{itemize}
\item For $a\in J(A)$, the \emph{fiber} over $a$ is
$A_a=\{x\in A:J(x)=a\}$. If $x_a\in A_a$, then
\[
 A_a=x_a+(V\cap\ker J_{\rm lin}).
\]
Thus all nonempty fibers have the same direction and dimension
$\dim V-\dim J_{\rm lin}(V)$.
\item An \emph{affine section} of $J|_A$ is an affine map
$\sigma:J(A)\to A$ such that $J(\sigma(a))=a$ for every $a\in J(A)$.
It is a right inverse of $J|_A$: its image contains exactly one point
of each fiber. A section is injective, and its image has dimension
$\dim J(A)$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{pre:affine}
Let $U$ be uniform on $u_0+V$, and let $J$ and $L$ be affine maps.
Every nonempty fiber $U\mid J(U)=j$ is uniform on a translate of
$V\cap\ker J_{\rm lin}$, where $J_{\rm lin}$ denotes the linear part.
Consequently, its conditional image entropy is independent of $j$ and
\[
 H(L(U)\mid J(U))\ge H(L(U))-H(J(U)).
\]
In particular, imposing at most $b$ affine constraints reduces the rank of
every affine image by at most $b$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Every consistent system $J(u)=j$ gives a coset of the stated kernel.
The codimension of that kernel in $V$ is $H(J(U))$. The dimension of a
linear image decreases by at most the codimension of a restriction of its
domain, proving the inequality.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{pre:reservoir}
Let $(Q,Q')$ be jointly affine, and let $J$ be an affine map on the joint
space with output length $r$. There are independent jointly affine tuples
$(A,A')$ and $(B,B')$ such that
\[
 (Q,Q')=(A,A')+(B,B'),
\]
$J(Q,Q')$ is determined by $(B,B')$, and
\[
 H(A)\ge H(Q)-r.
\]
If $V$ is the direction of the joint support, one may take $(A,A')$
uniform on $V\cap\ker J_{\rm lin}$ and $(B,B')$ uniform on a translate
of a complementary subspace of $V$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Decompose the joint direction into that kernel and a complementary subspace,
and sample their coordinates independently and uniformly. Assign the affine
offset to the complement. The kernel has codimension at most $r$, so its
selected projection loses at most $r$ dimensions by \Cref{pre:affine}.
The selected projection need not be injective, and no functional relation
between $Q$ and $Q'$ is used.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{pre:query-def}
We shall repeatedly fix affine functions of a source $U$ in succession.
Each bit has the form $\lambda(U)+b$, where $\lambda$ is linear. The
choice of $\lambda,b$, and whether to stop, depend only on the values
fixed previously and on fixed external parameters. At each step we
condition separately on every value of positive probability.
The resulting supports form an \emph{affine partition}: a partition
into affine subspaces. Its parts may have different directions or
dimensions, because the functions fixed later can depend on earlier
values. The function recording the complete sequence need not be
affine; the next lemma shows that each of its nonempty fibers is
nevertheless an affine subspace.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{pre:queries}
Suppose we successively fix at most $L$ affine functions of an affine
source $U$ as above. Conditioned on any possible sequence of values,
$U$ is an affine source whose support has codimension at most $L$ in
the original support. The entropy of any fixed affine image of $U$
decreases by at most $L$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Once the sequence of values is specified, each fixing imposes one
affine equation. Their conjunction defines the corresponding conditional
support. Apply \Cref{pre:affine}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{pre:rank}
Let $L:\mathsf{F}_2^N\times\{0,1\}^d\to\mathsf{F}_2^r$ be a strong linear seeded
$(k,\epsilon)$ extractor. For a fixed linear subspace $V\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^N$
of dimension at least $k$, put
\[
 \mathcal B_V=\{y:\mathsf{rank}(L(\cdot,y)|_V)<r\}.
\]
Then $\mathbf{Pr}_{U_d}[\mathcal B_V]\le2\epsilon$. Every seed outside this set
gives an exactly uniform output on every translate of $V$.
If $Y\approx_\eta U_d$, then
\[
 \mathbf{Pr}[Y\in\mathcal B_V]\le\eta+2\epsilon.
\]
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $U_V$ denote the uniform distribution on $V$. For a fixed seed,
$L(U_V,y)$ is uniform on a linear image. A proper
image has distance at least $1/2$ from $U_r$. Average over an independent
uniform seed in the strong-extractor guarantee. Translation of the source
only translates its image, and statistical distance bounds the change in
the probability of the fixed bad-seed set.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{pre:t-affine-nm}
For $t\ge1$, a function $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ is a
$(k,\epsilon)$ $t$-non-malleable affine extractor if, for every affine
source $X$ with $H(X)\ge k$ and affine maps $T_1,\ldots,T_t$ satisfying
$T_j(x)\ne x$ for every $x\in\mathsf{Supp}(X)$,
\begin{equation}\label{pre:t-affine-nm-condition}
 \bigl(F(X),(F(T_j(X)))_{j\in[t]}\bigr)
 \approx_\epsilon
 \bigl(U_m,(F(T_j(X)))_{j\in[t]}\bigr).
\end{equation}
The uniform variable is independent of all comparison outputs together.
The maps may coincide and need not be invertible. Repeating maps gives
the same guarantee for fewer than $t$ tamperings.
For $t=0$, we use the convention that this means an ordinary
$(k,\epsilon)$ affine extractor.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{pre:affine-nm-equivalence}
\Cref{pre:t-affine-nm} is equivalent, with the same $k,m,\epsilon$,
to requiring
\[
 \bigl(F(X^0),(F(X^j))_{j\in[t]}\bigr)
 \approx_\epsilon
 \bigl(U_m,(F(X^j))_{j\in[t]}\bigr)
\]
for every jointly affine tuple $(X^0,\ldots,X^t)$ with
$H(X^0)\ge k$ and $\mathbf{Pr}[X^0=X^j]=0$ for $j>0$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Let $A$ be the joint support, $\pi_0$ its first-coordinate projection,
and $S=\pi_0(A)$. Choose an affine section $\sigma:S\to A$ as in
\Cref{pre:fibers-sections}. If $V$ is the direction of $A$, put
$K=V\cap\ker\pi_0$. The tuple has the representation
\[
 (X^0,\ldots,X^t)=\sigma(X^0)+W,
\]
where $W$ is uniform on $K$ and independent of $X^0$: the map
$(x,w)\mapsto\sigma(x)+w$ is a bijection from $S\times K$ to $A$.

Fixing $W=w$ preserves the law and entropy of $X^0$. Each remaining
coordinate is an affine function $T_{j,w}(X^0)$; extend this function
affinely from $S$ to $\mathsf{F}_2^n$. The pointwise inequalities persist on
every fiber. Apply Eqn.~\eqref{pre:t-affine-nm-condition} and average
over $w$, with no change in the error. Conversely, every tuple
$(X,T_1(X),\ldots,T_t(X))$ in the definition is jointly affine.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{pre:linear}
There is an absolute constant $C_L$ such that, for every pair of integers
$r,q\ge1$ and every $N\ge C_L(r+q)$, there is an explicit strong linear
seeded extractor on $N$-bit sources with the following parameters:
\begin{itemize}
\item output length $r$ and error $2^{-q}$;
\item entropy requirement at most $C_L(r+q)$;
\item seed length at most $C_L(r+q+\log N)$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{pre:linear-tunable}
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for positive integers
$t,m,p$ and $N\ge C(m+p)$, there is an explicit strong linear
seeded extractor on $N$ bits with
\begin{itemize}
\item output length $m$;
\item entropy requirement at most $C(m+p)$ and error $2^{-p}$;
\item seed length at most
$C(m/t+\log N+p+\log^2(t)(\log m+p))$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
A function $\mathsf{SCB}:\{0,1\}^N\times\{0,1\}^r\times\{0,1\}^a\to\{0,1\}^t$ is a
strong correlation breaker with advice for source entropy $r$ and error
$\epsilon$ if the following holds. Let $(V,V')$ and $(R,R')$ be arbitrary tuples satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item $(V,V')\perp(R,R')$;
\item $H_\infty(V)\ge r$;
\item $R=U_r$.
\end{itemize}
For distinct fixed advice strings $\alpha,\alpha'$, one has
\[
 (\mathsf{SCB}(V,R,\alpha),\mathsf{SCB}(V',R',\alpha'),R,R')
 \approx_\epsilon(U_t,\mathsf{SCB}(V',R',\alpha'),R,R').
\]
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{pre:scb}
There are absolute constants $C_S,c_S>0$ such that, whenever
$r\ge C_S(a+\log(N/\epsilon))$ and $r\le N$, there is an explicit
strong correlation breaker with advice as above with output length
$\lfloor c_Sr\rfloor$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{pre:affine-ext}
For every fixed $\alpha>0$ there are constants $\gamma_\alpha,
\xi_\alpha>0$ and an integer $D_\alpha$ and an explicit affine extractor
$E:\mathsf{F}_2^N\to\mathsf{F}_2^{\lfloor\gamma_\alpha N\rfloor}$ for entropy
$\alpha N$, with error at most $2^{-\xi_\alpha N}$, such that every
output bit has algebraic degree at most $D_\alpha$.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:overlap-legal-family}
Let $\varphi$ be an unsatisfiable CNF on $m$ variables and let
$1\le w\le m$. A family $\mathcal P$ of partial assignments has capacity
$w$ if it contains the empty assignment, is closed under restriction, and
satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item No member of $\mathcal P$ falsifies a clause of $\varphi$.
\item If $\rho\in\mathcal P$ has domain of size less than $w$ and $i$ is
unassigned, then at least one value of $i$ extends $\rho$ to a member of
$\mathcal P$.
\end{enumerate}
We restrict the family to domains of size at most $w$. For
$A\subseteq[m]$, $|A|\le w$, write $\mathcal P_A$ for its assignments
with domain exactly $A$. The family is affine if every $\mathcal P_A$ is
an affine subspace of $\mathsf{F}_2^A$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{cb:retained}
There is an absolute constant $C_{\rm cb}$ such that the following holds for
the construction in Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:construction}. Let $A,A',B,B'\in\{0,1\}^n$
and $Y,Y'\in\{0,1\}^d$ be random variables such that $(A,A')$ is
independent of $\mathcal C=(B,B',Y,Y')$. Put $X=A+B$ and
$X'=A'+B'$, and assume $H_\infty(A)\ge K$.  Fix distinct advice strings $\alpha,\alpha'$.  The
second computation uses $(X',Y',\alpha')$, and its intermediate variables
are marked by primes. There is a tuple $\mathcal T$ determining
\[
 B,B',Y,Y',R_1,R_1',S_2,S_2',\mathsf{ACB}(X',Y',\alpha')
\]
such that, if $Y=U_d$, then
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:retained}
 \Delta\bigl((\mathsf{ACB}(X,Y,\alpha),\mathcal T),(U_w,\mathcal T)\bigr)
 \le C_{\rm cb}\epsilon.
\end{equation}
The constant $C_{\rm cb}=20$ suffices.  More generally, if
$H_\infty(Y)\ge d-\lambda$, the right-hand side can be replaced by
$C_{\rm cb}2^\lambda\epsilon$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
We follow the conditioning argument for the affine correlation breaker,
allowing the two input sources to be arbitrarily correlated,
as in~\cite[Theorem~3.5]{Li23}.

Write $R_2=\mathsf{ACB}(X,Y,\alpha)$ and
$R_2'=\mathsf{ACB}(X',Y',\alpha')$. For $j=1,2$, define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{j,A}&=L_j(A,S_j), & R_{j,B}&=L_j(B,S_j),\\
 R_{j,A}'&=L_j(A',S_j'), & R_{j,B}'&=L_j(B',S_j').
 \end{aligned}
\]
Linearity gives $R_j=R_{j,A}+R_{j,B}$ and
$R_j'=R_{j,A}'+R_{j,B}'$, as in the affine correlation-breaker analysis
in~\cite[proof of Theorem~37]{LZdir}. Initially assume $Y=U_d$, and set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_0&=(S_1,S_1',R_{1,B},R_{1,B}'),\\
 T_1&=(T_0,R_1,R_1'),\\
 T_2&=(T_1,S_2,S_2').
 \end{aligned}
\]

\paragraph{First extraction.}
The tuple $T_0$ is a function of $\mathcal C$.  Conditional on $T_0$, the
tuple $(A,A')$ remains independent of $\mathcal C$.  Since $S_1$ is
a uniform seed independent of $A$, the strong-extractor guarantee gives
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:first-uniform}
 \Delta((R_1,T_0),(U_r,T_0))\le\epsilon.
\end{equation}
Indeed, conditional on $\mathcal C$, the law of $R_{1,A}$ depends only on
$S_1$; retaining all of $\mathcal C$ does not increase its average
error.  Adding the fixed value $R_{1,B}$ preserves this error.

For each fixed $T_0$, the tuple $(R_1,R_1')$ is a function of $(A,A')$ plus
known shifts.  Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:markov-before-scb}
 (R_1,R_1')\quad\hbox{and}\quad(Y,Y')
 \quad\hbox{are independent conditional on }T_0.
\end{equation}
Moreover, conditioning on $T_0$ decreases the average conditional min-entropy of
$Y$ by at most $2e+2r$ bits, so
\[
 \widetilde{H}_\infty(Y\mid T_0)\ge d-2e-2r\ge r+q.
\]
Thus $H_\infty(Y\mid T_0=u)\ge r$ for all values $u$ except a set of
total probability at most $\epsilon$.

\paragraph{The standard correlation breaker.}
For a value $u$ of $T_0$, let
$\delta_u=\Delta((R_1\mid T_0=u),U_r)$.  In the conditional law, replace the
marginal of $R_1$ by uniform while keeping the conditional law of $R_1'$ given
$R_1$; choose arbitrary conditional laws at values outside the original
support.  This changes the joint seed tuple by distance $\delta_u$ and, by
Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:markov-before-scb}, preserves its independence of $(Y,Y')$.
For values $u$ with $H_\infty(Y\mid T_0=u)\ge r$,
Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:standard} applies.  Returning to the original seed law costs at
most $2\delta_u$, once for the actual distribution and once for its ideal
distribution.  Average Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:first-uniform} and charge at most
$\epsilon$ for the remaining values of $u$.  We obtain
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:second-seed}
 \Delta((S_2,S_2',T_1),(U_t,S_2',T_1))\le4\epsilon.
\end{equation}

Fixing $(R_1,R_1')$ after $T_0$ imposes conditions only on $(A,A')$.
Thus $(A,A')$ and $\mathcal C$ are still independent conditional on $T_1$.  With $T_1$ fixed, the tuple $(S_2,S_2')$ is a function of
$\mathcal C$.  It follows in particular that
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:exact-markov}
 (A,A')\quad\hbox{and}\quad\mathcal C
 \quad\hbox{are independent conditional on }T_2.
\end{equation}
All these independence statements hold exactly in the original distribution;
the preceding replacements were used only to bound statistical distance.

\paragraph{Second extraction.}
The tuple $(R_1,R_1')$ has length $2r$, and $T_0$ is independent of
$(A,A')$. Conditioning on these variables therefore gives
\[
 \widetilde{H}_\infty(A\mid T_1)\ge K-2r.
\]
Apply the independence-merging argument of \Cref{pre:merge} to
$(A,A')$ and $(S_2,S_2')$ conditional on $T_1$.  For completeness, its
specialization here is as follows.  Replace the conditional marginal of
$S_2$ given $(S_2',T_1)$ by uniform, retaining the law of $(S_2',T_1)$ and
the independent conditional law of $(A,A')$.  Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:second-seed}
bounds the distance of the complete input laws by $4\epsilon$.  In this
auxiliary law $S_2$ is independent of
$(A,A',S_2',T_1)$. Conditioning further on $S_2'$ does not decrease the
average conditional min-entropy of $A$ given $T_1$, because of conditional
independence. Conditioning on the $w$-bit string
$R_{2,A}'=L_2(A',S_2')$ decreases it by at most $w$ bits.
Therefore
\[
 \widetilde{H}_\infty(A\mid T_1,S_2',R_{2,A}')\ge K-2r-w\ge k_2+q.
\]
The strong-extractor guarantee for $L_2$, averaged over this conditioning,
has error at most $2\epsilon$.  Returning to the original law costs at
most twice $4\epsilon$.  In the original distribution we thus have
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:reservoir-output}
 \Delta((R_{2,A},R_{2,A}',T_2),(U_w,R_{2,A}',T_2))\le10\epsilon.
\end{equation}
This is the single-tampering counterpart of Eqn.~(9)
in~\cite[Section~6]{CL22}, with a conservative error bound.

\paragraph{Including $(B,B',Y,Y')$ in the conditioning tuple.}
Conditional on $T_2$, both $R_{2,A}$ and $R_{2,A}'$ are functions of
$(A,A')$.  The exact independence in~Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:exact-markov}
therefore permits adjoining all of $\mathcal C$ to
Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:reservoir-output} with no additional error.  Take
\[
 \mathcal T=(T_2,\mathcal C,R_{2,A}').
\]
The shift $R_{2,B}$ and the second output
$R_2'=R_{2,A}'+R_{2,B}'$ are determined by $\mathcal T$.  Adding the known
shift $R_{2,B}$ to $R_{2,A}$ proves
Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:retained}, since $C_{\rm cb}=20$.  Equivalently, the
tuple can include $R_2'$ instead of $R_{2,A}'$, since $\mathcal C$ and
$S_2'$ determine $R_{2,B}'$.

\paragraph{A seed with bounded deficiency.}
The entropy deficiency of a $d$-bit seed $Y$ is $d-H_\infty(Y)$;
the hypothesis in the lemma bounds this quantity by $\lambda$.
For a general seed distribution, define an auxiliary distribution by making $Y$
uniform, keeping the conditional law of $(B,B',Y')$ given $Y$, and drawing
$(A,A')$ independently with its original law. Extend the conditional law
of $(B,B',Y')$ arbitrarily at unsupported values of $Y$. The original law
has density
\[
 2^d\mathbf{Pr}[Y=y]\le2^\lambda
\]
relative to this auxiliary distribution. Since $Y$ is included in $\mathcal T$,
the two distributions have identical conditional distributions of $R_2$ on
every value of $\mathcal T$ in the original support. The average conditional
distance from uniform in the original distribution is at most $2^\lambda$
times that in the auxiliary distribution. Applying the
uniform-seed conclusion in the auxiliary distribution proves the claimed
bound for a seed of min-entropy at least $d-\lambda$.
The auxiliary distribution need not be affine.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cb:affine-fibers}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{cb:retained}, assume in addition that
$(A,A',B,B',Y,Y')$ is jointly affine and
$H_\infty(Y)\ge d-\lambda$ for some $\lambda\ge0$. Then every nonempty
fiber obtained by fixing the tuple $\mathcal T$ from its proof is affine, and
$W=\mathsf{ACB}(X,Y,\alpha)$ is affine on it. The total probability of fibers on which $W$ is
not exactly uniform on $\{0,1\}^w$ is at most
\begin{equation}\label{cb:eq:bad-fibers}
 2C_{\rm cb}2^\lambda\epsilon.
\end{equation}
On every other fiber, $\mathsf{ACB}(X',Y',\alpha')$ is fixed and $W$ is an exactly
uniform affine $w$-bit variable.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Use the tuple with the second output $R_2'$ in place of
$R_{2,A}'$.  First fix the affine variables $B,B',Y,Y'$.  This fixes
$S_1,S_1',R_{1,B},R_{1,B}'$. With the two first seeds fixed, both
extractor outputs $R_1,R_1'$ are affine in the underlying uniform parameter.  Once their
values have also been fixed, the possibly nonlinear computations defining
$S_2,S_2'$ are determined and impose no further constraints.  Fixing
$R_2'=L_2(X',S_2')$ is one final system of affine constraints.  This proves
that each nonempty fiber of $\mathcal T$ is affine; the output
$L_2(X,S_2)$ is affine there as well.  Its conditional law is uniform on
an affine subspace of $\{0,1\}^w$.  If that subspace is proper, its distance
from $U_w$ is at least $1/2$.  The average conditional distance is bounded
by \Cref{cb:retained}, so the total probability of fibers on which the
image is a proper affine subspace is at most twice that bound.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{cb:two-transcripts}
The tuple $\mathcal T$ includes all of $\mathcal C$. It can be long and
depend on the affine-source decomposition. Fixing $\mathcal T$ gives the
affine partition on which $\mathsf{ACB}(X,Y,\alpha)$ is exactly uniform, apart
from the exceptional fibers in \Cref{cb:affine-fibers}.

To fix the outputs of the other iterations in \Cref{merge:general}, we
use fewer variables. For fixed $y,\alpha$, first fix the $r$ bits of
$R_1$. These are linear functions of the input because $S_1$ is fixed.
The value of $S_2$ is then determined, so the $w$ bits of the final output
are also linear functions of the input and can be fixed next. Thus at
most $r+w$ bits need to be fixed, and each linear function is determined
by $y,\alpha$ and the values fixed previously. This procedure does not
use the decomposition $(X,X')=(A,A')+(B,B')$. The tuple $\mathcal T$
and this sequence of fixings serve different purposes in the proof.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{branch:advice}
There is an absolute constant $c_0>0$ with the following property. For every
integer $p\ge1$ satisfying $p+\log n\le c_0n$, there is an explicit function
\[
 \mathsf{Adv}:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^{r_0}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^a
\]
with seed and advice lengths $r_0,a=O(p+\log n)$ such that the following
holds. Let $(Q,Q',Z,Z')$ be jointly affine, with
$Q,Q'\in\mathsf{F}_2^n$, $Z,Z'\in\{0,1\}^{r_0}$, $Z=U_{r_0}$, and
$Q\ne Q'$ at every point of the joint support. Then
\begin{equation}\label{branch:advice-error}
 \mathbf{Pr}[\mathsf{Adv}(Q,Z)=\mathsf{Adv}(Q',Z')]\le2^{-p}.
\end{equation}
For an affine input tuple $(Q,Z)$, we can fix the advice by first fixing
$Z$ and then fixing linear functions of $Q$, with at most $a$ bits fixed
in total. The two advice strings can therefore be fixed jointly with at
most $2a$ bits fixed. The same function may be applied to longer rows by
ignoring the suffix after position $r_0$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Put $q_0=p+\lceil\log n\rceil+4$ and $e=2^{-q_0}$. Let
\[
 L_0:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^{d_0}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{q_0}
\]
be a strong linear seeded extractor with error $e$, entropy threshold
$k_0=O(q_0)$, and seed length $d_0=O(q_0+\log n)$, using
\Cref{pre:linear}. Take $z=z_1\circ z_2$, where $|z_2|=d_0$ and
$|z_1|=C_0q_0$, and set $r_0=C_0q_0+d_0$. The absolute integer $C_0$ is large enough that
$|z_1|\ge2k_0$ and a rate-$1/2$ affine extractor $E_0$ on $|z_1|$ bits,
supplied by \Cref{pre:affine-ext}, has error at most $e$ and enough
output for the sampler below. These requirements are compatible because
the rate-$1/2$ extractor has linear output and exponentially small error.

Let $\mathsf{Enc}$ be a binary linear encoding of constant relative distance.
The sampler $\mathsf{Samp}$ uses $O(q_0+\log n)$ uniform seed bits to sample
$O(q_0)$ codeword positions. For every fixed codeword of constant relative
weight, it misses the support with probability at most $e$. Define
\begin{equation}\label{branch:advice-formula}
 \mathsf{Adv}(x,z)=z_1\circ z_2\circ
   \mathsf{Enc}(x)|_{\mathsf{Samp}(E_0(z_1))}\circ L_0(x,z_2).
\end{equation}
Here the restriction of $\mathsf{Enc}(x)$ lists its bits at the sampled
positions, and $a$ is the total length of the concatenation.
All lengths are $O(p+\log n)$. Choosing $c_0$ small enough ensures the
feasibility of $L_0$ on $n$ bits.

Write $\Delta=Q+Q'$. Joint affineness implies that the conditional entropy
\[
 v=H(\Delta\mid Z_2)
\]
is the dimension of a conditional affine support, and hence is the same
on every nonempty $Z_2$ fiber. The uniformity
of $Z$ makes $Z_1,Z_2$ independent and individually uniform.

If $v\le k_0$, fix $Z_2$ and $\Delta$. On each nonempty fiber, $Z_1$ is
an affine source of entropy at least
\[
 |Z_1|-v\ge |Z_1|/2.
\]
The vector $\Delta$ is nonzero by hypothesis. Thus $\mathsf{Enc}(\Delta)$ is
a fixed codeword of constant relative weight. The extractor followed by
the sampler misses its support with probability at most $2e$ on each
fiber. A collision in~Eqn.~\eqref{branch:advice-formula} implies $Z_1=Z_1'$
and $Z_2=Z_2'$, hence identical sample positions on the two sides. It
therefore implies this miss event, whose unconditional probability is at
most $2e\le2^{-p}$.

If $v>k_0$, the conditional sources $\Delta\mid Z_2=z_2$ have a common
direction of dimension $v$. \Cref{pre:rank} supplies a fixed set of
bad seeds of uniform measure at most $2e$. Outside this set,
$L_0(\Delta,z_2)$ is exactly uniform on $\{0,1\}^{q_0}$, despite the
dependence of the affine offset on $z_2$. Consequently
\[
 \mathbf{Pr}[L_0(\Delta,Z_2)=0]\le2e+2^{-q_0}
   =3e\le2^{-p}.
\]
Advice equality implies equality of $Z_2,Z_2'$ and of the last advice
components, and hence implies this zero event because
$L_0(\cdot,z_2)$ is linear for every fixed seed $z_2$.
This proves~Eqn.~\eqref{branch:advice-error}. In both cases the probability
is bounded before conditioning on equality of the two initial seeds.

To bound the number of bits fixed, first fix $z_1,z_2$ in each call. This
determines the sampler positions and the seed of $L_0$. Every remaining
advice bit is then a linear function of $x$. Fixing these bits fixes the
entire advice, with at most its length in bits fixed. Each resulting
nonempty fiber is affine by \Cref{pre:queries}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{branch:row-growth}
Let $(Q^0,\ldots,Q^{q_*-1},Y_0^0,\ldots,Y_0^{q_*-1})$ be jointly
affine, where each $Q^j$ has length $n$, every row has length $r_*$,
and $Y_0^0=U_{r_*}$.
Suppose
\[
 H(Q^0)\ge2q_*R+C_1(R+p).
\]
Apply the maps $L_1,\ldots,L_J$ in Eqn.~\eqref{branch:grow} to each
input, starting with its given row. There is an affine partition,
obtained by fixing fewer than $2q_*R$ bits, such that outside total
probability $2J2^{-p}$ the final row on $Q^0$ is exactly uniform on
$\{0,1\}^R$ and all final rows are affine on the corresponding part.
The final rows themselves are not fixed in this partition.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Work on a part where the current rows are affine and the row at
index $0$ is uniform. The nonempty fibers obtained by fixing all
current rows have a common direction. Its projection onto $Q^0$
has dimension at least the current entropy of $Q^0$ minus $q_*r$,
where $r$ is the current row length. This direction is independent
of the values being fixed.

For this direction, \Cref{pre:rank} bounds the uniform measure of
seeds for which the next linear extractor does not have full rank
by $2\cdot2^{-p}$. We call quantities computed on the original input
$Q^0$ \emph{honest}, to distinguish them from those on the comparison
inputs. The current honest row is uniform before it is fixed, so the
same bound holds for its marginal seed, even when the other rows are
correlated with it. On every other fiber the next
honest row is uniform, and all next rows are affine because their
seeds are fixed. Iterate this argument. The number of linear constraints imposed is at most
\[
 q_*\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}r_j<2q_*R,
\]
so the entropy hypothesis supplies every extractor threshold.
Average the failure probabilities at each stage and sum them.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{branch:seed-ingredients}
There are absolute constants $\beta>0$ and $A_0\ge1$ with the following
properties. Let $0<\kappa\le1/2$ and $\ell=\Theta(\kappa n)$, in the
parameter ranges considered in \Cref{sec:parameters}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item There are uniformly explicit linear maps
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_b&:\mathsf{F}_2^\ell\longrightarrow\mathsf{F}_2^q &&(b\in[u_0]),\\
 T_a&:\mathsf{F}_2^n\longrightarrow\mathsf{F}_2^q &&(a\in[v_0]),
 \end{aligned}
\]
with $u_0,v_0,n/q\le(2/\kappa)^{A_0}$, such that an affine source of entropy
at least $\kappa\ell/8$ has a $C_b$ image of entropy at least
$(1/2+\beta)q$. An affine source of entropy at least $\kappa n/8$ has a
$T_a$ image with the same guarantee.
\item For every $r\le\beta q/4$, there is a uniformly explicit bilinear
map $\mathsf{IP}_r:\mathsf{F}_2^q\times\mathsf{F}_2^q\to\mathsf{F}_2^r$ such that, for independent
affine sources $U,V$ of entropy at least $(1/2+\beta)q$,
\[
 \Delta((\mathsf{IP}_r(U,V),V),(U_r,V))\le\epsilon_{\rm IP},
\]
where $\epsilon_{\rm IP}\le2^{-c_{\rm IP}q}$ for an absolute
$c_{\rm IP}>0$.
\item An affine somewhere-random source with $T$ rows of length $r$ and
one exactly uniform row, in the range
$r/(2T)^{A_0\log(2T)}\ge(2T)^4$, admits a uniformly explicit extractor
$\mathsf{SRExt}$ with output length at least $r/(2T)^{A_0\log(2T)}$,
error at most $2^{-r/(2T)^{A_0\log(2T)}}$, and coordinate degree at most
$(2T)^{A_0}$, with harmless integer rounding in the output length.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Part (i) uses the linear somewhere condenser of
\cite[Theorem~18]{LZdir}. Its number of rows and reciprocal output length
are polynomial in the reciprocal entropy rate. The two input lengths
can be matched using the additional $O(\log(1/\kappa))$ applications of
$\mathsf{BasicCond}$ in Steps 1--2 of Algorithm 8 there. Pad the local
and global input lengths separately to powers of two, and use the common
condenser entropy rate $\kappa/16$. The longer input requires
$O(\log(1/\kappa))$ additional halving steps. The output family at each
step includes the two coordinate projections, so some row preserves the
good entropy rate. Both bounds remain polynomial in $1/\kappa$.
Part (ii) is the bilinear inner-product extractor of
\cite[Theorem~38]{LZdir}, restricted to the indicated output length.
Part (iii) is the affine somewhere-random extractor of Li~\cite{Li11b},
in the form recorded in \cite[Theorem~39]{LZdir}. The original
construction~\cite[Algorithms 6.3.9--6.3.10 and Theorem 6.3.12]{Li11a}
uses $O(\log T)$ stages of constant-degree operations, giving coordinate
degree $T^{O(1)}$. Its output and error losses are $T^{O(\log T)}$.
The row-length assumption ensures the size requirements at every level.
The exponents are absolute and do not require $T$ to be constant.
Increasing $A_0$ covers all three parts and their uniform implementations.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{branch:interface}
There is an absolute constant $C_*\ge1$ for which the following holds
for \Cref{alg:branch}, with $s\ge u\ge\max\{\lceil\log n\rceil+2,(2T)^4\}$.
Assume $\epsilon_{\rm IP}\le2^{-8s}$,
$2\ell\le\kappa n/8$, and
\begin{equation}\label{branch:budget}
 2\ell+2A_{s,u}+C_*(s+\log n)\le\kappa n/4.
\end{equation}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every fixed initial seed $h$, we can fix $G(x,h)$ by successively
fixing at most $L\le C_*(s+\log n)$ affine functions of $x$. Each function
is determined by $h$ and the values fixed previously. If $Px$ is fixed,
we can fix $W(x)$ in the same way with at most $A_{s,u}+L$ bits fixed.
\item Let $(Q,Q')$ be jointly affine, with $Q\ne Q'$ at every point of
the joint support. Suppose
\begin{equation}\label{branch:entropy}
 \begin{aligned}
 H(PQ)&\ge\kappa\ell/8,\\
 H(Q)&\ge\kappa n/3.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Its joint support has a partition into affine subspaces such that, except
on subspaces of total probability at most
\begin{equation}\label{branch:exceptional}
 \epsilon_{s,u}\le2\epsilon_{\rm IP}
 +(2\lceil\log n\rceil+3)2^{-8u}+2\cdot2^{-4s}\le2^{-u},
\end{equation}
$W(Q)$ is an exactly uniform affine $s$-bit variable and $W(Q')$ is
fixed on each subspace.
\end{enumerate}
The conclusion also holds after interchanging $Q$ and $Q'$ in both the
entropy assumptions and the conclusion. The same
constant $C_*$ bounds the initial-seed length by $C_*(u+\log n)$
and all additional entropy requirements by $C_*(s+\log n)$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Increase $C_*$ to dominate every length and entropy requirement below.
Eqn.~\eqref{branch:budget} then ensures $4s+\log n\le c_0n$.
Every fixing is made separately on each nonempty fiber; exceptional
probabilities are averaged over the preceding fixings.

\paragraph{Fixing the output for a fixed initial seed.}
First fix the intermediate rows in $\mathsf{Grow}(x,h)$ in order,
using fewer than $3R$ linear bits, then fix the advice as in
\Cref{branch:advice}. This determines the correlation-breaker seed and
advice. In Eqn.~\eqref{cb:eq:construction}, fix $R_1$, which determines
$S_2$, and then fix $L_2(x,S_2)$. At each step, the seed has already been
fixed, so these are affine functions of $x$. The number of bits fixed is
$O(s+\log n)$. If $Px$ is fixed but the initial seed is not, first fix
the $A_{s,u}$ linear entries of $\mathsf{SR}(x)$. These determine $\mathsf{H}(x)$.

\paragraph{A uniform row after fixing the two blocks.}
Put $J=(PQ,PQ')$. An affine decomposition gives
\[
 (Q,Q')=A(J)+(B,B'),
\]
where $A_Q(j)$ is the $Q$-coordinate of $A(j)$, and $(B,B')$ is uniform
on the kernel direction and independent of $J$. In particular,
$H(B)\ge H(Q)-2\ell\ge\kappa n/8$.
Choose a full-input condenser row $T_a(B)$ of entropy at least
$(1/2+\beta)q$, and a local row $V=C_b(PQ)$ with the same guarantee.
They are independent. The strong guarantee of $\mathsf{IP}_{r_{\rm SR}}$
bounds its average conditional distance from uniform by
$\epsilon_{\rm IP}$. For fixed $V$, the output is a linear image of an
affine source; unless its rank is full, its distance from uniform is at
least $1/2$. Bad values of $V$ therefore have probability at most
$2\epsilon_{\rm IP}$.

On the fiber obtained by fixing $J=j$, the selected row of $\mathsf{SR}(Q)$ is
\[
 \mathsf{IP}_{r_{\rm SR}}(T_a(B),V(j))+
 \mathsf{IP}_{r_{\rm SR}}(T_a(A_Q(j)),V(j)).
\]
The second term is fixed. Thus this row is exactly uniform outside
fibers of $J$ of total probability at most $2\epsilon_{\rm IP}$.
This bound uses the marginal law of $V$ and requires no residual entropy
in $PQ$ after $PQ'$ is fixed.

\paragraph{Fixing the seed matrices and growing the row.}
For every nonexceptional fixing of the block pair $J$, both seed
matrices are affine and $\mathsf{SR}(Q)$ has a uniform row. Hence
$\mathsf{H}(Q)$ is $2^{-8u}$-close to uniform. The fibers obtained by
fixing both complete matrices have a common direction, whose
projection onto $Q$ has dimension at least
$H(Q)-2\ell-2A_{s,u}$.
For this direction, the bad-seed set for $L_0$ has uniform measure
at most $2\cdot2^{-8u}$. Its definition is independent of the matrix
values. The marginal near-uniformity of the initial seed therefore
bounds the mass of bad matrix fibers by
\begin{equation}\label{branch:outer-bad}
 3\cdot2^{-8u}.
\end{equation}

Fix the two matrices. On every other fiber, the first row pair is
affine and its honest row is exactly uniform. Apply
\Cref{branch:row-growth} with $q_*=2$. It fixes fewer than $4R$
additional bits and fails with probability at most
$2\lceil\log n\rceil2^{-8u}$. For sufficiently large $C_*$, Eqn.~\eqref{branch:budget} leaves enough
entropy after these fixings to apply each extractor.
On each surviving part the final tuple $(Q,Q',Z,Z')$ is jointly
affine and $Z=U_R$. In particular, this exact uniformity is obtained
before fixing the advice.

\paragraph{Advice and the correlation breaker.}
Apply \Cref{branch:advice} and fix both advice strings by successively
fixing at most $2a$ affine functions. Discard the individual fibers on which they coincide,
with total conditional probability at most $2^{-4s}$. On each remaining fiber the
advice strings are fixed and distinct, while
$Y=\operatorname{prefix}_{d_C}Z$ has entropy at least $d_C-2a$.
Apply \Cref{pre:reservoir} with the jointly affine final rows $(Z,Z')$.
Writing the current source as
$(Q,Q')=(A_0,A_0')+(B_0,B_0')$, the pair $(A_0,A_0')$ is independent of
$(B_0,B_0',Y,Y')$, with
\begin{equation}\label{branch:reservoir-entropy}
 H(A_0)\ge H(Q)-2\ell-2A_{s,u}-4R-2a-2R\ge K_C.
\end{equation}
The last inequality follows from Eqn.~\eqref{branch:budget} and the
choice of $C_*$. \Cref{cb:affine-fibers}, with seed deficiency at most
$2a$, supplies the required finer affine partition except on a set of conditional probability at most
$2C_{\rm cb}2^{2a-q_C}\le2^{-4s}$.
Averaging over fibers and adding the exceptional probability from fixing
the block pair, the bound in Eqn.~\eqref{branch:outer-bad}, the failure probabilities
from growing the row, and the
last two exceptional probabilities proves Eqn.~\eqref{branch:exceptional}. Interchanging $Q$ and $Q'$
throughout the argument gives the conclusion with $W(Q')$ uniform and
$W(Q)$ fixed, under the entropy assumptions on $Q'$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{amp:robust}
For every nonzero $a\in\mathsf{F}_2^m$ and every polynomial
$P:\mathsf{F}_2^s\to\mathsf{F}_2$ of degree at most $D$,
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{W\sim U_s}(-1)^{a\cdot\Phi(W)+P(W)}\right|
 \le2^{-\zeta_Ds}.
\]
The statement allows $D$ to grow with $s$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let $I$ be the support of $aM$. Fix the coordinates outside its
majority blocks, including the unused coordinates. The remaining
coordinates are uniform, and the restriction of $P$ still has degree
at most $D$. By~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{CHLLTV26}, its correlation with
 the $\mathsf{XOR}$ of these $|I|$ majorities is at most
\[
 (2D/\sqrt c)^{|I|}\le2^{-|I|}.
\]
Average over the fixed coordinates and use
$|I|\ge\delta_0\lfloor s/c\rfloor\ge\delta_0s/(2c)$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{merge:general}
Fix $0<\kappa\le1/2$ and positive integers $n,B,\ell$ with $B\ell\le n$.
Partition the first $B\ell$ coordinates of an $n$-bit string into
$B$ consecutive blocks of length $\ell$.  Suppose
\begin{equation}\label{merge:rounding}
 \begin{aligned}
 B&\ge64/\kappa,\\
 2(n-B\ell)&\le\kappa n/4.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For each $i\in[B]$, let
$\mathsf{H}_i:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{d_i}$ be an initial-seed function from Eqn.~\eqref{branch:seed-function}, with
algebraic degree at most $D$ and seed-matrix length $A_i$.  Let $G_i$ be the map evaluated in iteration $i$
as in \Cref{branch:interface}, with output length $s_i$ and exceptional
probability at most $\varepsilon_i$. For every fixed initial seed, its output
is determined by successively fixing at most $L_i$ affine functions as above.
Let $C_*$ be
an absolute constant that bounds all parameters of an iteration as in that
proposition. The selected source must have entropy at least $\kappa n/3$, and its
$i$th block must have entropy at least $\kappa\ell/8$. Assume the
bilinear and somewhere-random primitive parameters are feasible at every
scale, as in \Cref{branch:interface}, and
\begin{equation}\label{merge:budgets}
 \begin{aligned}
 2\sum_{i=1}^B (A_i+L_i)&\le\frac{\kappa\ell}{16},\\
 \max_i\bigl(2\ell+2A_i+C_*(s_i+\log n)\bigr)&\le\frac{\kappa n}{4}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Set $c=16\lceil D\rceil^2+1$, assume $s_i\ge2c$ for all $i$,
and choose a positive integer $m$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{merge:code-budget}
 m\le R_0\min_i\lfloor s_i/c\rfloor.
\end{equation}
For each iteration let $\Phi_i:\mathsf{F}_2^{s_i}\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be the amplifier
in~Eqn.~\eqref{amp:definition}.  Define
\begin{equation}\label{merge:formula}
 \mathsf{anmExt}(x)=\bigoplus_{i=1}^B
    \Phi_i\bigl(G_i(x,\mathsf{H}_i(x))\bigr).
\end{equation}
Write $Q_i=2\sum_{j>i}d_j$ for the total length of the later initial
seeds on the two inputs, and set
\begin{equation}\label{merge:beta}
 \beta=\max_{i\in[B]}2^{Q_i}
       \bigl(\varepsilon_i+2^{-\zeta_Ds_i}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Then $\mathsf{anmExt}$ is an ordinary affine extractor for entropy $\kappa n$
with error at most $\tfrac12\sqrt{2^m-1}\,\beta$.  Moreover, for every
affine source $X$ with $H(X)\ge2\kappa n$ and every affine map $T$ having
no fixed point in the support of $X$,
\begin{equation}\label{merge:nm-error}
 \Delta\bigl((\mathsf{anmExt}(X),\mathsf{anmExt}(TX)),
          (U_m,\mathsf{anmExt}(TX))\bigr)
 \le2^{m-1}\beta.
\end{equation}
The ideal uniform variable is independent of the second coordinate.
If the initial-seed functions and maps $G_i$ are uniformly computable in
polynomial time with these parameters, so is $\mathsf{anmExt}$.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{merge:good-block}
Under the assumptions of \Cref{merge:general}, let $(X,X')$ be jointly
affine, supported on distinct pairs, with
\begin{equation}\label{merge:pair-entropies}
 H(X),H(X')\ge\kappa n.
\end{equation}
There are $g\in[B]$ and $\sigma\in\{0,1\}$ such that, after fixing any
joint prefix $(X_{<g},X'_{<g})$ and then successively fixing any sequence of
at most $2\sum_i(A_i+L_i)$ affine functions, each chosen according to the
previously fixed values, the conditional sources $Z^0,Z^1$ on every
nonempty part satisfy
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H(Z_g^\sigma)&\ge3\kappa\ell/16,\\
 H(Z^\sigma)&\ge\kappa n/3.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The choices of $g,\sigma$
depend only on the original conditional ranks.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Neither projection is required to determine the other. For $i\in[B]$
let
\[
 h_i=H(X_i,X_i'\mid X_{<i},X_{<i}').
\]
Here $X_{<i}=(X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1})$, and similarly for $X'_{<i}$.
Since the pair is jointly affine, these conditional entropies are the same
on every nonempty fiber of the conditioning variables.  The omitted coordinates have total length
$2(n-B\ell)$ in the pair.  Hence
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^Bh_i
 \ge H(X,X')-2(n-B\ell)
 \ge3\kappa n/4
 >\kappa B\ell/2.
\]
Let $g$ be the first index with $h_g\ge\kappa\ell/2$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{merge:prefix-rank}
 H(X_{<g},X_{<g}')=\sum_{i<g}h_i<\kappa n/2.
\end{equation}
Fix a value $v$ in the support of $(X_{<g},X'_{<g})$. Each of the two
sources still has entropy at least $\kappa n/2$.  At least one of the two conditional
block entropies at index $g$ is at least $\kappa\ell/4$, since their
sum is at least $h_g$.  Call that side $\sigma\in\{0,1\}$, with $0$
denoting $X$ and $1$ denoting $X'$.  The choice of $g$ and $\sigma$
can be made from the original conditional ranks, independently of $v$.

Successively fixing at most $2\sum_i(A_i+L_i)$ further affine functions
preserves the affine structure on every nonempty cell. On each cell the
selected block and whole input, denoted by $Z_g^\sigma$ and $Z^\sigma$, satisfy
\begin{align}\label{merge:leaf-ranks}
 H(Z_g^\sigma)&\ge\kappa\ell/4-\kappa\ell/16
                =3\kappa\ell/16,\notag\\
 H(Z^\sigma)&\ge\kappa n/2-\kappa\ell/16
                \ge\kappa n/3.
\end{align}
These inequalities hold in the conditional distribution at each
nonempty cell. In particular, the selected block has the entropy required
by its local condenser. Since $B\ge64/\kappa$ and $B\ell\le n$,
$2\ell\le\kappa n/32$. The second inequality in Eqn.~\eqref{merge:budgets}
supplies the remaining entropy budget. Thus \Cref{branch:interface}
applies on every such cell.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{merge:mixed-correlations}
Under the assumptions of \Cref{merge:general}, every jointly affine
pair $(X,X')$ supported on distinct points and satisfying
Eqn.~\eqref{merge:pair-entropies} obeys
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{a_0\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(X)+a_1\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(X')}\right|\le\beta
 \qquad(a_0,a_1\in\mathsf{F}_2^m\setminus\{0\}).
\]
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Choose $g,\sigma$ by \Cref{merge:good-block}. Fix character indices $a_0,a_1\in\mathsf{F}_2^m\setminus\{0\}$ and a prefix value
$v$ as above.  We bound the corresponding Fourier coefficient.  Write $Z^0=X$, $Z^1=X'$, and
let $\mathcal H_{>g}(Z^0,Z^1)\in\mathsf{F}_2^{Q_g}$ concatenate the two
initial seeds at every index greater than $g$. For a possible value
$h\in\mathsf{F}_2^{Q_g}$, write $h_j^\tau\in\mathsf{F}_2^{d_j}$ for the component
corresponding to iteration $j$ on side $\tau\in\{0,1\}$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{merge:forced}
 F_h^\tau(z)=
  \bigoplus_{j\le g}\Phi_j(G_j(z,\mathsf{H}_j(z)))
  \;\oplus\!\bigoplus_{j>g}\Phi_j(G_j(z,h_j^\tau)),
 \qquad \tau\in\{0,1\},
\end{equation}
Thus $F_h^\tau$ uses the prescribed seeds $h_j^\tau$ in iterations
$j>g$ and the actual seeds in iterations $j\le g$. On the event
$\mathcal H_{>g}=h$, it agrees with $\mathsf{anmExt}$.  Therefore
\begin{align}\label{merge:decompose}
 &\mathbf{E}\bigl[(-1)^{a_0\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(Z^0)+a_1\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(Z^1)}
            \mid v\bigr]\notag\\
 &\quad=\sum_{h\in\mathsf{F}_2^{Q_g}}
   \mathbf{E}\bigl[\mathbf1[\mathcal H_{>g}=h]
       (-1)^{a_0\cdot F_h^0(Z^0)+a_1\cdot F_h^1(Z^1)}\mid v\bigr].
\end{align}
The expectation in each summand is conditioned only on $v$; the
possibly nonlinear event $\mathcal H_{>g}=h$ remains inside the expectation.

Fix $h$. For $j<g$, both local blocks are determined by $v$.
Fix their two seed matrices, whose $2A_j$ coordinates are affine after
the local blocks have been fixed. Then determine their outputs by
successively fixing at most $2L_j$ further affine functions. For $j>g$,
use the prescribed seeds in $h$ and determine the two outputs by fixing
at most $2L_j$ affine functions in the same way. This gives an affine
partition $\mathcal L_{v,h}$. Define its weights by
\[
 p_L=\mathbf{Pr}[(Z^0,Z^1)\in L\mid v].
\]
They satisfy $\sum_{L\in\mathcal L_{v,h}}p_L=1$.
The number of bits fixed is at most
$2\sum_{j<g}(A_j+L_j)+2\sum_{j>g}L_j\le2\sum_{j\ne g}(A_j+L_j)$. On each cell $L$,
all outputs in~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:forced}, except the two outputs
at index $g$, are fixed.

By~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:leaf-ranks} and \Cref{branch:interface}, each
cell $L$ admits a further partition into affine subspaces. Call a subcell
exceptional if it fails the conclusion of that proposition; the total
conditional probability of these subcells is at most $\varepsilon_g$.
On every other subcell $C$, the map $W_g(Z^\sigma)$ is affine and uniform
on $\mathsf{F}_2^{s_g}$, while $W_g(Z^{1-\sigma})$ is constant.

Fix a nonexceptional subcell $C=z_C+V_C$. Let $K\subseteq V_C$ be the
kernel of the linear part of the selected output map, and choose a
complement $J$ so that $V_C=K\oplus J$. A uniform point of $C$ has the
unique representation $z_C+k+j$, where $k\in K$ and $j\in J$ are
independent and uniform. Refine $C$ by fixing $k$.  The variable
$W=W_g(Z^\sigma)$ remains uniform on $\mathsf{F}_2^{s_g}$, and the entire
pair $(Z^0,Z^1)$ is now an affine function of $W$.  Consequently every coordinate of $\mathcal H_{>g}$ is a polynomial
of degree at most $D$ in $W$: it is a coordinate of some $\mathsf{H}_j$
composed with an affine function of $W$.

On this refined cell the phase in~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:decompose} has the form
\[
 (-1)^{b_C+a_\sigma\cdot\Phi_g(W)},
\]
where $b_C\in\mathsf{F}_2$ is fixed.  Expand the remaining consistency
indicator as
\begin{equation}\label{merge:indicator}
 \mathbf1[\mathcal H_{>g}(W)=h]
 =2^{-Q_g}\sum_{\lambda\in\mathsf{F}_2^{Q_g}}
       (-1)^{\lambda\cdot(\mathcal H_{>g}(W)+h)}.
\end{equation}
The exponent of each phase on the right is a polynomial of degree at most $D$.
Since $a_\sigma\ne0$, \Cref{amp:robust} and the fact that the
absolute coefficients in~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:indicator} sum to one imply
\begin{equation}\label{merge:good-cell}
 \left|\mathbf{E}\left[
  \mathbf1[\mathcal H_{>g}=h]
  (-1)^{b_C+a_\sigma\cdot\Phi_g(W)}\right]\right|
 \le2^{-\zeta_Ds_g}.
\end{equation}

We now average over the partitions, still without conditioning on
$\mathcal H_{>g}=h$. Let $q_{C\mid L}$ be the conditional probability
of subcell $C$ within cell $L$. The absolute contribution of exceptional
subcells is at most
\[
 \sum_Lp_L\sum_{C\text{ exceptional}}q_{C\mid L}
 \le\varepsilon_g.
\]
For the other subcells, averaging~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:good-cell} first over the
fixings of $k$, then over subcells $C$ and cells $L$, contributes at most
$2^{-\zeta_Ds_g}$.  Thus each summand of~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:decompose} has absolute value at
most
$\varepsilon_g+2^{-\zeta_Ds_g}$.  Summing over the $2^{Q_g}$ guesses
and averaging over $v$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{merge:mixed-bias}
 \left|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{a_0\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(X)+a_1\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(X')}\right|
 \le2^{Q_g}(\varepsilon_g+2^{-\zeta_Ds_g})\le\beta.
\end{equation}
The cell probabilities sum to one, so the number of cells causes
no additional loss. The factor $2^{Q_g}$ comes from summing over the
possible initial seeds of the later iterations.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The argument just given requires only that the character on the
selected side be nonzero.  To prove the ordinary affine extractor guarantee, take an
affine source $X$ with $H(X)\ge\kappa n$, choose any nonzero fixed
$u\in\mathsf{F}_2^n$, and consider the artificial pair $(X,X+u)$.  It has no
diagonal points, and its conditional joint block ranks equal the
conditional block ranks of $X$. In particular, the $X$ side may
always be selected at the first good block.  Apply the same proof with
characters $(a,0)$ for $a\ne0$.  This gives
\begin{equation}\label{merge:ordinary-bias}
 |\mathbf{E}(-1)^{a\cdot\mathsf{anmExt}(X)}|\le\beta.
\end{equation}
Parseval's identity and Cauchy--Schwarz give statistical error at most
$\tfrac12\sqrt{2^m-1}\,\beta$.

Now let $H(X)\ge2\kappa n$ and let $T$ be an affine map with no fixed
point on the support of $X$.  If $H(TX)\ge\kappa n$, the pair
$(X,TX)$ satisfies~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:pair-entropies}.  Eqn.~\eqref{merge:mixed-bias} treats characters with both coordinates
nonzero, while~Eqn.~\eqref{merge:ordinary-bias} treats characters $(a,0)$
with $a\ne0$.  In the difference of the two distributions in
Eqn.~\eqref{merge:nm-error}, every Fourier coefficient with first
character zero vanishes.  Each of the remaining
$(2^m-1)2^m$ character expectations has absolute value at most
$\beta$.  Hence
\[
 \Delta\bigl((\mathsf{anmExt}(X),\mathsf{anmExt}(TX)),(U_m,\mathsf{anmExt}(TX))\bigr)
 \le\tfrac12\sqrt{(2^m-1)2^m}\,\beta
 \le2^{m-1}\beta.
\]

If $H(TX)<\kappa n$, fix the complete affine variable $TX$.  Every
nonempty fiber is an affine source, with
\[
 H(X\mid TX)=H(X)-H(TX)\ge\kappa n.
\]
The ordinary affine-extractor guarantee applies on each fiber, while
$\mathsf{anmExt}(TX)$
is fixed.  Averaging the resulting bounds proves
Eqn.~\eqref{merge:nm-error} also in this case.  This proves both statistical guarantees in \Cref{merge:general}.

To evaluate the construction, we compute the $B$ outputs,
apply their amplifiers, and take the $\mathsf{XOR}$. Selecting $g$, prescribing the
later seeds, and partitioning the source are operations used only in the
analysis. Thus the construction is explicit whenever its components are
explicit, as claimed.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{merge:decay}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{merge:general}, choose positive numbers
$u_i\le\zeta_Ds_i$ and let $u_{\min}=\min_i u_i$. Assume
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \varepsilon_i&\le2^{-u_i},\\
 2\sum_{j>i}d_j&\le u_i/4\quad(i\in[B]),
 \end{aligned}
\]
and choose the output length so that $m\le u_{\min}/8$.
Then the non-malleability error is at most $2^{-5u_{\min}/8}$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
The two terms in Eqn.~\eqref{merge:beta} give
$\beta\le2\max_i2^{-3u_i/4}=2^{1-3u_{\min}/4}$.
Multiply by $2^{m-1}$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{thm:affine-rate-quantitative}
There is an absolute constant $C$ with the following property.
For $0<\rho\le1$, put $E_\rho=n2^{-C/\rho}$. If
$E_\rho\ge C\log n$, there is a uniformly explicit non-malleable
affine extractor on $n$ bits with entropy threshold
$\lceil\rho n\rceil$, at least $\lfloor E_\rho\rfloor$ output bits,
and error at most $2^{-E_\rho}$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Choose a sufficiently small absolute rational $c_0>0$ and set
\begin{equation}\label{param:linear-head}
 S=\left\lfloor\frac{c_0b\kappa^{A+2}n}{H_\kappa}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
Then $\overline S\le c_0\kappa^{A+2}n/H_\kappa+1$.
The choice of $c_0$ and Eqn.~\eqref{param:queries} give
\begin{equation}\label{param:linear-budgets}
 \begin{aligned}
 2\sum_i(A_i+L_i)&\le\kappa\ell/16,\\
 \max_i r_{{\rm SR},i}&\le\beta q/4,\\
 8\overline S&\le c_{\rm IP}q.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the first right-hand side is $\Theta(\kappa^2n)$,
whereas the corresponding cost is $O(c_0\kappa^{A+2}n)$.
The row bound follows from $q\ge n(\kappa/2)^A$ and
$r_{{\rm SR},i}\le H_\kappa(u_i+\log n)$; the last bound follows
from the same lower bound on $q$. There is constant slack in each
inequality. Also $2\ell\le\kappa n/32$, and all other terms in
Eqn.~\eqref{param:branch-budget} are
$O(H_\kappa\overline S)=O(c_0\kappa^{A+2}n)$.
Thus the entropy constraints in Eqn.~\eqref{param:branch-budget} and
the error bound in Eqn.~\eqref{param:branch-error} hold.

The accumulated losses satisfy
\begin{align}
 \log H_\kappa&=O(\log^2(2/\kappa)),\notag\\
 \log(1/b)&=O(\log(2/\kappa)),\notag\\
 B\log(1/\lambda)&=O(1/\kappa).
 \label{param:geometric-loss}
\end{align}
Thus, for absolute $C_0,C_1$, the unrounded final scale is at least
\begin{equation}\label{param:last-scale}
 \lambda^{B-1}\frac{c_0b\kappa^{A+2}n}{H_\kappa}
 \ge n2^{-C_0/\kappa-C_1\log^2(2/\kappa)}
 \ge n2^{-C_2/\rho}.
\end{equation}
Choose the theorem constant $C>C_2$ sufficiently large.
The hypothesis $E_\rho\ge C\log n$ leaves a factor
$2^{(C-C_2)/\rho}$ between the last expression and $E_\rho$.
It absorbs rounding, the fixed output and error constants, and every
polynomial lower bound in $1/\kappa$, including $(2T)^4$ and $2c$.
In particular, $u_B\ge\max\{\lceil\log n\rceil+2,(2T)^4\}$,
$\nu u_B\ge E_\rho$, and $5u_B/8\ge E_\rho$.
This also justifies the minimum-length assumptions used above.
The rounding condition is checked below. Apply
\Cref{merge:general} and \Cref{merge:decay} and truncate the output if needed.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
For fixed $\rho>0$, \Cref{thm:affine-rate-quantitative} has
$E_\rho=\Omega_\rho(n)$. Its size hypothesis holds for sufficiently
large $n$, giving linear output and exponentially small error.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Fix $0<\eta<1$ and take $\rho=C_\eta/\log n$.
For a sufficiently large constant $C_\eta$, the quantity
$E_\rho$ in \Cref{thm:affine-rate-quantitative} is at least
$n^{1-\eta/2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Its hypotheses
hold, and truncation gives at least $\lfloor n^{1-\eta}\rfloor$
output bits with error at most $2^{-n^{1-\eta}}$.
The extension to every fixed number of tamperings follows from
\Cref{thm:joint-affine-quantitative} below.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{thm:joint-affine-tuple}
For fixed $h\ge1$ and $0<\rho\le1$, there is an explicit family
$F_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^{m_n}$, with $m_n=\Omega_{\rho,h}(n)$, such that
for all sufficiently large $n$ and every jointly affine tuple
$(X^0,\ldots,X^u)$, $u\le h$, with $H_\infty(X^0)\ge\rho n$ and
$\mathbf{Pr}[X^0=X^j]=0$ for every $j>0$,
\[
 (F_n(X^0),F_n(X^1),\ldots,F_n(X^u))
 \approx_{2^{-\Omega_{\rho,h}(n)}}
 (U_{m_n},F_n(X^1),\ldots,F_n(X^u)).
\]
Here $U_{m_n}$ is independent of all the other outputs.
No entropy condition is imposed on $X^1,\ldots,X^u$, and these
random variables may equal one another. The condition
$\mathbf{Pr}[X^0=X^j]=0$ requires only that each $X^j$ differ from $X^0$
on every outcome of their joint distribution; it does not require
disjoint supports or different marginal distributions.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:fixed-multi-affine}
For every fixed $h\ge1$ and fixed positive entropy rate, there is
an explicit $h$-non-malleable affine extractor with linear output length
and exponentially small error. Each tampering is affine and has no
fixed point on the source support. The maps need not be invertible,
and distinct maps may have coincident outputs.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:multi-retained}
Write $X^j=A^j+B^j$ for $0\le j\le H$, and assume that
$\mathcal A=(A^0,\ldots,A^H)$ is independent of
$\mathcal C=(B^0,\ldots,B^H,Y^0,\ldots,Y^H)$.
Suppose $H_\infty(A^0)\ge K$, $Y^0=U_d$, and the fixed advice
satisfies $\alpha^0\ne\alpha^j$ for all $j>0$.
There are choices $K,d=O_h(a+w+q+\log n)$ and a tuple
$\mathcal T$ containing $\mathcal C$ and determining the outputs
at indices $1,\ldots,H$, such that
\[
 \Delta((\mathsf{ACB}_h(X^0,Y^0,\alpha^0),\mathcal T),
                  (U_w,\mathcal T))\le C_h\epsilon.
\]
For $H_\infty(Y^0)\ge d-\lambda$, the bound is
$C_h2^\lambda\epsilon$.
If the full tuple $(A^j,B^j,Y^j)_{j=0}^H$ is jointly affine, every nonempty
set obtained by fixing $\mathcal T$ is affine, and the output
at index $0$ is affine on that set. Except for fixings of total probability at most
$2C_h2^\lambda\epsilon$, this output is exactly uniform after
conditioning on the fixing.
For fixed seed and advice, the output is determined by successively fixing
at most $O_h(a+w+q+\log n)$ affine functions of the input. Each function
depends only on the seed, advice, and previously fixed values, independently
of the source distribution.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
For fixed seeds, linearity decomposes each output of a linear seeded
extractor into two summands. The subscripts $A$ and $B$ denote evaluation
on the corresponding source summands with the seed fixed. For example,
$W_i^j=W_{i,A}^j+W_{i,B}^j$. For the prefix $P_i^j$, these subscripts
denote the corresponding prefixes of $W_{i,A}^j$ and $W_{i,B}^j$;
for $V_i^j$, they denote the evaluations of $L_m$ on the two summands
of $W_{i-1}^j$ with seed $Q_{m,i-1}^j$ fixed.
Let the tuples of variables fixed through round $i$ be
\begin{align*}
 J_0&=(S_1^{[0,H]},R_{1,B}^{[0,H]},R_1^{[0,H]},S_2^{[0,H]}),\\
 J_i&=(J_{i-1},P_{i-1,B}^{[0,H]},P_{i-1}^{[0,H]},
       Q_{m,i-1}^{[0,H]},V_{i,B}^{[0,H]},V_i^{[0,H]},Q_{r,i}^{[0,H]}).
\end{align*}
The superscript $[0,H]$ denotes the tuple of variables at indices
$0,\ldots,H$. For $T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\}$, write
$W_{i,A}^{T}=(W_{i,A}^j)_{j\in T}$, and let $E_i$ denote the error bound
after round $i$. The two induction invariants are
\begin{align}
 (W_{i,A}^0,W_{i,A}^{T},J_i)
   &\approx_{E_i}(U_r,W_{i,A}^{T},J_i)
       &&(|T|\le2^i),\label{eq:multi-uniform-invariant}\\
 \mathcal A&\perp\mathcal C\mid J_i.
       \label{eq:multi-independence-invariant}
\end{align}
The second statement is exact. Each variable fixed at this step is,
conditional on the previously fixed variables, a function of
either $\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal C$.
For each such output, first fix the summand determined by
$\mathcal C$; fixing the output then fixes the summand determined by
$\mathcal A$. This proves Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-independence-invariant}
without assuming independence among $A^0,\ldots,A^H$.

For the first phase put
$T_0=(S_1^{[0,H]},R_{1,B}^{[0,H]})$ and
$T_1=(T_0,R_1^{[0,H]})$. Conditional on $T_0$, the tuple
$R_1^{[0,H]}$ is independent of $\mathcal C$. Apply the strong
single-tampering correlation breaker to the pair with indices
$0,j$, keeping
$R_1^0,R_1^j,T_0$. The remaining $R_1$ outputs may be adjoined:
given the variables already included they are independent of $\mathcal C$,
which determines $S_2^0,S_2^j$ together with those values.
Thus $S_2^0$ is nearly uniform and independent of $(S_2^j,T_1)$.
Conditional on $T_1$, $\mathcal A$ is independent of the entire $S_2$ tuple.
Apply the independence-merging lemma of~\cite[Lemma~3.26]{CL22}, with
index set $\{j\}$ on the seed side and an empty index set on the source
side. Its conclusion includes all seed values and gives
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-uniform-invariant} for $T=\{j\}$. Since $j$ is
arbitrary, this proves the $i=0$ case of the induction.

For a later round split a set of at most $2^i$ indices from
$\{1,\ldots,H\}$ into two sets of size at most $2^{i-1}$. The four extraction steps
transfer uniformity to $Q_{m,i-1}$, combine the guarantees for the two index sets
in $V_i$, and restore the output length through $Q_{r,i},W_i$.
These are the four applications of the same independence-merging
lemma in~\cite[Section~6, Eqns.~(10)--(11)]{CL22};
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-independence-invariant} supplies their exact
conditional independence premise. The variant allowing different,
arbitrarily correlated sources $A^j$ is also stated
in~\cite[Definition~3.4 and Theorem~3.5]{Li23}.
The conservative recurrence
$E_i\le8E_{i-1}+20\epsilon$, with $E_0=O(\epsilon)$,
gives $E_\nu\le C_h\epsilon$.

To check the entropy requirements, the variables in $J_\nu$ contain at most
$(H+1)O(|R_1|+e+\nu(d_x+d_y))$ bits of information about $\mathcal A$.
Choose $K$ larger than this amount plus the extractor thresholds,
$Hr$, and $q$ additional bits of entropy slack. Choose $d$ analogously,
accounting for the bits fixed from $\mathcal C$ before extraction
from $Y^0$ and leaving $q$ bits above the required entropy thresholds.
Since $h$ is fixed, all lengths have the stated order. For each entropy
check on $A^0$ or $Y^0$, let $U$ denote that source and $Z$ the tuple
fixed at that step. The chosen lengths ensure
$\widetilde{H}_\infty(U\mid Z)\ge k_{\rm ext}+q$, where $k_{\rm ext}$ is the
required extractor entropy. By \Cref{pre:entropy},
\[
 \mathbf{Pr}_{z\sim Z}\bigl[H_\infty(U\mid Z=z)<k_{\rm ext}\bigr]
 \le 2^{-q}=\epsilon.
\]
A union bound over the $O_h(1)$ entropy checks bounds the total
probability of exceptional fixings by $O_h(\epsilon)$, which is
absorbed into $C_h\epsilon$.

At the last round take
$\mathcal T=(J_\nu,\mathcal C,W_\nu^1,\ldots,W_\nu^H)$.
By Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-independence-invariant}, adjoining $\mathcal C$
to Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-uniform-invariant} adds no error. The
contributions from $B^0,\ldots,B^H$ are now fixed shifts. This proves the uniform-seed
claim. For a seed with min-entropy at least $d-\lambda$, make $Y^0$
uniform while preserving
the conditional law of the remaining variables in $\mathcal C$ given $Y^0$.
The original law has density at most $2^\lambda$ relative to this
law. Since $Y^0$ is retained, the conditional output distributions
for each value of $\mathcal T$ in the original support agree. Their average distance is
therefore multiplied by at most $2^\lambda$.

For affine inputs, first fix $\mathcal C$. Each subsequent output
of a linear seeded extractor is affine in the underlying source parameter
once its seed is fixed; the nonlinear seed computations are determined
by previously fixed values. Thus each set obtained by fixing $\mathcal T$ is affine,
and the final output at index $0$ is affine on that set. A proper affine image has distance at least $1/2$ from
uniform, proving the exceptional-mass bound. With seed and advice fixed,
successively fix the required linear seeded-extractor outputs in their
order of computation. At each step the seed is already determined, so
each output coordinate is an affine function of the input. Their total
length has the claimed bound. The tuple $\mathcal T$ used in the
conditioning argument contains additional variables; no such length
bound is asserted for $\mathcal T$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:joint-affine-quantitative}
There is an absolute constant $C$ with the following property. Given
$n$, $h\ge1$, and $0<\rho\le1$, put $q_*:=h+1$. Define
\[
 \Psi:=\dfrac{q_*^2}{\rho}\log(2q_*)+
                  \log^2\!\left(\dfrac{2q_*^2}{\rho}\right)
\]
and set $E_*:=n2^{-C\Psi}$.
If $E_*\ge C\log n$, there is a uniformly polynomial-time function
$F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$, with $m\ge\lfloor E_*\rfloor$, such that
for every jointly affine tuple $(X^0,\ldots,X^u)$, $u\le h$, with
$H(X^0)\ge\rho n$ and $\mathbf{Pr}[X^0=X^j]=0$ for $j>0$,
\[
 (F(X^0),F(X^1),\ldots,F(X^u))
 \approx_{2^{-E_*}}(U_m,F(X^1),\ldots,F(X^u)).
\]
The uniform variable is independent of the comparison outputs.
No entropy assumption is imposed on the comparisons, which may
coincide with one another. The running-time exponent is absolute.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
First suppose all inputs differ pairwise at every point. We construct
the function for honest rate $\rho_0$; the theorem will use
$\rho_0=\rho/2$. Set
\begin{itemize}
\item Whole-input working rate: $\kappa:=\rho_0/(4q_*)$.
\item Local working rate: $\theta:=\kappa/q_*$.
\item Block count and length: $B:=\lceil256/\theta\rceil$ and
$\ell:=\lfloor n/B\rfloor$.
\item Reciprocal rate parameter: $\mathcal R:=2/\theta=8q_*^2/\rho_0$.
\end{itemize}
We distinguish the whole-input rate from the local rate: fixing all
$q_*$ local blocks costs $q_*\ell\le\kappa n/256$, although the
local block may have only $\theta\ell/8$ entropy. The seed ingredients
are instantiated at rate $\theta$; after the blocks are fixed, the
whole source still has more than their required $\theta n/8$ entropy.

Consider an output Fourier coefficient whose coefficient at index
$0$ is nonzero. Omit zero-coefficient inputs, and repeatedly fix and
remove a comparison whose current rank is less than $\kappa n$.
These operations fix fewer than $h\kappa n$ bits in total, leaving
more than $3\rho_0n/4$ honest entropy. Every remaining whole input
has rank at least $\kappa n$.

Let $h_i$ be the joint conditional rank of block $i$ given the
preceding joint blocks. The omitted-coordinate loss is at most
$q_*B$. In the parameter range verified below this is at most
$\kappa n/4$, so $\sum_i h_i\ge3\kappa n/4$. This subtraction bounds
the entropy of the local blocks; the omitted coordinates are not fixed.
The first $g$ with $h_g\ge\kappa\ell/2$ has preceding joint rank
less than $\kappa n/2$. After fixing that prefix, all active whole
inputs retain rank at least $\kappa n/2$, and one active local block
has rank at least $\theta\ell/2$.

The nonselected outputs are fixed as in \Cref{merge:mixed-correlations},
using prescribed initial seeds after index $g$. It suffices to ensure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-fixing-budget}
 q_*\sum_i(A_i+L_i)\le\theta\ell/4.
\end{equation}
Then the selected block retains rank at least $\theta\ell/4$ and
its whole input retains rank at least $\kappa n/3$.
The proof for the selected iteration just given applies under
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-branch-budget}
 q_*\ell+q_*A_i+Cq_*^{C_0}(s_i+\log n)\le\kappa n/4.
\end{equation}
This bounds the total entropy lost by fixing the local blocks, matrices,
intermediate rows, and advice, while leaving the entropy required by the correlation
breaker. The available entropy here is measured by the whole-input rate
$\kappa$.

Let $q_{\rm row}$ be the condenser input length. Increase an absolute
integer $A$ and define $\mathcal H=2^{A\lceil\log \mathcal R\rceil^2}$
so that the seed ingredients satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-seed-costs}
 \begin{aligned}
 T,n/q_{\rm row},D&\le \mathcal R^A,\\
 A_i+L_i&\le\mathcal H(s_i+\log n).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Polynomial factors
in $q_*$ are absorbed into $\mathcal H$, since $q_*^2\le \mathcal R$.
Take $D=\lceil \mathcal R^A\rceil$, majority block length $c=16D^2+1$,
and $b=\delta_0/(2c)$. Choose
\begin{itemize}
\item A dyadic ratio $\lambda$ between $1/(C_2q_*)$ and
$2/(C_2q_*)$, for a sufficiently large absolute $C_2$.
\item For the initial error scale, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-start-scale}
 S:=\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{C_3\mathcal R^{A+C_0+4}\mathcal H}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
\item Set $u_1=S$ and define the subsequent error scales by
$u_{i+1}=\lfloor\lambda u_i\rfloor$.
\item Use iteration lengths $s_i=\lceil u_i/b\rceil$.
\end{itemize}
For $u_B\ge C\log n$, Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-short-head} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-tail-budget}
 q_*\sum_{j>i}d_j\le u_i/4.
\end{equation}
The sums of the $s_i$ and of their rounding errors are
$O(S/b)$. Thus Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-seed-costs} and
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-start-scale} verify
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-fixing-budget} and
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-branch-budget}, for a sufficiently large $C_3$.
For example, the first cost is at most $Cq_*\mathcal HS/b$,
whereas $\theta\ell/4=\Theta(n/\mathcal R^2)$.
The same choice gives
$r_{{\rm SR},i}\le\beta q_{\rm row}/4$ and
$8\max_i s_i\le c_{\rm IP}q_{\rm row}$, since
$q_{\rm row}\ge n/\mathcal R^A$. Hence every iteration has error at most
$2^{-u_i}$.

The proof of \Cref{merge:mixed-correlations} now applies to the
remaining tuple. After fixing the kernel coordinates of the selected
output map as in that proof, all later initial-seed coordinates still have degree at most
$D$. Every Fourier coefficient under consideration has absolute value
at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-phase-bound}
 \beta=\max_i2^{q_*\sum_{j>i}d_j}
                    (2^{-u_i}+2^{-bs_i})
       \le2^{1-3u_B/4}.
\end{equation}
We average the conditional bounds over the fixings that removed inputs
of small rank and over the subsequent affine partitions, so their numbers
of parts do not multiply the bound. Take
$m\le\nu u_B/q_*$ for a sufficiently small absolute $\nu>0$.
The code-dimension constraints hold, and Parseval gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-output-error}
 \Delta((F(X^0),Z),(U_m,Z))
 \le\tfrac12\sqrt{(2^m-1)2^{(q_*-1)m}}\,\beta
 \le2^{-5u_B/8},
\end{equation}
where $Z$ denotes the comparison outputs.

Finally,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi-schedule-loss}
 \begin{aligned}
 B\log(1/\lambda)&=O\!\left(\frac{q_*^2}{\rho_0}\log(2q_*)\right),\\
 \log\mathcal H&=O(\log^2 \mathcal R).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
All remaining factors in $u_B/q_*$ are polynomial in $\mathcal R$.
It follows that the available output length and error exponent are
at least
\[
 n2^{-C_4[(q_*^2/\rho_0)\log(2q_*)+\log^2(2q_*^2/\rho_0)]}.
\]
Choose the theorem constant larger than $C_4$ by a sufficiently
large absolute factor. The resulting slack dominates every polynomial
in $\mathcal R$, verifying $u_B\ge\max\{C\log n,(2T)^4\}$, all
intermediate-row requirements, and the omitted-coordinate condition
$q_*B\le\kappa n/4$. It also absorbs floors and the constants in
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:multi-output-error}.

The size hypothesis implies $q_*^2/\rho=O(\log n)$.
All row counts and lengths are polynomially bounded, with
$\mathcal H=2^{O((\log\log n)^2)}$.
The row-growing sequence has $O(\log n)$ stages and the breaker has
$O(\log h)$ rounds. The primitive algorithms have absolute polynomial
running-time bounds. This proves the pairwise-distinct case uniformly
in $h$ and $\rho$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:collision-partition}
Let $(X^0,\ldots,X^h)$ be jointly affine and let
