$P=\binom h2$. For every integer $L\ge1$, there is a partition
obtained by successively fixing at most $PL$ affine functions, each
determined by the values fixed previously, such that, outside total
mass $P2^{-L}$, for every pair $1\le i<j\le h$, either $X^i=X^j$ throughout
the corresponding part or $X^i\ne X^j$ throughout that part.
Each nonempty part is affine, and conditioning on any such part
reduces the entropy of $X^0$ by at most $PL$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Process each pair $X^i,X^j$ with $1\le i<j\le h$ on each
current part of the partition. The difference
of a pair is uniform on an affine image. If zero is outside this
image, the pair is already distinct. Otherwise the image is a
linear space of dimension $d$. Successively fix independent coordinates
of this image until a coordinate has value one, certifying distinctness
on the resulting part. If $d\le L$, fixing all $d$ coordinates to zero
certifies equality. If $d>L$, declare the part with $L$ initial zeros
exceptional; its conditional mass is $2^{-L}$. Earlier certificates persist
under restriction. Summing the costs and exceptional masses proves
the lemma.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Use the pairwise-distinct construction at rate $\rho_0=\rho/2$.
If $P=\binom h2>0$, take
$L=\lfloor\rho n/(4P)\rfloor$ in \Cref{lem:collision-partition}.
On every nonexceptional part retain one representative of each
comparison equality class. The honest source still has entropy at
least $3\rho n/4$, the representatives differ pointwise, and none
can equal the honest input. Apply the proved guarantee for the same
function built for the original upper bound $h$. Duplicate outputs
to restore the list and average over the parts.

The additional error is $P2^{-L}$, with exponent
$\Omega(\rho n/q_*^2)$. Increasing the theorem constant makes this
smaller than half the target error and leaves the other half for the
tuple construction. Indeed $E_*=n2^{-C\Psi}$ is smaller by an
arbitrarily large constant factor than $\rho n/q_*^2$, uniformly in
the admitted range. When $P=0$, no partition is needed.
All partitioning and equality-class choices occur only in the proof.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
For fixed $\rho,h$, the quantity $\Psi$ is constant and
$E_*=\Omega_{\rho,h}(n)$. Apply
\Cref{thm:joint-affine-quantitative} for sufficiently large $n$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:affine-logarithmic-rate}
For every fixed $h\ge1$ and $0<\eta<1$, there is a constant
$C_{\eta,h}$ such that entropy $C_{\eta,h}n/\log n$ suffices for
an explicit non-malleable affine extractor against $h$ tamperings,
with at least $\lfloor n^{1-\eta}\rfloor$ output bits and error
at most $2^{-n^{1-\eta}}$. The jointly affine tuple guarantee holds
with the same parameters.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
For fixed $h$, $\Psi=O_h(1/\rho)$.
Set $\rho=C_{\eta,h}/\log n$ and choose the constant large enough
that $E_*\ge n^{1-\eta/2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
This proves the remaining case of \Cref{thm:affine-sublinear}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:affine-error-tuning}
For every fixed $h\ge1$ and $0<\rho\le1$, there is
$G_{\rho,h}\le2^{C_h/\rho}$ with the following property.
For positive integers $m,E$ satisfying $E\ge\log n$ and
$G_{\rho,h}(m+E)\le n$, the construction can be chosen to output
$m$ bits with error at most $2^{-E}$ on all jointly affine tuples
in \Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple}. Its degree bounds and the number
of affine bits fixed have the same dependence on the parameters as
in that proof.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Retain the block count, degree of the initial-seed function, and
majority length above, using working honest rate $\rho/2$. Let $P_{\rho,h}$ dominate all minimum
row lengths, including $(2T)^4$, and all polynomial factors in
$h$ and $1/\rho$. It can be chosen polynomial in $1/\rho$ for fixed
$h$. Choose the final error scale to be at least
$C_hP_{\rho,h}(m+E+\log n)$ and set the first scale by multiplying
this quantity, with rounding slack, by $\lambda^{-(B-1)}$.
This ensures all minimum lengths, the Fourier output bound, and error
at most $2^{-E-1}$ before the collision partition.

The length-dependent costs in the upper-bound constraints are at most
linear in the first iteration length. To satisfy these constraints,
it suffices that $n/(m+E+\log n)$ be at least a sufficiently large
polynomial in $1/\rho$ times $\mathcal H\lambda^{-(B-1)}/b$.
For fixed $h$, the logarithm of this bound is
$O_h(\rho^{-1}+\log^2(2/\rho))=O_h(1/\rho)$.
Increase the bound if necessary to make the collision error at most
$2^{-E-1}$. Since $E\ge\log n$, a suitable
$G_{\rho,h}\le2^{C_h/\rho}$ makes $G_{\rho,h}(m+E)\le n$
sufficient for all these requirements.
The row-growing and correlation-breaker algorithms are unchanged;
only their integer length parameters are adjusted.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{def:lbp-weakly-read-once}
For a node $v$, let $\operatorname{Pre}(v)$ be the span of all linear forms queried on all directed source-to-$v$ paths, excluding $q_v$ itself. A linear branching program is \emph{weakly read-once} if
\[
q_v\notin\operatorname{Pre}(v)
\]
for every internal node $v$.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
\label{def:lbp-derivative-bias}
A Boolean function $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ has directional derivative bias at most $\beta$ at entropy $K$ if, for every affine source $X$ of dimension at least $K$ and every $c\in\mathsf{F}_2^n\setminus\{0\}$,
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{D_c f(X)}\right|
=\left|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{f(X)+f(X+c)}\right|\le\beta.
\label{eq:lbp-derivative-bias}
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{def:lbp-section-decorrelation}
Let $1\le k<n$. A Boolean function $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ has $(k,\delta)$ section decorrelation if, for every rank-$k$ linear map $Q:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^k$ and affine maps $\sigma,\tau:\mathsf{F}_2^k\to\mathsf{F}_2^n$ satisfying
\[
Q\circ\sigma=Q\circ\tau=\operatorname{id}_{\mathsf{F}_2^k},
\qquad \operatorname{Im}(\sigma)\cap\operatorname{Im}(\tau)=\varnothing,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_{a\sim U_k}(-1)^{f(\sigma(a))+f(\tau(a))}\right|\le\delta.
\label{eq:lbp-section-decorrelation}
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-nonmalleable-sections}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine extractor. For every nonzero $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^m$, the function $f_u(x)=\langle u,F(x)\rangle$ has $(k,2\varepsilon)$ section decorrelation. It suffices to assume non-malleability against globally fixed-point-free affine involutions.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Fix $Q,\sigma,\tau$ as in \Cref{def:lbp-section-decorrelation}. Put
$\Delta(a)=\sigma(a)+\tau(a)$ and define
\[
T(x)=x+\Delta(Qx).
\]
The map $\Delta$ is affine, $Q\Delta(a)=0$, and $\Delta(a)\ne0$ for every $a$. Consequently $T$ is affine, has no fixed points, and satisfies $QT=Q$. Thus
\[
T^2(x)=x+\Delta(Qx)+\Delta(QT(x))=x,
\qquad T(\sigma(a))=\tau(a).
\]
Since $Q\sigma=\operatorname{id}$, the source $X=\sigma(U_k)$ has dimension $k$. Applying non-malleability and taking the $u$-parity of each output gives
\[
(f_u(\sigma(U_k)),f_u(\tau(U_k)))
\approx_\varepsilon(U_1,f_u(\tau(U_k))).
\]
The sign $(-1)^{z+z'}$ has expectation zero under the ideal distribution. Its expectations under two distributions differ by at most twice their statistical distance, proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-directional-sections}
Suppose $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ has directional derivative bias at most $\beta$ at entropy $K$. For every integer $q<n$ with $2q-n\ge K$, the function $f$ has $(q,\beta)$ section decorrelation.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Fix a rank-$q$ map $Q$ and disjoint sections $\sigma,\tau$ of $Q$. The affine displacement $D(a)=\sigma(a)+\tau(a)$ takes its values in $\ker Q$, so its linear part has rank at most $n-q$. Every nonempty fiber $D^{-1}(c)$ has dimension at least
\begin{equation}
q-(n-q)=2q-n\ge K.
\label{eq:lbp-displacement-entropy}
\end{equation}
Its value $c$ is nonzero, since the section images are disjoint. The map $\sigma$ is injective, so $\sigma(U_q)$ conditioned on $D(U_q)=c$ is uniform on an affine space of the same dimension. On that fiber, $\tau(a)=\sigma(a)+c$. Apply Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-derivative-bias} and average over $c$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-full-cut}
Let $P$ be a size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program on $n$ bits, and let $1\le k<n$. There is a full weakly read-once linear branching program computing $P$, with a set $V$ of at most $2s$ nodes such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every computation reaches exactly one node in $V$.
\item For each $v\in V$, every path reaching $v$ has the same $k$-dimensional query span $W_v$.
\item If the rows of $Q_v:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^k$ form a basis for $W_v$, there is a set $A_v\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^k$ such that an input reaches $v$ exactly when $Q_vx\in A_v$. Its reaching probability is $p_v=|A_v|/2^k$, and $\sum_{v\in V}p_v=1$.
\end{enumerate}
The normalized program has $O(ns)$ vertices. The cut may contain original nodes, inserted nodes, and copies of sinks.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Discard vertices not reachable from the source. For every original internal node $v$, put $W_v=\operatorname{Pre}(v)$ in the original program. Process the edges in topological order. On an original edge $u\to v$ with internal destination,
\[
W_u+\operatorname{span}\{q_u\}\subseteq W_v.
\]
Insert a chain of queries completing a basis of the space on the left to a basis of $W_v$. Both outgoing edges of each inserted query lead to the next node. Inductively, every path reaching an original internal node $v$ now has query span exactly $W_v$. Each inserted query is independent of its preceding space, and $q_v$ remains outside $W_v$. The program is therefore weakly read-once and full.

Give each edge entering an original sink its own copy of that sink. On a terminal edge out of $u$, if $\dim W_u+1<k$, insert ignored independent queries until the prefix rank is $k$. Otherwise no padding is needed. In particular, an edge already at rank $k$ has its own output copy with a well-defined prefix space. The padding queries are chosen outside that edge's prefix space; they are not appended after a shared sink. If the original program is a constant sink, use one chain of $k$ ignored queries. Each edge receives at most $n$ queries, giving size $O(ns)$.

Take the first node of prefix rank $k$ on each computation. These nodes form a cut, since ranks grow by one at every query and every computation now makes at least $k$ queries. Associate an original cut node with itself, and a cut node inserted along an original edge with that edge's source. Each original node has at most two outgoing chains and hence accounts for at most two cut nodes. If the node itself is in the cut, neither outgoing chain contributes another. The constant-program case contributes one node. Thus $|V|\le2s$.

On every path reaching $v\in V$, the $k$ independent queries span $W_v$. Its inputs form one full fiber $Q_vx=a$: all inputs in this fiber follow that path because its queries and answers are fixed. Taking the union over paths gives $Q_v^{-1}(A_v)$ for some $A_v$. Since $Q_vU_n=U_k$, the reaching probability is $|A_v|/2^k$. The cut partitions the inputs, so the probabilities sum to one.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-future-sections}
Fix a node $v$ in the cut of \Cref{lem:lbp-full-cut}, let $Q=Q_v$, and put $d=n-k$. There are affine maps
\[
\sigma_b:\mathsf{F}_2^k\to\mathsf{F}_2^n
\qquad(b\in\mathsf{F}_2^d)
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Q\sigma_b=\operatorname{id}$ for every $b$, and the section images are disjoint and partition $\mathsf{F}_2^n$.
\item The map $(a,b)\mapsto\sigma_b(a)$ is a bijection, so uniform input corresponds to independent uniform $a,b$.
\item There is a Boolean function $P_v:\mathsf{F}_2^d\to\mathsf{F}_2$ such that the subprogram started at $v$ outputs $P_v(b)$ on $\sigma_b(a)$, for every $a,b$. On inputs reaching $v$, this equals $P(x)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Unfold the subprogram rooted at $v$ into a binary decision tree. Extend every terminating path by ignored independent queries until it has exactly $d$ queries from $v$ onward. Each added query is chosen outside the span of $W_v$ and the preceding suffix queries. This tree is used only for the analysis.

At an original query node $w$ on a suffix path, $W_v$ and all preceding suffix queries lie in $\operatorname{Pre}(w)$: concatenate the suffix with a source-to-$v$ path. The weak read-once condition therefore makes the next query independent of those forms. The added queries have the same property by construction. For every fixed $a$, every suffix transcript of length $d$ is thus feasible on $Qx=a$.

Fix a complete transcript $b$, and let $R_b$ be the matrix of the linear forms queried on that transcript. The rows of $Q$ and $R_b$ together form a basis, so
\begin{equation}
Qx=a,\qquad R_bx=b
\label{eq:lbp-section-system}
\end{equation}
have a unique solution $x=\sigma_b(a)$. Inverting this fixed matrix shows that $\sigma_b$ is affine. Conversely, every solution of Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-section-system} follows transcript $b$. Each input has one complete transcript, proving disjointness, coverage, and the bijection. The transcript determines the original terminal output; define $P_v(b)$ to be this output. The argument holds for every $a$, including values outside $A_v$, because independence uses the full prefix space $W_v$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-section-correlation}
Let $1\le k<n$, and suppose $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ has $(k,\delta)$ section decorrelation. Every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program $P$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Corr}(f,P)
\le\sqrt{2s\bigl(\delta+2^{-(n-k)}\bigr)}.
\label{eq:lbp-section-correlation}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Use the cut of \Cref{lem:lbp-full-cut} and the sections of \Cref{lem:lbp-future-sections}. Put $d=n-k$ and $h=(-1)^f$. For each $v\in V$, write $g_v(b)=(-1)^{P_v(b)}$ for the suffix output sign and define
\[
H_v(a)=\mathbf{E}_{b\sim U_d}g_v(b)h(\sigma_b(a)).
\]
For $b\ne b'$, section decorrelation bounds
$|\mathbf{E}_a h(\sigma_b(a))h(\sigma_{b'}(a))|$ by $\delta$. For $b=b'$, the product is one. Hence
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^2
&=\mathbf{E}_{b,b'}g_v(b)g_v(b')\mathbf{E}_a h(\sigma_b(a))h(\sigma_{b'}(a))\\
&\le2^{-d}+(1-2^{-d})\delta\le2^{-d}+\delta.
\end{split}
\label{eq:lbp-section-second-moment}
\end{equation}
All averages over $a$ are uniform on the whole of $\mathsf{F}_2^k$. The contribution from inputs reaching $v$ is
\[
\mathbf{E}_x\mathbf1_{\{x\text{ reaches }v\}}(-1)^{f(x)+P(x)}
=\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz bounds its absolute value by $\sqrt{p_v(2^{-d}+\delta)}$. Summing over the cut and applying Cauchy--Schwarz again gives
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(f,P)
\le\sqrt{2^{-d}+\delta}\sum_{v\in V}\sqrt{p_v}
\le\sqrt{(2^{-d}+\delta)|V|\sum_vp_v}
\le\sqrt{2s(2^{-d}+\delta)}.
\]
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:lbp-conditioning}
The reachability set $A_v$ may be arbitrary. We do not regard $U_k$ conditioned on $A_v$ as an affine source. Instead, fix two future transcripts and average over all uniform past answers, obtaining affine sections to which \Cref{lem:lbp-nonmalleable-sections} applies. Only after the second-moment estimate do we impose reachability, using Cauchy--Schwarz.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-directional-hardness}
Let $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ have directional derivative bias at most $\beta$ at entropy $K$. For every integer $q<n$ with $2q-n\ge K$ and every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program $P$,
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Corr}(f,P)\le\sqrt{2s\bigl(\beta+2^{-(n-q)}\bigr)}.
\label{eq:lbp-directional-hardness}
\end{equation}
In particular, if $F$ is a $(K,\varepsilon)$ directional affine extractor and $K\le n-2$, every nonzero output parity $f_u$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Corr}(f_u,P)
\le\sqrt{2s\bigl(2\varepsilon+2^{-\lfloor(n-K)/2\rfloor}\bigr)}.
\label{eq:lbp-directional-parity}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
\Cref{lem:lbp-directional-sections} gives $(q,\beta)$ section decorrelation, so \Cref{thm:lbp-section-correlation} applies. For the second assertion, take $q=\lceil(n+K)/2\rceil$ and $\beta=2\varepsilon$. Then $q<n$ and $n-q=\lfloor(n-K)/2\rfloor$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-affine-hardness}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine extractor, with $1\le k<n$. For every nonzero $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^m$ and every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program $P$,
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Corr}(f_u,P)
\le\sqrt{2s\bigl(2\varepsilon+2^{-(n-k)}\bigr)}.
\label{eq:lbp-affine-hardness}
\end{equation}
It suffices to assume non-malleability against globally fixed-point-free affine involutions.
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
\Cref{lem:lbp-nonmalleable-sections} gives $(k,2\varepsilon)$ section decorrelation. Apply \Cref{thm:lbp-section-correlation}. In particular,
\[
\mathbf{Pr}[P(U_n)=f_u(U_n)]
\le\frac12+\frac12\sqrt{2s\bigl(2\varepsilon+2^{-(n-k)}\bigr)}.
\]
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:lbp-cubic-trace}
For $n$ divisible by $15$, identify each of three $n/3$-bit blocks with $\mathsf{F}_{2^{n/3}}$, and define
\[
f_n(x,y,z)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathsf{F}_{2^{n/3}}/\mathsf{F}_2}(xyz).
\]
Here $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathsf{F}_{2^{n/3}}/\mathsf{F}_2}(u)=\sum_{j=0}^{n/3-1}u^{2^j}$ is the field trace.
Every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program satisfies
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Corr}(f_n,P)\le\sqrt{5s}\,2^{-n/15}.
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-trace}
\end{equation}
Consequently, exact computation requires size at least $2^{2n/15}/5$.
For every fixed $0<\eta<2/15$, programs of size at most
$2^{(2/15-\eta)n}$ have correlation at most
$\sqrt5\,2^{-\eta n/2}$. These bounds allow any number of independent
uniform auxiliary bits. At every sufficiently large input length $N$,
the same cubic formula applied to the first $3\lfloor N/3\rfloor$ bits requires size
$2^{\lfloor2\lfloor N/3\rfloor/5\rfloor}/5=2^{2N/15-O(1)}$.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{aq:phases}
Let $0\le\varepsilon\le1/2$ and let $q$ be quadratic.
Put $\Gamma_n^2=2\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)2^{-n}$.
If $f$ satisfies~Eqn.~\eqref{aq:derivative} at dimension $k\le n-1$, then
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{x\sim U_n}(-1)^{f(x)+q(x)}\right|
 \le\Gamma_n.
 \label{aq:phase-directional}
\end{equation}
If $f$ is an ordinary affine extractor with error $\varepsilon$ at
dimension $k\le\lceil n/2\rceil-1$, the same correlation is at most
$2\varepsilon$.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
For $a\ne0$, the derivative $D_aq(x)=q(x)+q(x+a)$ is affine.
Its nonempty level sets have dimension at least $n-1$. Applying
Eqn.~\eqref{aq:derivative} on these sets gives
$|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{D_af(x)+D_aq(x)}|\le2\varepsilon$. Therefore
\[
 \left(\mathbf{E}(-1)^{f(x)+q(x)}\right)^2
 =2^{-n}\sum_{a\in\mathsf{F}_2^n}
      \mathbf{E}_x(-1)^{D_af(x)+D_aq(x)}
 \le2^{-n}+(1-2^{-n})2\varepsilon.
\]
For the second assertion, the polar form
\[
 B_q(u,v)=q(u+v)+q(u)+q(v)+q(0)
\]
is an alternating bilinear form: $B_q(u,u)=0$ for every $u$. It has a
totally isotropic subspace $U$ of dimension at least $\lceil n/2\rceil$,
meaning that $B_q(u,v)=0$ for all $u,v\in U$.
On each coset of $U$, $q$ is affine. Split that coset into the
nonempty level sets of $q$. Each resulting affine space has dimension
at least $\lceil n/2\rceil-1$, and $q$ is constant there. The ordinary
affine extractor guarantee bounds the bias of $f+q$ by $2\varepsilon$
on each piece.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{aq:correlation}
Let $T$ be a degree-$2$ decision tree with $L$ leaves. Under the first
hypothesis of \Cref{aq:phases},
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f,T)\le\min\{1,L\Gamma_n\}.
 \label{aq:tree-directional}
\end{equation}
Under its second hypothesis,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f,T)\le\min\{1,2L\varepsilon\}.
 \label{aq:tree-ordinary}
\end{equation}
Consequently, a tree of uniform-input error $\delta<1/2$ has depth at
least $\log_2((1-2\delta)/\Gamma_n)$ in the first case and
$\log_2((1-2\delta)/(2\varepsilon))$ in the second.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Fix a leaf with path queries $q_1,\ldots,q_t$ and answers
$b_1,\ldots,b_t$. Although the tree is non-oblivious, these polynomials
are fixed on this path. Its indicator is
\[
 1_{\mathrm{leaf}}(x)
 =2^{-t}\sum_{a\in\mathsf{F}_2^t}
       (-1)^{a\cdot b+\sum_i a_iq_i(x)}.
\]
Every phase is quadratic, and the absolute coefficient sum is one.
Apply \Cref{aq:phases} and sum over the leaves. A depth-$d$ tree has
$L\le2^d$, whereas error at most $\delta$ gives correlation at least
$1-2\delta$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{aq:common-flat}
The nonempty common zero set of $r$ quadratic polynomials on
$\mathsf{F}_2^n$ contains an affine space of dimension at least
\[
 \max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{n-2r}{r+1}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
Such a space can be chosen through any specified common zero.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Translate the specified zero to the origin. Let $U$ be an
inclusion-maximal linear space on which every polynomial vanishes,
and put $s=\dim U$. Write $B_i$ for the polar form of the $i$th
polynomial and set
\[
 H=\{v:B_i(v,u)=0\text{ for all }u\in U,\ i\in[r]\}.
\]
Then $U\subseteq H$ and $\dim H\ge n-rs$. On $H$, each polynomial
is constant on cosets of $U$, and so defines a quadratic polynomial
on $H/U$ vanishing at zero. If $\dim(H/U)>2r$, the number of their
common zeros is even: sum their common-zero indicator
$\prod_i(1+q_i)$ over this quotient modulo two. Its degree is at most
$2r$, and every monomial misses a coordinate. There would then be a
nonzero common zero, extending $U$. Hence
$n-(r+1)s\le\dim(H/U)\le2r$, as required.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{aq:generic-bounds}
Suppose $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ satisfies~Eqn.~\eqref{aq:joint} with
$0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and $1\le k\le\lceil n/2\rceil-1$.
Put $E=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$. For every nonzero output parity $f$,
\begin{equation}
 D_2(f)\ge
 \max\left\{
 \lceil E-1\rceil,
 \left\lceil\frac{n-k+1}{k+1}\right\rceil,
 \lceil\log_2(n-k+2)\rceil
 \right\}.
 \label{aq:generic-max}
\end{equation}
For computation of the entire vector $F$, include $m$ in this maximum.
The last two terms in~Eqn.~\eqref{aq:generic-max} remain valid for
$1\le k\le n-1$; in this range the first can be replaced by
$\lceil\log_2(1/\Gamma_n)\rceil$.
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
The first term follows from \Cref{aq:correlation} with correlation
one. For the second, a nonempty depth-$t$ leaf is the common zero
set of $t$ quadratics after subtracting the answers. Since $f$ is
an affine disperser at dimension $k$, \Cref{aq:common-flat} implies
\[
 \left\lceil\frac{n-2t}{t+1}\right\rceil\le k-1,
 \qquad
 t\ge\frac{n-k+1}{k+1}.
\]

For the third term, we recall the oblivious argument
of~\cite[Lemma~7.1]{GG26}. If a quadratic map
$Q:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^s$ has $s\le n-k$, choose distinct $u,v$ with
$Q(u)=Q(v)$ and put $a=u+v$. The affine system
\[
 Q(x)+Q(x+a)=0
\]
is consistent and has a solution space of dimension at least
$n-s\ge k$. Every function of $Q$ agrees with its translate by
$a$ throughout that space, contrary to
Eqn.~\eqref{aq:derivative} and $\varepsilon<1/2$. Thus
$D_2^{\mathrm{obl}}(f)\ge n-k+1$. Ask all the polynomials at the
internal nodes of a non-oblivious depth-$d$ tree in an oblivious order.
Their answers determine its output, and there are at most $2^d-1$
such nodes. Hence $2^d-1\ge n-k+1$.

Finally, the ordinary affine extractor guarantee on $U_n$ implies that
$F$ has at least
$(1-\varepsilon)2^m$ distinct outputs. A depth-$d$ tree has at most
$2^d$ outputs, so
$d\ge m+\log_2(1-\varepsilon)>m-1$. Integer depth gives $d\ge m$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{aq:error-floor}
A Boolean affine extractor with error $\varepsilon$ at dimension
$k<n$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon\ge\frac12
 \sqrt{\frac{2^n-2^k}{2^k(2^n-1)}}.
 \label{aq:ordinary-floor}
\end{equation}
If $f$ satisfies~Eqn.~\eqref{aq:derivative} and $1\le k\le n-1$, then
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon\ge\frac12
 \sqrt{\frac{2^{n-1}-2^{k-1}}
 {2^{k-1}(2^{n-1}-1)}}.
 \label{aq:directional-floor}
\end{equation}
In particular, $\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\le k/2+1$ in the second case.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Let $h:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\{-1,1\}$ have mean $\mu$, and let $W$ be a
uniformly chosen affine $k$-space. Put $N=2^n$ and $K=2^k$.
Counting diagonal and distinct ordered pairs gives
\[
 \mathbf{E}_W\left(\mathbf{E}_{x\in W}h(x)\right)^2
 =\frac1K+\left(1-\frac1K\right)
       \frac{N\mu^2-1}{N-1}
 =\frac{N-K+N(K-1)\mu^2}{K(N-1)}
 \ge\frac{N-K}{K(N-1)}.
\]
For an affine extractor each bias has magnitude at most
$2\varepsilon$, proving~Eqn.~\eqref{aq:ordinary-floor}.

For the directional statement, fix $a\ne0$. The function
$(-1)^{f(x)+f(x+a)}$ is invariant under translation by $a$, and so
is a Boolean sign function on the $(n-1)$-dimensional quotient by
$\langle a\rangle$. Affine $k$-spaces whose direction contains
$a$ correspond to affine $(k-1)$-spaces in this quotient. Apply the
same squared-bias bound there. Since $k\le n-1$, its ratio is at
least $2^{-k}$, yielding the final assertion.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{aq:full-entropy}
The condition $k\le n-1$ in \Cref{aq:phases} is necessary. For
$n=2s$, the quadratic $f(x,y)=x\cdot y$ has global bias
$2^{-s}$ and balanced nonzero directional derivatives on $U_n$.
Its non-malleability error against any single nonzero translation on $U_n$ is exactly
$2^{-s-1}$: both marginal sign biases are $2^{-s}$, and their
product bias is zero. Nevertheless $D_2(f)=1$. This is a statement
about translation non-malleability; no guarantee against arbitrary
affine maps is asserted.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{aq:upper}
For every feasible choice of the parameters in
\Cref{param:schedule}, the function $F=\mathsf{anmExt}$ of
\Cref{alg:affine-nm} can be computed exactly by a non-oblivious
degree-$2$ decision tree of depth
\begin{equation}\label{aq:query-sum}
 D_2(F)\le\sum_{i=1}^B(A_i+L_i)\le\frac{8H_\kappa S}{b},
\end{equation}
provided $u_B\ge\log n$. The same bound holds for every fixed
postprocessing of $F$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
In iteration $i$, query all $A_i$ bits of the matrix in
Eqn.~\eqref{branch:seed-matrix}. Each bit is bilinear in two linear
functions of the input and therefore has degree at most two.
The answers determine $\mathsf{H}_i(x)$. With this seed fixed,
\Cref{branch:interface} computes $G_i(x,\mathsf{H}_i(x))$ using at most
$L_i$ affine queries whose coefficients may depend on earlier answers. Once all iteration outputs are known,
the amplifiers and their $\mathsf{XOR}$ require no further queries. Summing the
query counts and applying Eqn.~\eqref{param:queries} proves the claim.
Here each successive fixing in \Cref{branch:interface} is implemented
by an affine query whose coefficients are determined by earlier answers.
In particular, after each growing-row output is known, the next
seeded extractor output is an affine function of the input. The
somewhere-random extractor and the strong correlation breaker act
on values already known, so neither needs to be linear.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{aq:retuning}
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and $E\ge1$. Choose the scales as follows.
\begin{subequations}\label{aq:scale-choice}
\begin{itemize}
\item Set the minimum scale to
\begin{equation}
 L_0=\left\lceil\max\{\lceil\log n\rceil+2,2c,(2T)^4,C_{\min}\}\right\rceil.
\end{equation}
\item Set the target final scale to
\begin{equation}
 t_0=\left\lceil\max\left\{\frac m\nu,
                    \frac{8E}{5},L_0\right\}\right\rceil.
\end{equation}
\item Put
\begin{equation}
 K=\lambda^{-(B-1)}.
\end{equation}
\item Set the initial scale to
\begin{equation}
 S=\lceil K(t_0+2)\rceil.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}
\end{subequations}
Write $\overline S=\lceil S/b\rceil$ for the largest iteration
output length. Suppose that the block lengths and subroutine parameters satisfy
\begin{gather}
 2(n-B\ell)\le\kappa n/4,\notag\\
 16H_\kappa\overline S\le\kappa\ell/16,\notag\\
 H_\kappa(\overline S+\log n)\le\beta_{\rm IP}q/4,\notag\\
 8\overline S\le c_{\rm IP}q,\notag\\
 2\ell+(2H_\kappa+C_*)(\overline S+\log n)\le\kappa n/4.
 \label{aq:upper-feasibility}
\end{gather}
Then \Cref{alg:affine-nm}, with these scales, is an explicit
$m$-bit non-malleable affine extractor for entropy
$\lceil2\kappa n\rceil$ and error at most $2^{-E}$, with
\begin{equation}\label{aq:retuned-depth}
 D_2(F)\le\frac{8H_\kappa}{b}\lceil K(t_0+2)\rceil
 =O\left(\frac{H_\kappa K}{b}(m+E+L_0)\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, for an absolute constant $C$ one may take
\begin{equation}\label{aq:overhead}
 \begin{aligned}
 G_\kappa&=\frac{CH_\kappa K}{b},\\
 \log G_\kappa
 &=O\left(\kappa^{-1}+\log^2(2/\kappa)\right)=O(\kappa^{-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Writing $\mathcal P_\kappa=2c+(2T)^4+C_{\min}+1=(2/\kappa)^{O(1)}$, we obtain
\[
 D_2(F)\le G_\kappa
       \bigl(m+E+\log n+\mathcal P_\kappa\bigr).
\]
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Eqn.~\eqref{param:rounding} gives
\[
 t_0\le u_B\le t_0+3.
\]
Thus $m\le\lfloor\nu u_B\rfloor$, $s_B\ge2c$, and
$5u_B/8\ge E$. The minimum scale supplies the initial-seed and
somewhere-random extractor requirements in
\Cref{branch:seed-ingredients}. Since $s_i\le\overline S$, the
row-length and bilinear-error conditions follow from
Eqn.~\eqref{aq:upper-feasibility}; in particular,
$\epsilon_{\rm IP}\le2^{-8\overline S}$. The growing-row
construction and the unchanged scale-$s_i$ advice and
correlation-breaker parameters give $\epsilon_i\le2^{-u_i}$.

The remaining inequalities imply the parameter constraints of
\Cref{merge:general}. The later-seed estimate in
Eqn.~\eqref{param:tail} is unchanged by the choice of $S$.
Since $bs_i\ge u_i$, \Cref{merge:decay} gives error at most
$2^{-5u_B/8}\le2^{-E}$. Summing $s_i=\lceil u_i/b\rceil$
and using $u_i\ge\log n$ proves the query bound in
\Cref{aq:upper}. Here $\nu$ is an absolute positive constant,
so the definition of $t_0$ gives Eqn.~\eqref{aq:retuned-depth}.
Finally,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \log K&=(B-1)\log(1/\lambda)=O(\kappa^{-1}),\\
 \log(1/b)&=O(\log(2/\kappa)),\\
 \log H_\kappa&=O(\log^2(2/\kappa)).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The geometric ratio is independent of $\kappa$ because the guessed
initial seeds have length $O(u_i+\log n)$, rather than $O(s_i)$.
These estimates prove Eqn.~\eqref{aq:overhead}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{aq:multi-upper}
Fix $0<\rho\le1$ and an integer $h\ge1$. There are constants
$c_{\rho,h},C_{\rho,h}>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$,
every integer $m\ge1$ and real $E\ge1$ with
$m+E\le c_{\rho,h}n$ admit a choice of the seed lengths and
intermediate output lengths in \Cref{sec:multiple-tampering}
for which the construction satisfies \Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple}
with output length $m$ and error at most $2^{-E}$.
Thus its output on $X^0$ is nearly uniform and independent of
all the outputs on $X^1,\ldots,X^u$ together.
Its entire output can be computed exactly by a non-oblivious
degree-$2$ decision tree of depth
\begin{equation}\label{aq:multi-query-bound}
 D_2(F_h)\le C_{\rho,h}(m+E+\log n).
\end{equation}
For fixed $h$, one may take $C_{\rho,h}=2^{O_h(1/\rho)}$.
The same upper bound holds for every query degree $r\ge2$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Fix the block lengths and a dyadic geometric ratio $\lambda\le1/2$
from the pairwise-distinct construction at entropy rate $\rho/2$.
All constants below may depend on $\rho,h$. Let $b_0,c$ be the amplifier parameters in
\Cref{sec:multiple-tampering} and $R_0$ be the code rate.
Choose the remaining parameters in order:
\begin{itemize}
\item Put $\alpha=5/8$.
\item Put $\nu_h=\min\{1/(4(h+1)),R_0/(4b_0c)\}$.
\item Choose sufficiently large constants $C_0,C_{\min}$, with
$C_{\min}$ at least the minimum primitive lengths, $2c$, and $(2T)^4$.
\item Set
\[
 t_0=\left\lceil\max\left\{C_0\log n,\frac m{\nu_h},
              \frac{E+1}{\alpha},C_{\min}\right\}\right\rceil.
\]
\item Set
\[
 S=\left\lceil\lambda^{-(B-1)}(t_0+2)\right\rceil.
\]
\end{itemize}
Starting with $u_1=S$, set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 u_{i+1}&=\lfloor\lambda u_i\rfloor,\\
 s_i&=\lceil u_i/b_0\rceil.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The rounding estimate gives
$t_0\le u_B\le t_0+3$. Thus the output length is feasible and
the pairwise-distinct error is at most
$2^{-\alpha u_B}\le2^{-E-1}$. The seed lengths, matrix lengths,
and affine-query costs are $O_{\rho,h}(s_i+\log n)$.
The same fixed choice of $\lambda$ bounds the later-seed sums.
All remaining parameter constraints hold when $S+\log n$ is a sufficiently
small constant multiple of $n$, which follows by decreasing
$c_{\rho,h}$.

For $P=\binom h2>0$, apply \Cref{lem:collision-partition} with
$L=\lceil E+1+\log_2P\rceil$. Its exceptional mass is at most
$2^{-E-1}$. Decreasing $c_{\rho,h}$ also ensures $PL\le\rho n/2$,
so the conditional entropy of $X^0$ on each nonexceptional
part of the partition is at least $\rho n/2$. Apply the guarantee
for pairwise distinct inputs on that part, then duplicate the
outputs corresponding to identical inputs. Averaging gives
total error at most $2^{-E}$. For $h=1$, no collision partition
is needed.

To compute the function, query every bit of the bilinear seed
matrix in each iteration using degree-$2$ queries. The initial seed is then known, and the
advice and remaining computation use
$O_{\rho,h}(s_i+\log n)$ affine queries whose coefficients may depend on earlier answers, by
\Cref{branch:advice} and \Cref{lem:multi-retained}. In particular, every
nonlinear seed computation in the additional correlation-breaker
rounds is determined by previously computed extractor outputs. The amplifiers and
their $\mathsf{XOR}$ require no further queries. Hence
\[
 D_2(F_h)\le\sum_{i=1}^B(A_i+L_i)
       =O_{\rho,h}(S+\log n)
       =O_{\rho,h}(m+E+\log n).
\]
The collision partition is used only in the analysis. There are
$O_h(1/\rho)$ iterations, the ratio $\lambda$ depends only on
$h$, and the remaining multiplicative overhead is
$2^{O_h(\log^2(2/\rho))}$. This gives the stated dependence
of $C_{\rho,h}$ on the entropy rate.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Choose a sufficiently large absolute constant $C$. For the first
claim take $\kappa=C\log\log n/(2\log n)$ and
\[
 m=E=\lceil n^{1-\eta}\rceil.
\]
By Eqn.~\eqref{aq:overhead},
\[
 \log G_\kappa
 =O\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}
              +(\log\log n)^2\right)=o(\log n).
\]
Thus \Cref{aq:retuning} gives $D_2(F_n)\le n^{1-\eta+o(1)}$.
Every scale and query budget is $n^{1-\eta+o(1)}$, while
$q$ and $\kappa\ell$ are $n/(\log n)^{O(1)}$. All primitive
minimum lengths are $(\log n)^{O(1)}$. The remaining term
$2\ell$ is at most $\kappa n/32$, and the reserved coordinates
satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{aq:upper-feasibility}. Hence all feasibility
conditions hold for sufficiently large $n$. The generic error bound
gives $D_2(f_n)\ge E-1$, and directional dispersion gives
$D_2^{\mathrm{obl}}(f_n)\ge n-k_n+1$.

For the second claim take $\kappa=C\log\log\log n/(2\log\log n)$, with output length and error exponent
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 m&=\lceil a\log n\rceil,\\
 E&=\lceil e\log n\rceil.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Now
\[
 \log G_\kappa
 =O\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log\log\log n}
              +(\log\log\log n)^2\right)=o(\log\log n).
\]
Consequently $D_2(G_n)\le(\log n)^{1+o(1)}$.
The primitive minimum lengths are $(\log\log n)^{O(1)}=o(\log n)$,
and every scale and query budget is $(\log n)^{1+o(1)}$.
Since $q,\kappa\ell=n/(\log\log n)^{O(1)}$, feasibility again
holds. The error-dependent lower bound is $e\log n-O(1)$,
and the oblivious lower bound is $n-k_n+1$.
All primitive parameters and running times are polynomial in $n$.
Dyadic choices and integer rounding, as in \Cref{aq:retuning},
preserve uniform explicitness.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{ldt:transfer}
For a non-oblivious degree-$r$ decision tree $T$ with $L$ leaves,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f,T)\le\min\{1,L\delta_r(f)\}.
 \label{ldt:adaptive-transfer}
\end{equation}
For an oblivious degree-$r$ decision tree of depth $t$,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f,T)\le\min\{1,2^{t/2}\delta_r(f)\}.
 \label{ldt:oblivious-transfer}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 L_r(f)\ge2^{\lambda_r(f)},\qquad
 D_r(f)\ge\lambda_r(f),\qquad
 D_r^{\mathrm{obl}}(f)\ge2\lambda_r(f).
 \label{ldt:exact-transfer}
\end{equation}
For uniform-input error at most $\eta<1/2$, replace
$\lambda_r(f)$ in the two depth bounds by
$\lambda_r(f)+\log_2(1-2\eta)$, and multiply the leaf bound by
$1-2\eta$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
The proof of \Cref{aq:correlation} applies in every degree: on a fixed
path, the leaf indicator is a linear combination of phases
$(-1)^{\sum_i a_iq_i}$ with absolute coefficient sum one. Each exponent
has degree at most $r$. Its signed mass is therefore at most
$\delta_r(f)$ in absolute value. Summing over leaves proves
Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:adaptive-transfer}.

In the oblivious case let $q_1,\ldots,q_t$ be the fixed queries.
There is a function $H:\mathsf{F}_2^t\to\{-1,1\}$ with
$(-1)^{T(x)}=H(q_1(x),\ldots,q_t(x))$. Expand $H$ in its Fourier
basis. Parseval and Cauchy--Schwarz give
$\sum_a|\widehat H(a)|\le2^{t/2}$. Every resulting phase is again a
degree-$r$ polynomial, proving Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:oblivious-transfer}.
This argument does not assume that the query answers are independent
or uniformly distributed. Finally, a depth-$t$ binary tree has at most
$2^t$ leaves, and uniform-input error at most $\eta$ gives correlation
at least $1-2\eta$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{ldt:expected-queries}
Suppose $\delta_r(f)\le\delta<1$, where $\delta>0$, and put
$\Lambda=\log_2(1/\delta)$. Let a randomized non-oblivious degree-$r$
decision tree have uniform-input error at most $\eta<1/2$, and let
$Q$ be its number of queries. Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{E} Q\ge\Lambda\frac{1-2\eta-\delta}{1-\delta},\qquad
 \mathbf{Pr}[Q\le t]\le2\eta+2^t\delta\quad(t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}).
 \label{ldt:expected-tail}
\end{equation}
Both probabilities include the internal randomness of the tree.
In particular, zero-error computation requires $\mathbf{E} Q\ge\Lambda$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
First fix the internal randomness. For each leaf $v$, let $p_v$
be its probability and $c_v=\mathbf{E}[(-1)^{f(X)}\mathbf1_v(X)]$.
The leaf expansion in \Cref{ldt:transfer} gives
$|c_v|\le\min\{p_v,\delta\}$. For $0\le p\le1$,
\[
 p\log_2(1/p)\ge
 \frac{\Lambda}{1-\delta}\bigl(\min\{p,\delta\}-\delta p\bigr).
\]
For $p\le\delta$, this follows from $\log_2(1/p)\ge\Lambda$;
for $p\ge\delta$, it follows from concavity of $p\log_2(1/p)$
and its chord between $\delta$ and $1$. The strings of answers leading to leaves form a prefix-free binary
code: no such string is a proper prefix of another. Hence
$\mathbf{E} Q\ge H(v)$, where $H(v)=\sum_v p_v\log_2(1/p_v)$ is the
Shannon entropy of the leaf distribution. Summing the preceding
inequality over leaves gives
\[
 |\operatorname{Corr}(f,T)|
 \le\delta+\frac{1-\delta}{\Lambda}\mathbf{E} Q.
\]
Average over the internal randomness and use success correlation
at least $1-2\eta$.

For the second assertion, at most $2^t$ leaves have depth at most
$t$. Their signed success mass is at most $2^t\delta$, and at
least $\mathbf{Pr}[Q\le t]$ minus twice the error mass on those leaves.
Averaging again proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{ldt:joint-extraction}
Let $r\ge2$ and put $s=r-2$. Assume $s\le n$ and $0\le\varepsilon<1/2$. Suppose
$F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ is an affine extractor with error
$\varepsilon$ at dimension $k$. When $s\ge1$, assume in addition that,
for every linearly independent $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ and every affine source
$X$ of dimension at least $k$,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl(F(X),(F(X+\omega\cdot\boldsymbol a))_{\omega\ne0}\bigr)
 \approx_\varepsilon
 \bigl(U_m,(F(X+\omega\cdot\boldsymbol a))_{\omega\ne0}\bigr),
 \quad \omega\in\mathsf{F}_2^s.
 \label{ldt:cube-extraction}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 K_{s,n}&=\left\lceil\frac{n+s}{2}\right\rceil-1,\\
 p_{s,n}&=1-\prod_{i=0}^{s-1}(1-2^{i-n}),\\
 B_{s,n}&=2\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)p_{s,n},
 \end{aligned}
 \label{ldt:cube-parameters}
\end{equation}
where $p_{0,n}=0$. If $k\le K_{s,n}$, every nonzero output parity $f$
of $F$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \delta_r(f)&\le B_{s,n}^{1/2^s},\\
 D_r(f)&\ge\frac{\log_2(1/B_{s,n})}{2^s},\\
 D_r^{\mathrm{obl}}(f)&\ge
                \frac{\log_2(1/B_{s,n})}{2^{s-1}}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{ldt:cube-bounds}
\end{equation}
For $s=0$, only the ordinary affine extractor guarantee is required.
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
The case $s=0$ is the ordinary affine extractor case of \Cref{aq:phases}.
Suppose $s\ge1$, fix $p$ of degree at most $r$, and apply
Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:differencing} to $g=f+p$. Independent directions occur
with probability $1-p_{s,n}$. For such directions, put
$A=\operatorname{span}\{a_1,\ldots,a_s\}$. The polynomial
$D_{\boldsymbol a}p$ has degree at most two and is invariant under
translation by $A$. It therefore descends to a degree-$2$ polynomial
on $\mathsf{F}_2^n/A$.

As in \Cref{aq:phases}, the quotient can be partitioned into affine
spaces on which this polynomial is constant, each of dimension at
least $\lceil(n-s)/2\rceil-1$. Their lifts have dimension at least
$K_{s,n}$. On any such lifted space, apply
Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:cube-extraction} and take the product of the output
parity signs at all $2^s$ vertices. The ideal expectation is zero,
since the output parity at the original source is replaced by a
uniform bit independent of all the other output parities. The absolute expectation is at most $2\varepsilon$.
The phase $D_{\boldsymbol a}p$ is constant on the piece, so the same
bound holds after multiplying by this phase. Averaging over pieces
bounds the inner absolute value in Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:differencing} by
$2\varepsilon$. For dependent directions use the bound one. This
proves $\delta_r(f)^{2^s}\le B_{s,n}$; the depth bounds follow from
\Cref{ldt:transfer}.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{ldt:matching-depth}
Fix $r\ge2$, $0<\rho<1/2$, and
$h\ge\max\{1,2^{r-2}-1\}$. For
$1\le m\le E$, $E\ge\log n$, and
$m+E\le c_{\rho,h}n$, the construction of
\Cref{aq:multi-upper} satisfies, for every nonzero output parity $f$,
\[
 \frac{E}{2^{r-2}}-O_r(1)
 \le D_r(f)\le D_r(F_h)\le D_2(F_h)
 \le O_{\rho,h}(E).
\]
In particular, both $D_r(f)$ and $D_r(F_h)$ are
$\Theta_{\rho,h,r}(E)$.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Take $c_{\rho,h}\le1$. For sufficiently large $n$ the entropy
threshold $\lceil\rho n\rceil$ is below $n/2$.
\Cref{ldt:joint-extraction} gives the lower bound, and
\Cref{aq:multi-upper} gives the upper bound since
$m+\log n\le2E$. A tree computing $F_h$ also computes each
output parity, and degree-$2$ queries are allowed for every $r\ge2$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{ldt:sublinear-cubic}\label{ldt:sublinear-degree}
For every fixed $r\ge2$ and $0<\eta<1$, there is an explicit
non-malleable affine extractor with entropy threshold
$\lceil C_{\eta,r}n/\log n\rceil$, output length $\lfloor n^{1-\eta}\rfloor$,
and error at most $2^{-n^{1-\eta}}$, such that every nonzero
output parity $f$ satisfies
\[
 D_r(f)\ge\frac{n^{1-\eta}}{2^{r-2}}-O_r(1),\qquad
 D_r^{\mathrm{obl}}(f)\ge\frac{n^{1-\eta}}{2^{r-3}}-O_r(1).
\]
The same bounds hold for every fixed uniform-input error below $1/2$.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Use \Cref{thm:joint-affine-quantitative} with
$h=\max\{1,2^{r-2}-1\}$. Its common output and error exponent
is at least $n^{1-\eta}$ when $C_{\eta,r}$ is sufficiently large.
The entropy threshold is $o(n)$. Apply
\Cref{ldt:joint-extraction} and \Cref{ldt:transfer}; for $r=2$, the
ordinary affine extractor bound gives the sharper constant $E-1$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{ldt:growing-degree-extractor}
Fix $0<\rho<1/2$ and $0<\eta<1$. There is a constant
$c_{\rho,\eta}>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$
and integers $r\ge3$ satisfying
\[
 2^{r-2}\le c_{\rho,\eta}
            \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}},
\]
our non-malleable affine extractor has entropy threshold
$\lceil\rho n\rceil$, output length $\lfloor n^{1-\eta}\rfloor$,
and error at most $2^{-n^{1-\eta}}$, and every nonzero output
parity $f$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 D_r(f)&\ge\frac{n^{1-\eta}-\log_2 3}{2^{r-2}},\\
 L_r(f)&\ge2^{(n^{1-\eta}-\log_2 3)/2^{r-2}},\\
 D_r^{\mathrm{obl}}(f)&\ge
                  \frac{n^{1-\eta}-\log_2 3}{2^{r-3}}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{ldt:growing-degree-bounds}
\end{equation}
For uniform-input error at most $\gamma<1/2$, add
$\log_2(1-2\gamma)$ to the non-oblivious depth bound and twice this
quantity to the oblivious bound, and multiply the leaf bound by
$1-2\gamma$.
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Set $h=2^{r-2}-1$ in \Cref{thm:joint-affine-quantitative}.
Its quantified tampering range gives the stated extractor parameters.
Put $a=r-2$ and $E=n^{1-\eta}$. For sufficiently large $n$,
$E\le n-a$ and $\lceil\rho n\rceil\le K_{a,n}$.
The probability of dependent differencing directions satisfies
\[
 p_{a,n}\le\sum_{j=0}^{a-1}2^{j-n}<2^{a-n}\le2^{-E}.
\]
Consequently $B_{a,n}\le3\cdot2^{-E}$ in
Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:cube-parameters}. Apply
\Cref{ldt:joint-extraction} and \Cref{ldt:transfer}.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{ldt:common-flat}
Let $q_1,\ldots,q_t$ have degree at most $a$ on $\mathsf{F}_2^N$,
and let $x_0$ be a common zero. Their common zero set contains an
affine space through $x_0$ of dimension $u$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 N\le u+tW_a(u).
 \label{ldt:common-flat-bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Translate $x_0$ to zero and choose an inclusion-maximal linear
common-zero space $U$, of dimension $u$. In complementary coordinates
$v\in\mathsf{F}_2^{N-u}$ and coordinates $z\in\mathsf{F}_2^u$ on $U$,
write
\[
 q_i(v,z)=\sum_{J\subseteq[u]}c_{i,J}(v)\prod_{j\in J}z_j.
\]
The coefficient $c_{i,J}$ has degree at most $a-|J|$ and vanishes
at zero. The coefficients for $|J|=a$ vanish identically, and those
for $|J|>a$ are absent. The sum of the degree bounds of the remaining
coefficients is at most $tW_a(u)$.

If $N-u>tW_a(u)$, the common-zero indicator
$\prod_{i,J}(1+c_{i,J}(v))$, viewed over $\mathsf{F}_2$, has degree
less than $N-u$. Its sum over $v$ is zero: every monomial misses a
coordinate. Thus the number of common zeros of the coefficient
system is even. Zero is one such solution, so there is a nonzero
solution $v$. Every $q_i$ then vanishes on both $U$ and $v+U$, and
hence on the larger linear space $U+\operatorname{span}\{v\}$.
This contradicts maximality and proves
Eqn.~\eqref{ldt:common-flat-bound}.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
\label{ldt:disperser-depth}
If $f$ is an affine disperser at dimension $1\le k\le n$, then
\begin{equation}
 D_r(f)\ge
 \left\lceil\frac{n-k+1}{W_r(k-1)}\right\rceil.
 \label{ldt:disperser-adaptive}
\end{equation}
If $f$ is a directional affine disperser at dimension $2\le k\le n$,
then
\begin{equation}
 D_r^{\mathrm{obl}}(f)\ge
 \left\lceil\frac{n-k+1}{W_{r-1}(k-2)}\right\rceil.
 \label{ldt:disperser-oblivious}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
A nonempty leaf of length $t$ is defined by a consistent system of
$t$ degree-$r$ equations. Every affine space contained in this leaf
has dimension at most $k-1$. By \Cref{ldt:common-flat} and the
monotonicity of $W_r$, we have $n\le k-1+tW_r(k-1)$.

For the second bound, let $q_1,\ldots,q_t$ be the oblivious queries.
The assertion is immediate if $t\ge n$, so assume $t<n$. Two
distinct inputs have the same query vector; let $a\ne0$ be their
difference. The equations $D_aq_i(x)=0$ are consistent, have degree
at most $r-1$, and descend to the quotient by
$\operatorname{span}\{a\}$. A common-zero affine space of dimension
$u$ in this quotient lifts to one of dimension $u+1$ on which the
query vectors at $x$ and $x+a$ coincide. Consequently $D_af=0$
there, and directional dispersion implies $u\le k-2$.
\Cref{ldt:common-flat} on the $(n-1)$-dimensional quotient now gives
$n-1\le k-2+tW_{r-1}(k-2)$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
\label{thm:local-rectangle}
Fix a partition $I\sqcup J=[n]$ with
$|I|,|J|\ge h=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Suppose $f$ is nonconstant on
every product $A\times B$, where
$A\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^I$, $B\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^J$, and $|A|,|B|\ge2^k$.
For $\ell\ge3$, put
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 c_\ell&=\frac{\lfloor\ell^2/4\rfloor-1}{\ell-2},\\
 b_\ell&=(\ell-2)\sqrt{\frac{\ln2}{2}}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:local-constants}
\end{equation}
Every exact non-oblivious $\ell$-local tree of depth $d$ computing $f$
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 c_\ell d+b_\ell\sqrt d>h-k.
 \label{eq:local-rectangle}
\end{equation}
At locality three the stronger bound $d>h-k$ holds.
In particular, the hypotheses hold for every sumset disperser at
entropy $(k,k)$.
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Maintain nonempty sets $A\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^I$ and
$B\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^J$ whose product reaches one node of the tree.
Initially both sets are full cubes. Suppose the current query uses
$a$ coordinates of $I$ and $b$ of $J$, with $a+b\le\ell$.
If $a,b>0$, fix the queried coordinates in $A$ to a most frequent
pattern, retaining at least a $2^{-a}$ fraction. The query now
depends only on $B$; retain its more frequent answer, keeping at
least half of $B$. Interchanging the sources gives another choice.
Thus the two available upper bounds on the losses in
$(\log|A|,\log|B|)$ are
\begin{equation}
 (a,1)\quad\hbox{and}\quad(1,b).
 \label{eq:local-loss-vectors}
\end{equation}
Each choice retains a product contained in an actual child.
A one-sided query costs at most $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$; a constant
query costs nothing.

For $a+b>2$, choose the first vector in
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-loss-vectors} with probability
$(b-1)/(a+b-2)$, and the second otherwise. Each coordinate of
the resulting random vector $V$ has expectation
\[
 \frac{ab-1}{a+b-2}\le c_\ell.
\]
Indeed, at a fixed sum $s=a+b$ the product is largest at the
balanced integer pair, and
$(\lfloor s^2/4\rfloor-1)/(s-2)$ is nondecreasing for $s\ge3$.
If $a=b=1$, use $(1,1)$ deterministically. Each coordinate of
$V$ ranges over an interval of length at most $\ell-2$.

Let $D_I,D_J$ be cumulative upper bounds on the entropy losses,
and fix $\eta>0$. Use the potential
$\Phi=e^{\eta D_I}+e^{\eta D_J}$.
A random variable $Z$ in an interval of length $R$ satisfies
\[
 \mathbf{E} e^{\eta Z}\le
 \exp\bigl(\eta\mathbf{E} Z+\eta^2R^2/8\bigr).
\]
To see this, the second derivative of
$\log\mathbf{E} e^{\eta Z}$ is a variance under an exponentially
tilted distribution, hence at most $R^2/4$; integrate twice.
Therefore one of the two restrictions multiplies $\Phi$ by at most
\[
 \exp\bigl(\eta c_\ell+\eta^2(\ell-2)^2/8\bigr).
\]
Choose that restriction. The deterministic one-sided cases satisfy
the same estimate. Starting from $\Phi=2$, after at most $d$ queries
we obtain
\[
 \max\{D_I,D_J\}
 \le c_\ell d+\frac{\ln2}{\eta}
                 +\frac{d\eta(\ell-2)^2}{8}.
\]
For $d>0$, optimizing $\eta$ gives the right side of
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-rectangle}. If this quantity is at most
$h-k$, both sets have size at least $2^k$ at the resulting leaf,
contrary to the hypothesis on $f$. The case $d=0$ is immediate.

At locality three, every two-sided query has $\min\{a,b\}=1$.
One choice in Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-loss-vectors} then costs at
most $(1,1)$, so each source loses at most $d$ bits.
Finally, embed $A$ and $B$ in their disjoint coordinate blocks,
with zeroes elsewhere. Their sumset is exactly $A\times B$.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:local-small}
If $f$ is an affine disperser at dimension $k$, then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{LDT}_{2}(f)\ge n-k+1,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{LDT}_{3}(f),\operatorname{LDT}_{4}(f)
 \ge\left\lfloor\frac{n-k}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
 \label{eq:local-small}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Maintain an affine space $W$ of inputs reaching the current node.
Its projection onto the query support is an affine space of
dimension $r\le\ell$. A monochromatic affine subspace of this
image pulls back to a subspace of the same codimension in $W$.
For $r\le1$, fixing a point costs at most one dimension. For
$r=2,3$, some color contains two points, which form an affine line.
For $r=4$, some color contains at least eight points. Among their
$28$ unordered pairs two have the same nonzero sum, since only
$15$ sums are possible. These pairs are disjoint and their union
is an affine plane. Thus the codimension cost is at most one for
$\ell=2$, and at most two for $\ell=3,4$.
At a leaf the surviving affine space has dimension at least
$n-d$ or $n-2d$, respectively. Its dimension must be below $k$.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- corollary-11: body_md -->
\label{cor:local-explicit-family}
There is an explicit Boolean family $f_n$, independent of $\ell$,
such that, uniformly for $3\le\ell\le n$,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{LDT}_{\ell}(f_n)
 \ge\frac{2n}{\ell+2}
 -O\left(\frac{\log n}{\ell}+\sqrt{\frac n\ell}+1\right).
 \label{eq:local-uniform}
\end{equation}
The same family satisfies
$\operatorname{LDT}_{2}(f_n)\ge n-O(\log n)$ and
$\operatorname{LDT}_{3}(f_n),\operatorname{LDT}_{4}(f_n)
\ge n/2-O(\log n)$.
For $\ell\to\infty$ and $\ell=o(n)$,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{LDT}_{\ell}(f_n)\ge(2-o(1))n/\ell.
 \label{eq:local-growing}
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-11 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
The sumset extractor of Li~\cite{Li23} gives one Boolean family at
entropy $k=C\log n$ and any prescribed constant error. Fix an
error below $1/2$ and apply \Cref{thm:local-rectangle}.
If $d<(h-k)/c_\ell$, Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-rectangle} implies
\[
 d>\frac{h-k}{c_\ell}
       -\frac{b_\ell}{c_\ell}\sqrt{\frac{h-k}{c_\ell}}.
\]
The same weak lower bound holds when $d\ge(h-k)/c_\ell$.
Now $c_\ell=\Theta(\ell)$, $b_\ell/c_\ell=O(1)$, and
\[
 c_\ell=\begin{cases}
 (\ell+2)/4,&\ell\text{ even},\\
 (\ell+2)/4-1/(4(\ell-2)),&\ell\text{ odd}.
 \end{cases}
\]
This proves Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-uniform}, including the vacuous
small-$n$ cases after adjusting the absolute constant.
A sumset disperser is an affine disperser: take independent
uniform sources on an affine space and its direction space.
Thus \Cref{prop:local-small} applies to the same family.
Finally divide the error term in Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-uniform}
by $n/\ell$ to obtain Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-growing}.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:local-rectangle-cost}
A single $\ell$-local query can force a loss of $\Omega(\ell)$ bits when the surviving inputs must form a rectangle. For
$q(x,y)=\langle x,y\rangle$ on two $r$-bit blocks,
every monochromatic rectangle $A\times B$ satisfies
$|A||B|\le2^r$. Indeed, constancy implies
$\langle a+a',b+b'\rangle=0$ for all $a,a'\in A$, $b,b'\in B$.
Hence $\mathsf{Span}(A-A)$ and $\mathsf{Span}(B-B)$ are orthogonal, and their
dimensions sum to at most $r$. Since $A$ and $B$ lie in cosets
of these spans, the bound follows. With $\ell=2r$, one query
can therefore force at least $\ell/2$ bits of total loss.
In the next argument, we choose the coordinate partition using all query supports on a path at once.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:local-signed-completion}
Let $A\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^m$, where $m\ge k+1$, and put
$\alpha=|A|/2^m$ and $\theta=2^{k-m}$.
The measure $2^{-m}\mathbf1_A$ is a signed combination of
probability distributions of min-entropy at least $k$, with absolute
coefficient sum at most $\min\{1,\alpha+2\theta\}$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
If $\alpha\ge\theta$, use $2^{-m}\mathbf1_A=\alpha U_A$.
The claim is immediate if $A$ is empty. Otherwise, when
$0<\alpha<\theta\le1/2$, let $R$ be uniform on
$\mathsf{F}_2^m\setminus A$ and put
\[
 P=\theta^{-1}2^{-m}\mathbf1_A+(1-\alpha/\theta)R.
\]
Both $P$ and $R$ have point masses at most $2^{-k}$: on $A$,
$P$ has mass exactly $2^{-k}$, and on its complement its mass is
$(\theta-\alpha)/(\theta(1-\alpha)2^m)\le2^{-k}$.
Now $2^{-m}\mathbf1_A=\theta P-(\theta-\alpha)R$, whose
absolute coefficient sum is $2\theta-\alpha\le\min\{1,\alpha+2\theta\}$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:local-separated-leaves}
Suppose every path of a depth-$d$ tree $T$ with $L$ leaves has a
separated partition with $|I|,|J|\ge m\ge k+1$.
If $f$ is a Boolean sumset extractor at entropy $(k,k)$ and error
$\varepsilon$, then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f,T)
 \le2\varepsilon(1+6L2^{k-m})
 \le2\varepsilon(1+6\cdot2^{d+k-m}).
 \label{eq:local-separated-correlation}
\end{equation}
If $f$ is only a sumset disperser at entropy $(k,k)$, exact computation
is impossible whenever $m\ge d+k$.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Fix a leaf $\tau$ and its separated partition. On a slice $x_S=s$,
write the leaf as $A_s\times B_s\times\{s\}$, with densities
$\alpha_s,\beta_s$ in their respective coordinate cubes.
Let $\theta=2^{k-m}\le1/2$.
Apply \Cref{lem:local-signed-completion} to both factors.
Their product has a signed decomposition with absolute coefficient sum
at most
\[
 (\alpha_s+2\theta)(\beta_s+2\theta)
 \le\alpha_s\beta_s+6\theta.
\]
Each product distribution is the sum of two independent entropy-$k$
sources: embed the first in $I\cup S$, with fixed $S$ coordinates,
and the second in $J$, with zeroes elsewhere.
The absolute bias of $f$ on each such sum is at most $2\varepsilon$.
Averaging over $s$ bounds the leaf's signed contribution by
$2\varepsilon(p_\tau+6\theta)$, where
$p_\tau=\mathbf{Pr}[U_n\text{ reaches }\tau]=\mathbf{E}_s\alpha_s\beta_s$.
Sum over the leaves and use $\sum_\tau p_\tau=1$.

For dispersion, some leaf has probability at least $2^{-d}$, and
some slice of that leaf satisfies $\alpha_s\beta_s\ge2^{-d}$.
Both factors therefore have density at least $2^{-d}$, and each set
has size at least $2^{m-d}\ge2^k$. Their product is an admissible
sumset contained in a monochromatic leaf, a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:local-symmetric-separator}
For any collection of at most $d$ supports of size at most $\ell$,
put $\mu=(n/2)2^{-d\ell/n}$.
If $\mu\ge8\ell\ln4$, there is a separated partition with
$|I|,|J|\ge\lfloor\mu/2\rfloor$.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Add a singleton support for each coordinate absent from the collection.
If $t_v$ is the resulting incidence count of coordinate $v$, then
$t_v\ge1$ and $\sum_vt_v\le d\ell+n$.
Color the supports independently red or blue with equal probability.
Let $I$ consist of coordinates whose incident supports are all red,
and $J$ of those whose incident supports are all blue.
These sets are disjoint, and no original support meets both.
Convexity gives
\[
 \mathbf{E}|I|=\mathbf{E}|J|=\sum_v2^{-t_v}\ge n2^{-(d\ell+n)/n}=\mu.
\]
Each random support color affects at most $\ell$ coordinate
indicators. The read-$\ell$ tail bound of
Gavinsky, Lovett, Saks, and Srinivasan~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{GLSS15}
states that a sum of such indicators with expectation $\nu$ is
below $\nu/2$ with probability at most $e^{-\nu/(8\ell)}$.
Consequently each event $|I|<\mu/2$ and $|J|<\mu/2$ has
probability at most $1/4$. Some coloring avoids both events.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- theorem-25: body_md -->
\label{thm:local-sumset-logarithmic}
Fix $0<\delta<1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$.
Let $f_n$ be a Boolean sumset extractor at entropy
$(C\log n,C\log n)$ and error $\varepsilon$, for a fixed $C$.
There is $c_\delta>0$ such that every non-oblivious $\ell$-local
tree $T$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f_n,T)\le2\varepsilon(1+o(1))
 \quad\text{if}\quad
 \operatorname{depth}(T)\le c_\delta\frac n\ell\log\ell,
 \label{eq:local-sumset-logarithmic}
\end{equation}
whenever $\ell\to\infty$ and $\ell\le n^{1-\delta}$.
In particular,
\[
 \operatorname{LDT}_{\ell}(f_n)
 =\Omega_\delta\left(\frac n\ell\log\ell\right).
\]
The explicit sumset extractor of~\cite{Li23} supplies one such family
for every prescribed constant $\varepsilon$.
<!-- end theorem-25 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Take
$c_\delta=\min\{1/4,\delta/(4(1-\delta))\}$ and
$d\le c_\delta(n/\ell)\log\ell$.
Then $\mu=(n/2)2^{-d\ell/n}\ge n/(2\ell^{c_\delta})$.
Since $\ell\le n^{1-\delta}$,
\[
 \frac\mu\ell\ge\frac12n^{1-(1-\delta)(1+c_\delta)}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus \Cref{lem:local-symmetric-separator} applies to every leaf path
with $m=\lfloor\mu/2\rfloor$.
Moreover,
\[
 \frac d\mu=O\left(\frac{\log\ell}{\ell^{1-c_\delta}}\right)=o(1),
 \qquad C\log n=o(\mu).
\]
Hence $m-d-C\log n\to\infty$, and
\Cref{prop:local-separated-leaves} proves the correlation bound and
excludes exact computation.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:local-asymmetric-separator}
Fix $0<\rho<1/2$. For a collection of at most $d$ supports of
size at most $\ell$, set
\begin{itemize}
 \item $a_\rho=(1-\rho)/2$ and $\kappa_\rho=a_\rho(\ln4-3/4)$;
 \item $\lambda=1+d\ell/n$ and $p=a_\rho/(4\lambda)$;
 \item $t=\lfloor np^\lambda-ne^{-\kappa_\rho n/\ell}\rfloor$.
\end{itemize}
If $t>0$, there is a separated partition with
$|I|\ge t$ and $|J|\ge(1-a_\rho)n$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Again add singleton supports for unused coordinates. Their sizes
$s_i$ satisfy $1\le s_i\le\ell$ and $\sum_i s_i\le\lambda n$.
Color each support red independently with probability $p$.
Define $I,J$ by all-red and all-blue incidence, respectively.
As before, $\mathbf{E}|I|\ge np^\lambda$.
Let $W$ be the sum of the sizes of the red supports. Then
$n-|J|\le W$, and independence gives
\[
 \mathbf{E}4^{W/\ell}
 =\prod_i(1+p(4^{s_i/\ell}-1))
 \le\exp\left(\frac{3p}{\ell}\sum_i s_i\right)
 \le e^{3a_\rho n/(4\ell)}.
\]
Here $4^x-1\le3x$ for $0\le x\le1$.
Markov's inequality yields
$\mathbf{Pr}[W>a_\rho n]\le e^{-\kappa_\rho n/\ell}$.
On the event $G=\{W\le a_\rho n\}$, the set $J$ has the
required size, and
\[
 \mathbf{E}[|I|\mathbf1_G]\ge np^\lambda-ne^{-\kappa_\rho n/\ell}.
\]
Some coloring in $G$ has $|I|$ at least this expectation,
which proves the assertion.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:local-directional-rectangle}
Suppose $f$ satisfies Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-directional-bias}.
If each path of a depth-$d$ tree $T$ with $L$ leaves has a separated
partition with $|I|\ge t$ and $|J|\ge k$, then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f,T)^2
 \le L(2^{-t}+2\varepsilon)
 \le2^d(2^{-t}+2\varepsilon).
 \label{eq:local-directional-correlation}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Fix a leaf and a slice $x_S=s$, with rectangle $A\times B$ of
densities $\alpha,\beta$. Write $\phi(u,v)=(-1)^{f(u,v,s)}$.
For distinct $u,u'$, the source $(u,U_J,s)$ has dimension
$|J|\ge k$, and translation by $(u+u',0_J,0_S)$ is nonzero.
Thus Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-directional-bias} gives
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_v\phi(u,v)\phi(u',v)\right|\le2\varepsilon.
\]
Put $R(v)=\mathbf{E}_u\mathbf1_A(u)\phi(u,v)$.
Expanding the second moment, separating equal and unequal rows, gives
\[
 \mathbf{E}_vR(v)^2
 \le\alpha2^{-|I|}+2\varepsilon\alpha^2
 \le\alpha(2^{-t}+2\varepsilon).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz therefore bounds the signed contribution of this
rectangle by
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_v\mathbf1_B(v)R(v)\right|
 \le\sqrt{\alpha\beta(2^{-t}+2\varepsilon)}.
\]
Average over $s$ and apply Cauchy--Schwarz again: a leaf of probability
$p_\tau$ contributes at most
$\sqrt{p_\tau(2^{-t}+2\varepsilon)}$.
Finally, $\sum_\tau\sqrt{p_\tau}\le\sqrt L$.
The derivative bound is used on the full $J$-cube before restriction
to $B$, so we do not need to assume that the conditional distribution
on the leaf is an affine source.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- theorem-26: body_md -->
\label{thm:local-directional-logarithmic}
Fix $0<\rho<1/2$ and $a>0$.
Suppose $f_n$ satisfies Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-directional-bias} with
$k=\lceil\rho n\rceil$ and $\varepsilon\le2^{-an}$.
There is $C_\rho>0$ such that, whenever
$\ell\to\infty$ and $\ell\le n/(C_\rho\log n)$, every
non-oblivious $\ell$-local tree of depth
\begin{equation}
 d\le\left\lfloor\frac{n}{4\ell}
                  \frac{\log\ell}{\log\log\ell}\right\rfloor
 \label{eq:local-directional-depth}
\end{equation}
has correlation at most $2^{-\Omega_{\rho,a}(n/\sqrt\ell)}$ with $f_n$.
Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{LDT}_{\ell}(f_n)
 =\Omega_{\rho,a}\left(\frac n\ell
                         \frac{\log\ell}{\log\log\ell}\right).
\]
<!-- end theorem-26 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
For the parameters of \Cref{lem:local-asymmetric-separator},
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-directional-depth} gives
\[
 \lambda\le1+\frac{\log\ell}{4\log\log\ell},
 \qquad
 \lambda\log(4\lambda/a_\rho)\le\tfrac12\log\ell
\]
for all sufficiently large $\ell$. Hence $p^\lambda\ge\ell^{-1/2}$.
Choose $C_\rho$ large enough that
$ne^{-\kappa_\rho n/\ell}\le n^{-4}$ in the stated range.
Every leaf path then has a separated partition with
\[
 |I|\ge t\ge(1-o(1))n/\sqrt\ell,
 \qquad |J|\ge(1+\rho)n/2\ge\lceil\rho n\rceil.
\]
Since $d=o(n/\sqrt\ell)$ and $\varepsilon\le2^{-an}$,
\Cref{lem:local-directional-rectangle} gives
$\operatorname{Corr}(f_n,T)^2
\le2^d(2^{-t}+2\varepsilon)=2^{-\Omega_{\rho,a}(n/\sqrt\ell)}$.
Taking square roots proves the correlation bound; exact computation
would have correlation one.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
\label{cor:local-anm-logarithmic}
Let $F_n:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a non-malleable affine extractor at
entropy $\lceil\rho n\rceil$ and error at most $2^{-an}$, for fixed
$0<\rho<1/2$ and $a>0$.
Every nonzero output parity $\langle u,F_n\rangle$ satisfies the
correlation and depth bounds of \Cref{thm:local-directional-logarithmic}.
Only single-tampering non-malleability is needed.
<!-- end corollary-12 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
For every nonzero $c$, the affine map $x\mapsto x+c$ has no fixed
points. Non-malleability, followed by the character
$(z,z')\mapsto(-1)^{\langle u,z+z'\rangle}$, gives
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:local-directional-bias} with error $\varepsilon$.
Apply \Cref{thm:local-directional-logarithmic}.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- corollary-13: body_md -->
\label{local:optimized-condenser}
For the constants $C'>C>1$ above, suppose
$\ell\log^{C-1}n=o(n)$. There is a polynomial-time computable
function $F:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ with
\begin{equation}
 m=O\!\left(
 \ell\log^{C-1}n\log\frac{en}{\ell\log^{C-1}n}
 +\log^{C'}n\right)=o(n)
 \label{local:optimized-output}
\end{equation}
such that every oblivious $\ell$-local decision tree computing
$F$ has depth at least $n-2m+1$.
<!-- end corollary-13 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Put $P=\lceil\log^{C-1}n\rceil$ and
$\Delta=\lceil\log^{C'}n\rceil$. Choose the remaining parameters in order:
\begin{itemize}
\item Set $\alpha=\lceil4\ell P\rceil$ and define
\[
 R=\alpha\left(\log\frac n\alpha+3\right).
\]
\item Set the output length to $m=\lceil4(R+\Delta)\rceil$.
\item Set $d=n-2m$.
\end{itemize}
These parameters satisfy $\alpha=o(n)$, $m=o(n)$ and
$d\ge n/2$ for sufficiently large $n$. In particular,
$2\ell d/n\le\alpha\le d$ and $m\le n$.
The concentration theorem~\cite[Theorem~5.2]{GG26} applies to
source entropies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 k_1&=n-d=2m,\\
 k_2&=\frac{\alpha n}{2d\ell}
                  \log\frac{2d\ell}{\alpha},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and requires output entropy at least
$\alpha(\log(d/\alpha)+3)$. Since
$4\ell P\le\alpha\le5\ell P$, we have
\[
 k_2\ge2P\log\frac n{5P}\ge\lceil\log^C n\rceil
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$. We therefore use the condenser
above with second-source threshold $\lceil\log^C n\rceil$,
first-source threshold $2m$, and $\delta=1/2$. Its output entropy
is at least
\[
 m-\Delta\ge R\ge\alpha\left(\log\frac d\alpha+3\right),
\]
and its error is below $1/2$. Theorem~5.2 of~\cite{GG26} gives
depth at least $d+1$. The stated bound on $m$ follows from the
choice of $\alpha$.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- theorem-27: body_md -->
\label{thm:deterministic-lossless}
For every fixed $0<\xi<1$, there is a deterministic polynomial-time
construction of an infinite family of unsatisfiable CNFs on $N$
Boolean variables, with polynomially many clauses of width
$O_\xi(\log N)$, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ refutation has width at least
$(1-\xi)N$;
\item every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ refutation of resolution depth
at most $N$ has size at least $2^{(1-\xi)N}$.
\end{itemize}
The polynomial bounds may depend on the fixed $\xi$.
<!-- end theorem-27 -->
<!-- theorem-28: body_md -->
\label{thm:deterministic-gadgets}
Fix a rational $0<\eta\le1$ and an integer $a\ge1$. There are integers
$C,C_0\ge1$ and a uniform deterministic algorithm with the following
property. Given $r\ge1$, set $\ell=C\lceil\log r\rceil+C_0$.
The algorithm constructs functions $g_i:\mathsf{F}_2^\ell\to\mathsf{F}_2^a$ for
$i\in[r]$ in total time $r^{O_{\eta,a}(1)}$, with total truth-table
size $r^{O_{\eta,a}(1)}$. For every affine source
$X=(X_1,\ldots,X_r)$ satisfying
$H_\infty(X_I)\ge\eta\ell|I|$ for every $I\subseteq[r]$,
\[
 \{(g_1(x_1),\ldots,g_r(x_r)):x\in\mathsf{Supp}(X)\}=(\mathsf{F}_2^a)^r.
\]
One family satisfies this conclusion simultaneously for all such sources.
<!-- end theorem-28 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
Fix the constants $\alpha,\beta,H,Q,\ell_0$ from
\Cref{thm:universal-certificate}, decreasing $\beta$ if necessary so
that $\beta\le1$. Apply \Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple} with entropy rate
$\sigma=\beta/2$ and comparison count
$h=\max\{1,H2^Q-1\}$. Let $\mathsf{anmExt}_L$ denote this extractor on $L$-bit inputs, with error at most
$2^{-eL}$ for a fixed $e>0$ and all sufficiently large $L$.

Put $t=\lceil\log r\rceil$, assign distinct constants
$c_i\in\mathsf{F}_2^t$, and set $L=\ell+t$. Define
\begin{equation}
 g_i(x)=\operatorname{prefix}_a\bigl(\mathsf{anmExt}_L(c_i\circ x)\bigr).
 \label{eq:deterministic-tagged-gadgets}
\end{equation}
Choose $C\ge1$ and $C_0\ge\ell_0$ sufficiently large that $L\le2\ell$ and
$\mathsf{anmExt}_L$ has at least $a$ output bits. The tags carry no entropy and
introduce no variables.

Let $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\in(\mathsf{F}_2^a)^r$ be nonzero, and put
$S=\{i:v_i\ne0\}$. Rank spread is inherited when we keep only the
blocks indexed by $S$.
\Cref{thm:universal-certificate} therefore supplies a certificate
on these original blocks with at least $\alpha|S|$ honest blocks,
cluster size at most $H$, and at most $Q$ outside classes. Set
$k=\lceil\beta\ell\rceil$ and $k'=\beta\ell$. The private ranks,
being integers, are at least $k$; the joint-rank threshold $k'$ need
not be an integer. Every honest input to $\mathsf{anmExt}_L$ has entropy at least
$\beta\ell\ge\sigma L$ after the fixings in the cluster argument.
Set $\gamma=\alpha\min\{e,\beta\}/2^{Q+1}$.
\Cref{thm:lossless-cluster-phase}, applied to the nonzero characters
$v_i\cdot g_i$, gives
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{\sum_i v_i\cdot g_i(X_i)}\right|
 \le 2^{-\gamma\ell|S|},
 \label{eq:deterministic-phase-decay}
\end{equation}
provided $C_0$ is sufficiently large. Indeed, the quantity inside the
parentheses in Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-product} is at most
$2^{-\min\{e,\beta\}\ell/2}$. Coincident comparison inputs are
allowed by \Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple}; distinct tags separate
original blocks, but do not separate the corners belonging to the
same block.

There are $\binom r s(2^a-1)^s$ characters with support size $s$.
The sum of the absolute values of all nontrivial Fourier coefficients
is consequently at most
\begin{equation}
 \bigl(1+(2^a-1)2^{-\gamma\ell}\bigr)^r-1.
 \label{eq:deterministic-fourier-sum}
\end{equation}
Take $C\ge\max\{1,1/\gamma\}$ and enlarge $C_0$ so that
$\gamma C_0\ge\log(4(2^a-1))$. Then
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:deterministic-fourier-sum} is at most
$\exp(1/4)-1<1$. Fourier inversion gives positive probability to
every target in $(\mathsf{F}_2^a)^r$.

All parameters were fixed in the order
$\eta,a$; the certificate constants; the extractor constants;
and finally $C,C_0$. Evaluation of $\mathsf{anmExt}_L$ is uniformly polynomial in
$L$, with constants depending only on the fixed parameters. Evaluating
it on every tagged input takes $r2^\ell\mathsf{poly}(L)=r^{O_{\eta,a}(1)}$
time.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
Fix positive rationals $\varepsilon=\delta_0<\xi/16$. Use
\Cref{formula:sparse-base} at $\delta=\delta_0/2$, obtaining $Q=2^a$
and row width $s$. Apply \Cref{thm:deterministic-gadgets} with
$\eta=\varepsilon/2$ and output length $a$, and take
\begin{itemize}
\item block length $\ell=C\lceil\log_2r\rceil+C_0$;
\item legal-family capacity $w=\lfloor(1-\delta_0)r\rfloor$;
\item safeness parameter $k=\lfloor(1-\varepsilon/2)\ell\rfloor$;
\item initial variable count $N_0=r\ell$;
\item rank threshold $K_0=kw$;
\item path parameter $b_0=\lceil2(\varepsilon+\delta_0)N_0\rceil$.
\end{itemize}
For large $r$, $w<\gamma=\lceil(1-\delta_0/2)r\rceil$ and
$\varepsilon\ell/2\le\ell-k\le\varepsilon\ell$. Thus the gadgets
are surjective on safe systems and
\begin{equation}\label{formula:rank-threshold}
 K_0\ge(1-\varepsilon-\delta_0)N_0-O(\ell).
\end{equation}
By \Cref{formula:lifting}, the size exponent is at least
\begin{equation}\label{formula:final-exponent}
 K_0-b_0-(\ell-k)w
 \ge(1-4\varepsilon-3\delta_0)N_0-O(\ell)
 \ge(1-\xi)N_0.
\end{equation}
The last inequality holds eventually by the fixed slack in our choices.
Also $K_0+b_0>N_0$, so every depth-at-most-$N_0$ refutation is
$(K_0,b_0)$-path-free. The width bound follows from
Eqn.~\eqref{formula:rank-threshold}.

Enumerating violating raw tuples gives at most
$(r+1)2^{s\ell}=r^{O_\xi(1)}$ clauses, each of width
$s\ell=O_\xi(\log r)$, in deterministic polynomial time. Tags, field
symbols, and code coordinates introduce no Boolean variables.
If some designated raw variables never occur, omit them and write
$N\le N_0$ for the actual count. Both lower bounds remain valid with
$N$, and depth at most $N$ is covered. Since every CNF has a resolution
refutation of width at most its variable count, the width bound also
implies $N\ge(1-\xi)N_0$ eventually. Thus $\log r=\Theta(\log N)$,
completing the construction with its actual variable count.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-restricted-gadget}
Fix any incident blocks of a gadget, leaving at least $d_0$ blocks free.
Write $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^t$ for one free block and $v$ for the others.
For all real functions $a,b$ bounded in absolute value by one,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{u,v}h_i(u,v)a(u)b(v)\right|\le\delta.
 \label{eq:overlap-restricted-product}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
For distinct $u,u'$, the sections obtained by varying $v$ are parallel
affine spaces of dimension at least $(d_0-1)t\ge k$. Their displacement
is nonzero because $A_i$ is invertible. Hence
$|\mathbf{E}_v h_i(u,v)h_i(u',v)|\le2\varepsilon$; for $u=u'$ the
expectation is one. Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_v b(v)\mathbf{E}_u h_i(u,v)a(u)\right|^2
 \le \mathbf{E}_{u,u'}
       \left|\mathbf{E}_v h_i(u,v)h_i(u',v)\right|
 \le 2\varepsilon+2^{-t}.
\]
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-twisted-moments}
Fix any raw blocks. Let $I$ be a set of vertices each retaining at least
$d_0$ free incident blocks. For $S\subseteq I$ and any linear character
$\chi_a$ on the remaining raw variables,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}\chi_a(Z)\prod_{i\in S}h_i(Z)\right|
 \le\delta^{|S|/B}.
 \label{eq:overlap-twisted-moment-bound}
\end{equation}
The expectation is zero if $a$ is nonzero on a free block not incident
to any vertex of $S$.
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
Choose a maximal subset of $S$ whose distinct vertices have graph distance
at least three. Each chosen vertex excludes at most $B$ candidates, so
there are at least $|S|/B$ chosen vertices. Fix all free blocks not
incident to a chosen vertex. The remaining sets of blocks at the chosen
vertices are disjoint. Every unchosen gadget factor depends on at most
one remaining block: dependence on blocks at two chosen vertices would
put those vertices at distance two. The character also factors over the
remaining blocks. Thus the conditional expectation factors over the
chosen vertices, and \Cref{lem:overlap-restricted-gadget} bounds each
factor by $\delta$, absorbing the one-block factors into $a$ and $b$.
Average over the fixings. The last assertion follows by averaging a
nontrivial character on an unused block.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-safe-output-probabilities}
Suppose that, after some raw blocks are fixed, each active gadget has at
least $d_0$ free incident blocks. Let $A$ be a nonempty affine space on
the remaining variables with $\kappa$-safe equation row space. Put
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha&=2^{\kappa D}\delta^{1/B},\\
 \theta&=(1+\alpha)^m-1.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:overlap-safe-error}
\end{equation}
Every prescribed pattern on any $b$ active outputs has probability under
$U_A$ between $(1-\theta)2^{-b}$ and $(1+\theta)2^{-b}$. In particular,
if $\theta<1$, every pattern on all active outputs has a preimage in $A$.
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
Let $U$ be the equation row space, and let $\sigma(a)$ be the sign of
the consistent right-hand side for $a\in U$. Expanding the normalized
indicator of $A$ gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{E}_{Z\sim U_A}\prod_{i\in S}h_i(Z)
 =\sum_{a\in U}\sigma(a)
       \mathbf{E}_Z\chi_a(Z)\prod_{i\in S}h_i(Z).
 \label{eq:overlap-affine-fourier}
\end{equation}
Only forms supported on the at most $D|S|$ free blocks incident to $S$
contribute. Safeness bounds their number by $2^{\kappa D|S|}$, so
\Cref{lem:overlap-twisted-moments} bounds
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-affine-fourier} in absolute value by $\alpha^{|S|}$.
Fourier inversion on $b$ outputs bounds each pattern's relative deviation
from $2^{-b}$ by
\[
 \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[b]}\alpha^{|S|}
 =(1+\alpha)^b-1\le\theta.
\]
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-monotone-closure}
For every row space $U$ on all raw variables, there are a block set $C(U)$
and a vertex set $V(U)$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U\subseteq U'$ implies $C(U)\subseteq C(U')$ and
$V(U)\subseteq V(U')$.
\item Every vertex of $V(U)$ has all incident blocks in $C(U)$; every
other vertex has at least $d_0$ incident blocks outside $C(U)$.
\item The projection of $U$ outside $C(U)$ is $\kappa$-safe.
\item Writing $r=\dim U$, we have
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
