 |V(U)|&\le\frac{2r}{\kappa\gamma},\\
 |C(U)|&\le\frac r\kappa\left(1+\frac{2D}{\gamma}\right).
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:overlap-closure-size}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
Define the supermodular function
\[
 q_U(S)=\dim(U\cap W_S)-\kappa|S|.
\]
Supermodularity means that
$q_U(S)+q_U(T)\le q_U(S\cup T)+q_U(S\cap T)$.
Indeed, the intersection of $U\cap W_S$ and $U\cap W_T$ is
$U\cap W_{S\cap T}$, while their sum is contained in $U\cap W_{S\cup T}$.
Let $R_U(S)$ be the union of all sets $T\supseteq S$ maximizing
$q_U(T)$. The union of two maximizers is a maximizer, so $R_U(S)$
is the unique largest maximizer under set inclusion.
Supermodularity makes $R_U$ extensive and monotone in $S$.

It is also monotone in $U$. For $U\subseteq U'$, the difference
\[
 \dim(U'\cap W_T)-\dim(U\cap W_T)
\]
is nondecreasing in $T$, since it is the dimension of the image of
$U'\cap W_T$ in $U'/U$. If $T$ and $T'$ are the old and new largest
maximizers, these increasing differences and supermodularity imply
$q_{U'}(T\cup T')\ge q_{U'}(T')$. Since $T'$ contains every superset of $S$
maximizing $q_{U'}$, it contains $T\cup T'$, giving $T\subseteq T'$.
The same union argument applies when
the forced set increases.

Starting with no blocks, alternate $R_U$ with the following peeling
operation: whenever a vertex has fewer than $d_0$ incident blocks outside
the current set, adjoin all its incident blocks. Iterate to a common
fixed point $C(U)$, and let $V(U)$ consist of the vertices whose incident
blocks all lie in $C(U)$. Both operations are extensive and monotone,
which proves the first two assertions. For $C=C(U)$ and $T$ outside $C$,
\[
 \dim(\pi_{\overline C}U\cap W_T)
 =\dim(U\cap W_{C\cup T})-\dim(U\cap W_C)
 \le\kappa|T|.
\]
The equality follows by taking the preimage under projection, and the
inequality follows from $q_U(C\cup T)\le q_U(C)$.

Call a block first added by an $R_U$ operation a seed block. If such an
operation enlarges $S$ to $T$, then
\[
 \kappa|T\setminus S|
 \le\dim(U\cap W_T)-\dim(U\cap W_S).
\]
These dimension increases telescope to at most $r$, so there are at most
$r/\kappa$ seed blocks. Order the peeled vertices by when they close.
Each has at least $D-d_0+1$ previously fixed incident blocks. A seed edge
is charged at most twice. Every other edge charged in this way joins an
earlier peeled vertex to a later one and is charged at most once. If
there are $s$ seed blocks and $b=|V(U)|$ peeled vertices, there are at
most $Db/2$ such internal edges. Hence
\[
 (D-d_0+1)b\le2s+Db/2,\qquad \gamma b\le2s.
\]
Every final block is a seed or is incident to a peeled vertex. Thus
$|C(U)|\le s+Db$, proving Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-closure-size}.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-affine-invariant}
Suppose $\varphi$ has a legal family of capacity $w$ and $\theta<1$.
Set
\begin{equation}
 L=\left\lfloor\frac{\kappa\gamma w}{2}\right\rfloor.
 \label{eq:overlap-rank-threshold}
\end{equation}
An adversary can consistently answer parity queries and forget equations
as long as the stored equation row space, including a newly queried pivot
before any forgetting, has rank at most $L$.
It maintains a nonempty affine set on which no initial clause of
$\varphi\circ_\Lambda g$ is identically false.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
For a stored row space $U$, maintain its equation values, a fixing $\zeta$
of $C(U)$, and a legal coarse assignment $\rho$ on $V(U)$. Let $A$ be
the nonempty affine space satisfying the equations and $\zeta$. The
closed gadget outputs equal $\rho$. By
\Cref{lem:overlap-safe-output-probabilities} and \Cref{lem:overlap-monotone-closure}, every assignment to the active outputs
has a preimage in $A$.

When a parity $p$ is requested, first form $U'=U+\mathsf{Span}\{p\}$,
before selecting its answer. The closures grow monotonically and
$|V(U')|\le w$. Extend $\rho$ legally to $V(U')$. Surjectivity on the
old state supplies $z\in A$ with these newly prescribed outputs. Fix the
blocks in $C(U')\setminus C(U)$ to their values in $z$, and answer with
$p(z)$. The new affine space contains $z$, has the required closed
outputs, and again every assignment to the active outputs has a preimage
in it.

If equations are forgotten, so $U'\subseteq U$, discard the block
fixings outside $C(U')$ and restrict $\rho$ to $V(U')$. The old space
witnesses nonemptiness of the relaxed one. Monotonicity and
\Cref{lem:overlap-safe-output-probabilities} restore the invariant.
This also permits replacement by a basis for any subspace of the stored
row space.

Suppose an initial substituted clause were identically false on $A$.
It is implied by a substituted base clause, which would therefore also
be false throughout $A$. If one of that base clause's variables were
active, surjectivity could satisfy its literal. All its variables must
therefore be closed, contradicting legality of $\rho$.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- corollary-14: body_md -->
\label{cor:overlap-rank-width}
Under \Cref{lem:overlap-affine-invariant}, every refutation of
$\varphi\circ_\Lambda g$ contains a clause of rank at least $L$.
<!-- end corollary-14 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
If all clauses had rank at most $L-1$, follow falsified clauses backwards
from the empty clause while storing their falsifying equations. At a
resolution, query its pivot, select a falsified premise, and forget
unnecessary equations. The stored rank, including the temporary pivot,
is at most $L$. At backwards semantic weakening, the falsifying space
of the conclusion is contained in that of the premise, so only
forgetting is needed. Reaching an initial clause contradicts
\Cref{lem:overlap-affine-invariant}.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- theorem-29: body_md -->
\label{thm:directional-overlapping-lifting}
Assume the parameters $d_0,B,\delta,\gamma$ defined above satisfy
$\gamma>0$. Choose an integer $\kappa\ge1$, put
$\theta=(1+2^{\kappa D}\delta^{1/B})^m-1$, and assume
\begin{equation}
 \theta\le\frac1{4m}.
 \label{eq:overlap-small-error}
\end{equation}
Let $\varphi$ have a legal family $\mathcal P$ of capacity $w$, and let
$L\ge1$ be as in Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-rank-threshold}. Set $\nu=w$. If
$\mathcal P$ is affine, one may instead set
\begin{equation}
 \nu=\max_{|A|\le w}\bigl(|A|-\dim\mathcal P_A\bigr).
 \label{eq:overlap-legal-codimension}
\end{equation}
Every refutation of $\varphi\circ_\Lambda g$, of size $S$ and resolution
depth $d$, satisfies $d\ge L$ and
\begin{equation}
 (2d-L)\left(\log S+\nu\log\frac2{1-\theta}\right)\ge L^2.
 \label{eq:overlap-size-depth}
\end{equation}
More precisely, set
\[
 p=\left\lfloor\log S+\nu\log\frac2{1-\theta}\right\rfloor.
\]
With $J=\lceil L/p\rceil$, one has
\begin{equation}
 d\ge JL-\frac{pJ(J-1)}2
 \ge\frac{L^2}{2p}+\frac L2.
 \label{eq:overlap-staircase-bound}
\end{equation}
In particular, $p\le\nu+\lceil\log S\rceil$. The conclusions allow
arbitrary separate invertible affine maps $A_i$.
<!-- end theorem-29 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
We first give a sampler for the invariant in
\Cref{lem:overlap-affine-invariant}. Start uniformly on a valid
affine state $A_0$, retain all additional parity equations, and stop
when their rank together with the starting query space reaches $L$.
When a query closes $b>0$ new gadgets, prescribe a legal extension by
a fixed deterministic policy. By
\Cref{lem:overlap-safe-output-probabilities}, the prescribed pattern
has probability at least $(1-\theta)2^{-b}$ in the current uniform
affine state. Condition on this pattern, and sample the newly fixed raw
blocks and the query answer from this conditional distribution. After
fixing these sampled values, the residual distribution is uniform on
the new affine state: the prescribed output pattern is determined by
the fixed blocks. If no gadget closes, sample the additional block values
and the query answer from the current distribution and condition on
these values. At most $w$ new
coarse variables are assigned, giving the following density bound for
every completed input $z$ in $A_0$:
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbf{Pr}[Z=z]}{\mathbf{Pr}_{U_{A_0}}[z]}
 \le \left(\frac2{1-\theta}\right)^w
 \label{eq:overlap-density-general}
\end{equation}
after uniform completion in the stopped state.

For an affine legal family, write $h(A)=|A|-\dim\mathcal P_A$.
If $A\subseteq A'$ and $|A'|\le w$, the extension property makes the
restriction map $\mathcal P_{A'}\to\mathcal P_A$ surjective. Over a
fixed old assignment, the legal extensions therefore form an affine
space of size
\[
 2^{|A'\setminus A|-(h(A')-h(A))}.
\]
Condition on membership in this entire space, rather than on one
extension. Its probability is at least
$(1-\theta)2^{-(h(A')-h(A))}$. If $h(A')=h(A)$, every pattern is legal,
so no conditioning is required. The positive increments of $h$ telescope
to at most $\nu$, and their number is at most their sum. The bound in
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-density-general} consequently improves to the
following bound, where $D_\nu=(2/(1-\theta))^\nu$:
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbf{Pr}[Z=z]}{\mathbf{Pr}_{U_{A_0}}[z]}\le D_\nu.
 \label{eq:overlap-density}
\end{equation}
Fixing the additional blocks to their sampled values determines the
chosen legal extension, so the residual distribution is again uniform
on the resulting affine state.

These density bounds hold for every completed input, even when the
queries depend on previous answers. The input determines every query answer, closure,
fixed block value, and coarse assignment on its stopped path. Thus it
is compatible with only one sequence of these choices. The product of
reciprocal conditioning probabilities bounds its likelihood ratio;
summing over the possible sequences introduces no additional factor.

At the beginning of phase $j$, maintain a proof node $v_j$, a query
space $U_j$ of rank $r_j$, its equation values, fixed blocks $C(U_j)$,
and a legal assignment on $V(U_j)$. Let $A_j$ be the resulting nonempty
affine state and put
\[
 W_j=U_j+W_{C(U_j)}.
\]
Require every point of $A_j$ to falsify the clause at $v_j$. Initially,
$v_0$ is the empty conclusion, $U_0=0$, and $A_0$ is the whole input
space. Its closure is empty, since $d_0\le D$ and $\kappa>0$.

Suppose $r_j<L$. Follow falsified premises backwards using the sampler
with initial distribution $U_{A_j}$. The temporary query space is
$U_j$ plus the span of pivots encountered in this phase; fixed raw
coordinates are not counted in this rank. Stop when it reaches $L$.
The invariant prevents reaching an initial clause first. Thus every
sampled path advances at least $L-r_j$ resolution steps. A pivot already
determined by fixed raw coordinates still increases query rank by at most
one and has no conditioning cost.

For a possible boundary node $v$, let $T_v$ be the row space defining
its falsifying assignments. This affine space either misses $A_j$ or
has relative uniform mass
\begin{equation}
 2^{-\dim((T_v+W_j)/W_j)}.
 \label{eq:overlap-boundary-mass}
\end{equation}
Stopping at $v$ implies membership in that space, so
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-density} bounds its sampled probability by $D_\nu$
times Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-boundary-mass}. There are at most $S$ boundary
nodes. If every positively reached one had quotient rank at least
$p+1$, their probabilities would sum to at most
$SD_\nu2^{-(p+1)}<1$. Some positively reached $v$ therefore satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \dim((T_v+W_j)/W_j)\le p.
 \label{eq:overlap-boundary-rank}
\end{equation}
Here $S\ge2$, since the invariant excludes an empty initial clause;
hence $p\ge1$.

Fix a successful path to this node and let $Q$ be the span of its
pivots. The proof rules give
\begin{equation}
 T_v\subseteq W_j+Q,
 \label{eq:overlap-query-inclusion}
\end{equation}
with the corresponding right-hand sides. Indeed, $A_j$ falsifies the
starting clause. Querying a pivot and selecting a falsified premise
adds only that pivot equation, while backwards weakening drops implied
equations. This induction does not use the temporary block fixings.

Choose $t_1,\ldots,t_h\in T_v$ representing a basis modulo $W_j$, with
$h\le p$. By Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-query-inclusion}, write
$t_i=w_i+q_i$, where $w_i\in W_j$ and $q_i\in Q$, and set
\[
 U_{j+1}=U_j+\mathsf{Span}\{q_1,\ldots,q_h\}.
\]
Then $r_{j+1}\le r_j+p$ and $U_{j+1}\subseteq U_j+Q$. Monotonicity
gives
\[
 C(U_j)\subseteq C(U_{j+1})\subseteq C(U_j+Q),
\]
and the analogous inclusions for $V$. Give the retained equations and
raw blocks their values in the successful final state, and restrict its
legal assignment to $V(U_{j+1})$. The new affine state $A_{j+1}$ contains
that final state, so it is nonempty. It retains every equation and raw
fixing of $A_j$, as well as the $q_i$ equations, and therefore implies
all falsifying equations in $T_v$. Restart at $v_{j+1}=v$ uniformly on
$A_{j+1}$.

The density losses are not multiplied across phases. Each phase proves
the existence of a path segment and a valid next state, after which the
distribution is reset. The segments concatenate to a syntactic path in
the proof DAG; a single input need not realize the entire concatenation.

Since $r_j\le jp$, we may run $J=\lceil L/p\rceil$ phases. Their
total length is at least
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}(L-jp)=JL-\frac{pJ(J-1)}2
 \ge\frac{L^2}{2p}+\frac L2.
\]
The first phase also gives $d\ge L$. Since
$p\le\log S+\log D_\nu$, this proves
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-size-depth}. Finally,
\[
 \nu\log\frac1{1-\theta}
 \le m\log\frac1{1-1/(4m)}<1,
\]
so $p\le\nu+\lceil\log S\rceil$.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-tseitin-legal}
Let $G$ be a constant-degree graph on $v$ vertices with edge expansion
at least $h>0$: every vertex set of size at most $v/2$ has at least $h$
times its size edges leaving it. The CNF encoding an odd-charge Tseitin
system on $G$ has constant width and an affine legal family of capacity
$w=\lfloor hv/8\rfloor\ge1$. For a domain $A$ of assigned edges, $|A|\le w$,
the legal space has codimension
\begin{equation}
 c_G(A)=\#\operatorname{components}(G\setminus A)-1.
 \label{eq:overlap-tseitin-codimension}
\end{equation}
In particular, $w=\Omega(m)$ for $m=|E(G)|$, and the affine version of
\Cref{thm:directional-overlapping-lifting} applies with
\begin{equation}
 H_G(w)=\max_{|A|\le w}c_G(A).
 \label{eq:overlap-tseitin-cost}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
After at most $w$ edges are assigned, the unassigned graph has a unique
component with more than $v/2$ vertices. Otherwise a union of its
components has between $v/4$ and $v/2$ vertices, and its boundary has at
least $hv/4>w$ assigned edges. Uniqueness is immediate. Call this
component large. Move assigned edge values into the charges of their
endpoints. Declare an assignment legal if every component other than
the large one has even total residual charge. The total charge remains
odd, so the large component has odd residual charge.

The empty assignment is legal. Unassigning edges merges components and
preserves the residual charge of their union, proving restriction
closure. To assign an edge while fewer than $w$ are assigned, remove it
from its component. If the component stays connected, either value
preserves its total charge. If a small component splits, choose the edge
value making one new component even; the other is then even. If the
large component splits, one resulting component is still large, and
choose the edge value making the other even. A completely assigned
vertex is a singleton small component and has even residual charge, so
its constraint is satisfied. No legal assignment falsifies an initial
Tseitin clause.

For fixed $A$, the small-component conditions are affine equations in
the assigned edge values. Contract the components of $G\setminus A$.
The resulting multigraph of assigned edges is connected. Its incidence
rows indexed by all vertices except the large component are independent,
so the equations have rank $c_G(A)$. They are consistent because the
matrix has full row rank. This proves
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-tseitin-codimension}.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- corollary-15: body_md -->
\label{cor:overlap-explicit-lower-bounds}
There is a deterministic polynomial-time constructible family of
polynomial-size unsatisfiable CNFs $\Phi_N$ on $N$ variables and of width
$O(\log N)$ such that every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ refutation,
of size $S$ and resolution depth $d$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 d\bigl(\log S+O(N/\log N)\bigr)=\Omega(N^2).
 \label{eq:overlap-explicit-tradeoff}
\end{equation}
For every fixed $a>0$, refutations of depth at most $aN$ therefore have
size $2^{\Omega_a(N)}$. This includes top-regular refutations, whose
pivot forms are linearly independent along each path and whose depth
is consequently at most $N$.
<!-- end corollary-15 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
Take an explicit constant-degree expander family and its odd-charge
Tseitin formulas. \Cref{lem:overlap-tseitin-legal} gives legal
capacity $w=\Omega(m)$. Add at most four unused coarse variables so
that $m$ is divisible by five; extend the legal family by arbitrary
values on them, while retaining capacity $w$. Use a disjoint union of
$K_5$ graphs as the coupling graph. Then $D=4$ and $B=5$.

Set $t=C_0\lceil\log m\rceil$ and use the first output bit of the
directional affine extractor of Li and Zhong~\cite{LZdir} on $4t$ bits
at entropy threshold $k=t$. It has error $\varepsilon=2^{-\Omega(t)}$.
Thus $d_0=2$, $\gamma=1$, and $\delta\le2^{-\beta t}$ for a constant
$\beta>0$ and sufficiently large $t$. Take
$\kappa=\lfloor\beta t/40\rfloor$. Then
\[
 \alpha=2^{4\kappa}\delta^{1/5}\le2^{-\beta t/10}.
\]
Choosing $C_0$ sufficiently large makes $\alpha\le1/(8m^2)$ and hence
$\theta\le1/(4m)$. We have $\kappa=\Omega(t)$,
$N=2mt$, and $L=\lfloor\kappa w/2\rfloor=\Omega(N)$.
\Cref{thm:directional-overlapping-lifting}, with
$\nu=H_G(w)=O(m)$, proves Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-explicit-tradeoff}.

If the base width is $b_0$, every substituted clause depends on at most
$4b_0t=O(\log m)$ raw bits. Its truth table and canonical CNF can thus
be generated in polynomial time. The closure and sampler are used only
in the lower-bound proof and need not be computed by the construction.
Arbitrary specified invertible affine maps at the gadget locations are
permitted by \Cref{thm:directional-overlapping-lifting}.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:overlap-quadratic-gadget}
Without separate affine changes of coordinates,
\Cref{lem:overlap-restricted-gadget} also follows from
\[
 g(z_1,\ldots,z_D)
 =\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathsf{F}_{2^t}/\mathsf{F}_2}
       \left(\sum_{a<b}z_a z_b\right).
\]
After any fixing leaving two blocks free, distinct sections in one free
block have zero correlation: their product contains a nontrivial
character of a second free block. Cauchy--Schwarz gives
$\delta=2^{-t/2}$. Directional affine extractors supply robustness under
unrelated local affine maps, which need not arise from one global affine
change of the overlapping raw variables.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- theorem-30: body_md -->
\label{thm:overlap-tagged-matching}
Fix any raw blocks, and call a vertex active if it has at least one free
incident block. For a set $S$ of active vertices and any linear character
$\chi_b$ of the remaining raw variables,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}\chi_b(Z)\prod_{i\in S}h_i(Z)\right|
 \le(2\varepsilon)^{|S|/(D+1)}.
 \label{eq:overlap-tagged-moment}
\end{equation}
More precisely, the exponent may be the size of a maximum matching in the
graph of free edges incident to $S$. The expectation vanishes if $b$ is
nonzero on a free block not incident to $S$.
<!-- end theorem-30 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
Let $H$ be the graph consisting of the free edges incident to $S$ and all
their endpoints. It has maximum degree at most $D$, no isolated vertices,
and at least $|S|$ vertices. A maximum matching $M$ has
$|M|\ge |V(H)|/(D+1)$. For $D=1$ this is immediate. For $D\ge2$, the
unmatched vertices are independent. If both endpoints of a matched edge
had distinct unmatched neighbors, the resulting length-three alternating
path would augment $M$. Thus each matched edge has at most $D-1$
distinct unmatched neighbors: at most one if both endpoints have such a
neighbor, and at most $D-1$ if only one does. Assign each unmatched
vertex to a neighboring matched edge. Then
$|V(H)|-2|M|\le(D-1)|M|$, proving the bound.

Fix all free blocks outside $M$. Every selected gadget now depends on
at most one remaining block. Each matching block occurs in one or two
selected gadgets, and the character factors over matching blocks, so
the conditional expectation factors over these edges.

For a matching block $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^t$ appearing in one selected
gadget, the input to $F$, including its tag, is an injective affine
function of $u$. If its
character is nontrivial, condition on that character's value; each
fiber has dimension $t-1\ge K$. The affine extractor guarantee bounds its sign
expectation on each fiber by $2\varepsilon$, and hence gives the same
bound after inserting the character. For a trivial character, apply
the affine extractor guarantee without conditioning.

If both endpoints $i,j$ are selected, their inputs without the tags are
injective affine maps $p_i(u),p_j(u)$ into $\mathsf{F}_2^{Dt}$. The affine
isomorphism $p_i(u)\mapsto p_j(u)$ extends to an invertible affine map
$A$ of $\mathsf{F}_2^{Dt}$ by extending bases. Therefore
\[
 T(c,x)=(c+c_i+c_j,A(x))
\]
is an invertible affine map taking the first tagged input to the second.
It is globally fixed-point-free because $c_i\ne c_j$. After conditioning
on the character if necessary, the first tagged input is still an affine
source of dimension at least $t-1\ge K$. Non-malleability bounds the product of the two output
signs by $2\varepsilon$ on each fiber, and thus also after inserting
the character. Multiplying over matching edges and averaging the fixed
blocks proves Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-tagged-moment}. The vanishing statement
follows by averaging a character on an unused block.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- corollary-16: body_md -->
\label{cor:overlap-tagged-lifting}
Let the base formula have a legal family of capacity $w$. For an
integer $\kappa\ge1$, define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha&=2^{\kappa D}(2\varepsilon)^{1/(D+1)},\\
 \theta&=(1+\alpha)^m-1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Suppose
\begin{equation}
 \theta\le\frac1{4m}.
 \label{eq:overlap-tagged-error}
\end{equation}
Put $L_{\mathrm{tag}}=\lfloor\kappa Dw/2\rfloor$ and assume
$L_{\mathrm{tag}}\ge1$. Every refutation
of the tagged substitution, of size $S$ and resolution depth $d$,
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 (2d-L_{\mathrm{tag}})
 \left(\log S+\nu\log\frac2{1-\theta}\right)
 \ge L_{\mathrm{tag}}^2,
 \label{eq:overlap-tagged-tradeoff}
\end{equation}
where $\nu=w$, or the value in
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-legal-codimension} for an affine legal family. The
exact bound Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-staircase-bound} also holds with
$L_{\mathrm{tag}}$ in place of $L$. The coupling graph may have any
fixed degree $D\ge1$.
<!-- end corollary-16 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
For safe equation spaces, insert
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-tagged-moment} into
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-affine-fourier}. This gives
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-tagged-error} and the same probability bound for
every prescribed output pattern. For arbitrary row spaces, let $C(U)$ be
the union of all sets $C$ maximizing
$\dim(U\cap W_C)-\kappa|C|$. The proof of
\Cref{lem:overlap-monotone-closure} gives monotonicity and safeness
outside $C(U)$. No peeling is needed: every vertex outside $V(U)$, the
set of fully fixed vertices, retains a free block. Since the maximum
is nonnegative,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 |C(U)|&\le\frac{\dim U}{\kappa},\\
 D|V(U)|&\le2|C(U)|,\\
 |V(U)|&\le\frac{2\dim U}{\kappa D}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:overlap-tagged-closure}
\end{equation}
Thus the extension and forgetting invariant holds through rank
$L_{\mathrm{tag}}$. The density and restart argument of
\Cref{thm:directional-overlapping-lifting} uses only this invariant,
monotonicity, and the bound for every output pattern, so it applies
unchanged.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:overlap-nonmalleability-scope}
The matching bound leaves only one free block per active gadget and
removes peeling from the closure. It holds under arbitrary unrelated
affine maps $A_i$. The denominator $D+1$ is sharp for the bound obtained by counting matching edges:
if only the edges of one star are free and $S$ contains its
center and all $D$ neighbors, then $|S|=D+1$ and the maximum matching
has size one.

Directional affine extractors also give this matching bound when each
shared block is inserted unchanged at the same block position in both
endpoint inputs. The resulting affine sections are parallel, and distinct
tags make their displacement nonzero. If the graph admits a proper
$D$-edge-coloring, use the edge color to choose the block position.
For a general simple $D$-regular graph, a $(D+1)$-edge-coloring gives
$D+1$ positions, with the unused position fixed at each vertex; adjust
the extractor input length accordingly. Full affine non-malleability
allows unrelated local affine changes of coordinates.

The refinement for affine families of legal assignments charges the
codimension of legal extensions
rather than the number of newly assigned coarse variables. Even perfectly
uniform outputs assign a codimension-$h$ affine fiber probability $2^{-h}$.
Thus reducing extractor error alone does not remove this conditioning
cost. The matching decomposition and safeness establish the displayed
global moments for the overlapping construction; they do not establish
non-malleability for arbitrary multipoint affine configurations or
simultaneous surjectivity of the entire gadget family on every safe
affine space, as required for lossless lifting.
We establish that property separately in
\Cref{thm:deterministic-gadgets} using the rank certificates of
\Cref{def:lossless-certificate}.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-joint-table}
Let $F$ be one output bit of the extractor in
\Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple}, with $h=q-1$ and error $\varepsilon$.
Suppose that $(X^1,\ldots,X^q)$ is jointly affine, each source meets
the extractor's entropy threshold, and no two sources take the same
value in any outcome.
For every $b\in\mathsf{F}_2^q$,
\[
 \mathbf{Pr}[(F(X^1),\ldots,F(X^q))=b]
 \ge 2^{-q}\bigl(1-2\varepsilon(2^q-1)\bigr).
\]
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
For each nonempty $T\subseteq[q]$, choose one $j\in T$ and apply
the tuple theorem with $X^j$ as the original source. It bounds
$|\mathbf{E}(-1)^{\sum_{i\in T}F(X^i)}|$ by $2\varepsilon$, since replacing
the output bit $F(X^j)$ by an independent uniform bit makes the expectation
zero. Fourier inversion proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-block-length}
There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that the preceding construction
can be instantiated with $6\le t=t(D)\le2^{CD}$.
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Apply \Cref{cor:affine-error-tuning} with the preceding $h$ and $\rho$,
input length $n_0=1+Dt$, one output bit, and
\[
 E=\max\{132,\lceil\log_2 n_0\rceil\}.
\]
Its sufficient length condition is $G_{\rho,127}(1+E)\le n_0$,
where $G_{\rho,127}\le2^{C_0D}$ for an absolute $C_0$; this includes
the minimum lengths of the constituent extractors. Taking
$t=2^{\lceil C_1D\rceil}$ for a sufficiently large absolute $C_1$
satisfies this condition, since $E=O(C_1D+\log D+132)$.
The resulting error is at most $2^{-132}$, and the entropy threshold
$\rho n_0=t/2+1/(2D)$ is at most $t$. Enlarging one absolute constant
gives the stated bound.
<!-- end proof-79 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:overlap-majority-restriction}
There is a restriction of $\varphi\circ_\Lambda g$, followed by
negations of free variables, whose remaining axioms are weakenings
of canonical axioms of $\varphi\circ\operatorname{MAJ}_3$.
The majority gadgets have pairwise disjoint inputs. The restriction
is computable in time polynomial in $m$.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-80: body_md -->
Fix every nonmatching block to zero. On a matched edge $\{i,j\}$,
the endpoint inputs without their tags become injective affine maps
$p_i,p_j:\mathsf{F}_2^t\to\mathsf{F}_2^{Dt}$. Let $U$ be the span of the first six
coordinate vectors. For uniform $X\in\mathsf{F}_2^t$, consider the 128 affine
sources
\[
 (c_i,p_i(X+u)),\quad(c_j,p_j(X+u)),\qquad u\in U.
\]
They are jointly affine and have entropy $t$. Injectivity separates
different corners at one endpoint; the tags separate the endpoints.
By \Cref{lem:overlap-joint-table}, every assignment to their 128 output
bits has positive probability. Indeed, the parenthesized factor in that lemma exceeds
$7/8$ under Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-majority-parameters}. Prescribe
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F(c_i,p_i(X+u))&=\operatorname{MAJ}_3(u_1,u_2,u_3),\\
 F(c_j,p_j(X+u))&=\operatorname{MAJ}_3(u_4,u_5,u_6).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Choose an offset $x_e$ realizing these prescribed outputs. Fix coordinates outside
$U$ to those of $x_e$ and negate free coordinate $a$ when
$(x_e)_a=1$. The endpoints become majority functions on disjoint
triples. Apply this independently on each matched edge.

For a base clause $C$, a surviving truth-table axiom excludes a
falsifying assignment on all remaining raw coordinates incident to
$C$. Its literals on the majority inputs of variables in $C$ form
a canonical axiom of $C\circ\operatorname{MAJ}_3$. Any additional
literals lie on the triple of a matched partner outside $C$.
The surviving axiom is therefore a weakening of the canonical one.
Finally, exhaustive search over the $2^t$ offsets per matched edge
is polynomial time because $t$ is fixed.
<!-- end proof-80 -->
<!-- theorem-31: body_md -->
\label{thm:overlap-ips-transfer}
Suppose every ordinary-resolution refutation of $\varphi$ has width
at least $w$ or depth at least $H$. Every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$
refutation of the preceding $\varphi\circ_\Lambda g$, of size $S$
and resolution depth $d$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 d=\Omega\!\left(\min\left\{H,
                      \frac{w^2}{\log(2S)}\right\}\right).
 \label{eq:overlap-ips-tradeoff}
\end{equation}
If $\varphi$ has polynomially many clauses of width $O(\log m)$,
the substituted CNF is constructible in polynomial time and has
polynomial size.
<!-- end theorem-31 -->
<!-- proof-81: body_md -->
Use the parity-decision-DAG formulation of
\cite[Sections~2.5 and~6]{IPS26}. Restriction and variable negation
do not increase size or depth. At each surviving leaf, replace its
weakened axiom by the canonical majority axiom from
\Cref{lem:overlap-majority-restriction}; an assignment falsifying the
former also falsifies the latter. This gives a parity decision DAG
for the clause-search problem of
$\varphi\circ\operatorname{MAJ}_3$ with the same bounds.
Three-bit majority is 1-stifling: after any one input is left free,
fixing the other two inputs to a desired bit forces that output.
Thus
\cite[Theorem~6.1]{IPS26} gives Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-ips-tradeoff}.
Its implied constant is absolute, since the restricted gadget is always
$\operatorname{MAJ}_3$.
Each base clause involves $O(Dt\log m)=O(\log m)$ raw variables,
which proves the construction and size assertions.
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- corollary-17: body_md -->
\label{cor:overlap-quantitative-product}
For the condensed bases in \Cref{quad:main}, the preceding construction
gives, for every fixed $D\ge1$, polynomial-size CNFs with polynomial-size
ordinary-resolution proofs such that every
$\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ refutation satisfies
\begin{equation}
 d\log_2(2S)\ge2^{-CD}N^2
 \label{eq:overlap-ips-product}
\end{equation}
for an absolute constant $C>0$. Here $N=mDt/2$ counts all raw variables.
<!-- end corollary-17 -->
<!-- proof-82: body_md -->
The bases have $m=\Theta(b)$ and width--depth thresholds
$(\Theta(b),\Theta(b^2))$, with absolute constants. Thus
\Cref{thm:overlap-ips-transfer} gives $d\log_2(2S)\ge c m^2$ for an
absolute $c>0$. Substituting $m=2N/(Dt)$ and using
\Cref{lem:overlap-block-length} proves Eqn.~\eqref{eq:overlap-ips-product}.
The bases have polynomial-size ordinary-resolution proofs of line width
$O(\log b)$. Such proofs remain polynomial
after our substitution: each inference involves $O(\log b)$ raw
variables and hence admits a polynomial-size exhaustive resolution
derivation of its encoded implication. A sharing graph can be formed
from $D$ cyclically shifted perfect matchings between two equal
parts; if necessary, first add a variable constrained by a unit
clause to make $m$ even.
<!-- end proof-82 -->
<!-- theorem-32: body_md -->
\label{quad:main}
There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and a deterministic algorithm
which, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, constructs an
unsatisfiable CNF $\Psi_N$ on exactly $N$ variables in time $N^C$.
The formula has at most $N^C$ clauses and an ordinary-resolution
refutation of size at most $N^C$. Every $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$
refutation of $\Psi_N$ of size $S$ and depth $d$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{quad:product}
 d\log_2(2S)\ge cN^2.
\end{equation}
Every variable introduced by the construction or by padding is
included in $N$.
<!-- end theorem-32 -->
<!-- corollary-18: body_md -->
\label{quad:simulation}
If $d(N)=o(N^2/\log N)$, depth-$d(N)$
$\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ does not polynomially simulate ordinary
resolution.
<!-- end corollary-18 -->
<!-- proof-83: body_md -->
On the family in \Cref{quad:main}, this depth bound forces
$\log(2S)=\omega(\log N)$.
<!-- end proof-83 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{quad:partial}
If the clausewise encoding of $F(y,Ax)$ has a resolution refutation
of width $W$ and depth $d$, and $2(W+1)\le r$, then $F(y,z)$ has a
resolution refutation of width at most $W+1$ and depth at most $d$.
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-84: body_md -->
We use the usual query game for resolution: a prover remembers a
partial assignment, queries a variable, and may forget values. The
prover wins by falsifying a clause. A width-$W$, depth-$d$ refutation
gives a strategy using at most $W+1$ remembered variables and $d$
queries. Conversely, a winning strategy with memory $u$ and $d$
queries gives a width-at-most-$u$, depth-at-most-$d$ refutation, with
weakening. These implications follow by traversing a proof backwards
and, conversely, labelling a strategy by the negations of its
remembered assignments; see also~\cite[Lemma~5.1]{FPR22}.

For $H\subseteq[n]$, $|H|\le r$, define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L_H&=\{a:\operatorname{wt}(a)\le r,
                   \mathsf{Supp}(A^{\mathsf T}a)\subseteq H\},\\
 C(H)&=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal L_H}\mathsf{Supp}(a).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then $\mathcal L_H$ is a linear space and
\begin{equation}\label{quad:closure}
 |C(H)|\le |H|/2.
\end{equation}
To prove the bound, every individual relation has support at most
$|H|/2$. If their union were larger, take the first finite union $U$
whose size exceeds $|H|/2$. Then $|U|\le |H|\le r$. In the span
of these relations a uniform vector has expected weight $|U|/2$,
whereas its image under $A^{\mathsf T}$ has expected weight at most
$|H|/2$. Averaging Eqn.~\eqref{quad:expansion} gives $|U|\le |H|/2$,
a contradiction. Sums of relations are now supported on $C(H)$
and therefore remain within the range $r$, proving linearity.
The closure is monotone in $H$. Also, for $v\notin H$,
\begin{equation}\label{quad:one-relation}
 \dim(\mathcal L_{H\cup\{v\}}/\mathcal L_H)\le1,
\end{equation}
since evaluation of $(A^{\mathsf T}a)_v$ has kernel $\mathcal L_H$.

An assignment $\rho$ on $H$ and an assignment $\sigma$ on $C(H)$
have a common extension satisfying $(Ax)_{C(H)}=\sigma$ exactly when
\begin{equation}\label{quad:compatibility}
 a\cdot\sigma=(A^{\mathsf T}a)\cdot\rho
 \qquad(a\in\mathcal L_H).
\end{equation}
Indeed, these are precisely the linear dependencies of the equations
$x_H=\rho$ and $(Ax)_{C(H)}=\sigma$. On adding one raw coordinate,
first query all new coarse variables in the closure. Their answers
preserve every old relation. By Eqn.~\eqref{quad:one-relation}, at most
one new relation remains; choose the raw answer to satisfy it.
Thus arbitrary answers of the coarse adversary can be accommodated.

Put $u=W+1$. Let $I$ be the currently remembered identity variables
and $R$ the currently remembered raw variables. Maintain a historical
raw set $H\supseteq R$, its assignment $\rho$, and a compatible
coarse assignment on $C(H)$, with
\[
 |H|\le2(u-|I|).
\]
The coarse memory is at most $|I|+|C(H)|\le u$.
Forgetting an identity variable forgets its value on both sides;
forgetting a raw variable need only shrink $R$.

Write $v=u-|I|$. A query already in $H$ uses its historical value.
Before a fresh raw query, if $|H|=2v$, reset $H$ to $R$ and forget
coarse variables outside $C(R)$. The query is legal only if
$|R|\le v-1$, so this reset discards at least $v+1$ historical
coordinates and at most $v$ coarse variables. Then add the queried
coordinate and use Eqn.~\eqref{quad:compatibility}.
Before a fresh identity query, the historical capacity decreases
from $2v$ to $2(v-1)$. If $H$ does not fit, reset it to $R$ first.
In this case $|H|\ge2v-1$ and $|R|\le v-1$, so at least $v$
historical coordinates and at most $v$ coarse variables are
discarded. The new identity query then fits the memory bound.
Restriction and monotonicity preserve compatibility at both resets.

If $Q_z$ counts all simulated coarse nonidentity queries, including
queries repeated after forgetting, telescoping the closure changes
gives
\[
 Q_z=|C(H_{\rm end})|+\sum_{\rm resets}\Delta_C
 \le |H_{\rm end}|+\sum_{\rm resets}\Delta_H
 \le\text{number of raw nonidentity queries}.
\]
Here $\Delta_C\le\Delta_H$ at either type of reset, as just shown.
Each identity query requires at most one coarse identity query.
The entire simulation therefore makes at most $d$ queries.

Finally, falsification of a full truth-table clause assigns all
raw support coordinates of the corresponding coarse clause. Each
coarse variable in that clause belongs to $C(R)\subseteq C(H)$,
and compatibility gives it the value of its substituted parity.
The coarse assignment falsifies the original clause. This proves
the game simulation and hence the lemma.
<!-- end proof-84 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{quad:grouped}
Fix $K=2^{16}$. For integers $B,q\ge2$, put
$J=\lceil\log q\rceil$ and $L_j=J-j+2$ for $0\le j\le J$, and set
\[
 n=KB\sum_{j=0}^{J}L_j.
\]
One can deterministically construct a map
$T:\mathsf{F}_2^{Bq}\to\mathsf{F}_2^n$ in time $\mathsf{poly}(B,2^q)$,
with a fixed exponent, such that $\operatorname{wt}(Ta)\ge2\operatorname{wt}(a)$ for
$0<\operatorname{wt}(a)\le B$.
The inputs are partitioned into $B$ groups of length $q$.
Outputs at scale $j$ are indexed by $(j,v,c)$ with $v\in[KB]$
and $c\in[L_j]$. A group reaches at most $Kd_j$ distinct labels
$v$ at this scale, where $d_j=\max\{1,\lfloor2^j/128\rfloor\}$.
In particular, one input group reaches $O(q)$ outputs in total.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-85: body_md -->
At scale $t=2^j$, construct a biregular multigraph with $B$ left
vertices, $KB$ right vertices, and degrees $Kd$ and $d$, where
$d=\max\{1,\lfloor t/128\rfloor\}$. For $d=1$ use disjoint
stars. Otherwise use a Ramanujan graph with nontrivial singular
values at most
\[
 \lambda\le\sqrt{Kd-1}+\sqrt{d-1}.
\]
Existence and the interlacing construction are due to
Gribinski and Marcus~\cite[Theorems~1.2 and~1.4]{GM21}.
The uniformity in $d$ used here is justified below.
For a left set of size $s\le B/t$, the first and second moments
of its incidence vector give
\[
 |\Gamma(S)|\ge
 \frac{Kd\,s}{ds/B+\lambda^2/(Kd)}
 \ge(1-1/32)Kd\,s.
\]
Indeed, the denominator is at most
$1+1/128+2/\sqrt K+1/K$, and its excess over one is below $1/32$.
Consequently at most $Kd\,s/16$ selected edge slots reach
nonunique neighbors: a neighbor receiving $a\ge2$ slots contributes
$a\le2(a-1)$. This counts parallel edges with their multiplicities.
Repeat the graph on $L=L_j$ disjoint copies of its right side,
using the same labels and ports in every copy. Set $D=KdL$.

Set $\tau=\min\{4t,q\}$. There is a linear code
$C_t:\mathsf{F}_2^q\to\mathsf{F}_2^D$ such that every $u$ with
$1\le\operatorname{wt}(u)\le\tau$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{quad:local-code}
 \operatorname{wt}(C_tu)\ge D/4.
\end{equation}
Here $D\ge256tL$ and
$\sum_{a=1}^{\tau}\binom qa\le2^{4tL}$.
For a random binary matrix, the initial conditional estimator
\[
 \sum_{1\le\operatorname{wt}(u)\le\tau}
 2^{D/4}\mathbf{E}[2^{-\operatorname{wt}(C_tu)}\mid\text{fixed entries}]
\]
is at most $2^{4tL+D/4}(3/4)^D\le2^{4tL-D/8}<1$.
A row contributes $3/4$ when its parity is free, and $1$ or $1/2$
otherwise. Both choices of the next matrix entry can therefore be
evaluated exactly by enumerating at most $2^q$ vectors. Choose the
smaller estimator. Its final value excludes every violation of
Eqn.~\eqref{quad:local-code}. All denominators are powers of two with
polynomial bit length.

Apply $C_t$ within each input group, route its $D$ code bits through
the edge slots, and take their parity at each right output.
Concatenate all scales. For an input of weight $w\le B$ meeting
$s$ groups, choose
$j=\min\{J,\lfloor\log(B/s)\rfloor\}$.
If $j<J$, then $B<2ts$, and at least $s/2$ active groups have
weight at most $4t$. Their codewords contain at least $Ds/8$
ones. At most $Ds/16$ can lie on nonunique slots, including slots
from the other active groups. Thus at least $Ds/16\ge16ts>2w$
ones survive. If $j=J$, every active group is protected and at
least $3Ds/16\ge2qs\ge2w$ ones survive.
This proves the expansion claim. Finally
$\sum_jKd_jL_j=O(q)$, since
$\sum_j2^j(J-j+2)<12q$ and $\sum_jL_j=O(\log^2q)=O(q)$.
Reusing the routing labels gives the stronger per-scale statement.
<!-- end proof-85 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{quad:constant-degree}
There are absolute constants $C,C_g,c_g>0$ and $\kappa<3$ with
the following property. For every sufficiently large integer $L$
and every $M\ge CL^6$, one can construct a binary matrix
$A\in\mathsf{F}_2^{M\times n}$ with $n\le C_gM/L$ such that
every $a$ with $0<\operatorname{wt}(a)\le c_gM/L^4$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{wt}(A^{\mathsf T}a)\ge2\operatorname{wt}(a).
\]
Every row has weight at most sixteen. The running time is
$\mathsf{poly}(M)+\exp(O(L^{2\kappa}\log L))$, with absolute constants.
Deleting any subset of rows preserves both the expansion range
on the retained rows and the bound on the number of outputs.
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-86: body_md -->
Set $\delta=2^{-21}L^{-2}$. For the degree $D$ chosen below, put
$m=\lceil D/(2L)\rceil$.
There is a bipartite graph on $D$ left vertices and $m$ right
vertices, of left degree eight, with at least $4|T|$ unique
neighbors whenever $|T|\le\delta D$.
To see this, choose eight distinct neighbors independently for
each left vertex. Failure on an $s$-set implies fewer than $6s$
neighbors, so a union bound is at most
\[
 \binom Ds\binom m{6s}(6s/m)^{8s}
 \le\left[4e^7 6^2L^2(s/D)\right]^s
 \le(1/8)^s.
\]
Here $6s\le m$, and $4e^7 6^2<2^{18}$.
The sum over $s\ge1$ is below one. Exhaustive enumeration of
neighbor lists and subsets constructs such a graph in
$\exp(O(D\log D))$ time.

Use the degree-$65$ nonbipartite Morgenstern graphs on
$v_k=64^{6k}-64^{2k}$ vertices, with nontrivial eigenvalues of
absolute value at most $16$~\cite[Theorems~5.11 and~5.13]{Mor91}.
Let $p$ be least with $(16/65)^p\le\delta/8$ and take the
bipartite double cover of a $p$th walk power. With
$\kappa=\log65/\log(65/16)<3$, its degree is
\[
 D=65^p=O(\delta^{-\kappa})=O(L^{2\kappa}).
\]
Choose the first outer size with $M'=v_kD\ge M$.
The sizes $v_k$ have a bounded multiplicative ratio; the condition
$M\ge CL^6$ ensures $M'=\Theta(M)$ and covers the minimum outer
size. Its normalized second singular value is at most $\delta/8$.

Use outer edges as the new left vertices. At each endpoint, route
the incident edge's port through the eight-neighbor inner graph;
right vertices are the pairs of an outer vertex and an inner
right vertex. The resulting left degree is sixteen and there
are $2v_km=O(M/L)$ outputs.
For $s\le\delta^2M'/8$ selected outer edges, call an endpoint
heavy if it sees more than $\delta D$ selected edges. If the two
heavy sets have total size $h$, then $h\le2s/(\delta D)$.
Expander mixing bounds the number of edges between them by
\[
 \frac{Dh^2}{4v_k}+\frac{\delta Dh}{16}
 \le \frac{s^2}{\delta^2Dv_k}+\frac{s}{8}\le s/4.
\]
At least $3s/4$ selected edges therefore have a light endpoint.
The inner graph supplies four unique neighbors per selected
incidence there, and different endpoints have disjoint output
sets. There are at least $3s\ge2s$ unique neighbors in total.
They are nonzero coordinates of the binary parity image.

Retain exactly $M$ left vertices. The same estimate applies to
every retained subset, and all outputs remain counted. This gives
range $\Omega(M/L^4)$. Finite-field enumeration, walk enumeration,
and port labelling take polynomial time in the output description;
the inner search has the displayed cost. More generally, any row
restriction preserves the parity inequality by extending a
retained coefficient vector with zeros.
<!-- end proof-86 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{quad:uniform-recursion}
This construction has depth at most $H(q)$, and its final output
length is at most $BD(K+1)^{H(q)}$ for an absolute $D$.
At every prefix, an original group reaches at most $C_Pq$ current
coordinates, for an absolute $C_P$. Each active simultaneous map
satisfies Eqn.~\eqref{quad:expansion} through weight $B$, where $B$
is the initial group count. Its construction takes time
$\mathsf{poly}(B,2^q)$ with a fixed exponent.
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-87: body_md -->
For a nonterminal band with upper endpoint $R$, $q_{\mathcal B}\le R^2$.
Since $2^j=2^{J+2-L_j}<8q\,2^{-L_j}$,
\begin{equation}\label{quad:band-sum}
 \sum_{L_j\in\mathcal B}2^j q_{\mathcal B}
 \le16qR^2 2^{-\lceil4\log R\rceil}
 \le16q/R^2.
\end{equation}
Successive nonterminal upper endpoints at least halve. The terminal upper endpoint
is bounded by $64$. The terms coming from the $1$ in
$d_j\le1+2^j$ contribute at most $(J+1)(J+2)^2$.
It follows that, for an absolute $A_0$,
\[
 \sum_jKd_jq_{\mathcal B(L_j)}\le A_0q.
\]
For children that remain active, their band upper endpoints exceed $\sqrt{Q_*}$.
Eqn.~\eqref{quad:band-sum} and the unweighted estimate give
\begin{equation}\label{quad:active-mass}
 \frac1q\sum_{j:q_{\mathcal B(L_j)}>Q_*}
 Kd_jq_{\mathcal B(L_j)}
 \le\frac{64K}{3Q_*}+\frac{K43^3}{2^{40}}<\frac1{32}.
\end{equation}
For the second term, on $2^{40}<q\le2^{41}$ one has $J=41$;
the corresponding bound decreases on later dyadic intervals.

Let $P(q)$ be the largest path support of one original group.
A group reaches at most $Kd_j$ child groups at scale $j$, so
\[
 P(q)\le\sum_jKd_jP(q_{\mathcal B(L_j)}).
\]
Count the terminal children by their actual lengths and apply induction
to the active children. By Eqn.~\eqref{quad:active-mass},
$P(q)\le A_0q+C_Pq/32\le C_Pq$ for a sufficiently large fixed
$C_P$. The same induction applies to every unfinished prefix:
an unprocessed child contributes its identity support.

Every child length is at most $(J+2)^2\le f(q)<q$.
In descending band order, successive lengths $q_i,q_{i+1}$ obey
$q_{i+1}\le f(q_i)$. Indeed a nonterminal band with upper endpoint $R$ has
$q_i\ge R^2/4$, while the next has length at most
$16(\log R)^2$. Thus the positive child heights are distinct and
at most $H(q)-1$. There are at most $64$ terminal children: after
the first terminal length, the upper endpoint is at most $2\sqrt{Q_*}$,
and it continues to halve until the last band.
If $E(q)$ denotes final output length per input group, then
$E(q)=K\sum_iE(q_i)$ at an active node and $E(q)=q$ at a terminal
node. Set $D=64KQ_*$. Induction gives
\[
 E(q)\le D(K+1)^{H(q)}.
\]
The active child contributions sum over distinct smaller heights;
their geometric sum leaves an additive $D$ to cover all terminal
children. This also proves the depth bound.

Every descendant group count is at least $B$. A direct sum of
active maps therefore expands every input of total weight at most
$B$; terminal coordinates are handled by \Cref{quad:partial}.
Finally the sum of child input lengths at an active node is
\[
 KB\sum_{\mathcal B}q_{\mathcal B}
 =KB(J+1)(J+4)/2<Bq/2.
\]
Hence total input mass over the recursion tree is at most $2Bq$.
No group length increases, and the fixed-exponent algorithms of
\Cref{quad:grouped} give the claimed time bound.
<!-- end proof-87 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
\label{quad:accumulator}
There is a uniformly polynomial-time continuation of the preceding
substitution sequence whose final variable count is at most $Ab$
for an absolute $A$. The total number of stages is
$T=O(1+H(q))$, each active map expands through weight $b$, and
at every prefix each original group reaches only $O(q)$ variables.
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-88: body_md -->
Fix an admissible integer $L_0\ge2C_g$, and then an integer
\[
 A\ge\max\{1,R_*,C_Z,L_0^4/c_g\}.
\]
On $2Ab$ input rows, \Cref{quad:constant-degree} supplies a
sixteen-neighbor map with at most $Ab$ outputs and expansion
range at least $2b$. Its size condition holds for large $b$
because $L_0$ is fixed.

Start with an empty accumulator. For $j=0,\ldots,J_*-1$, merge
it with $B_j$ by this map. Assign the at most $2Ab$ active
variables to distinct rows and delete the unassigned rows.
Keep every output coordinate; these form the next accumulator.
All other variables are left unchanged. Finally merge the
accumulator with $Z$ by the same procedure. If $J_*=0$, this
last map simply processes $Z$. Each intermediate accumulator
has at most $Ab$ variables, and after the last merge no untouched
part remains.

Row deletion preserves expansion by zero extension of coefficient
vectors. It adds neither input variables nor clauses. Outputs
adjacent only to deleted rows are still counted, and all retained
outputs are available as rows at later merges. A clause acquires
no path through an unused input row. This is also why unused
allocated coordinates do not enlarge its support.

The order of the merges controls support. Bucket $j$ traverses
$J_*-j+1$ new maps. By Eqn.~\eqref{quad:height-halving},
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h_j&\ge513\cdot2^{J_*-1-j},\\
 16^{J_*-j+1}&\le256(h_j/513)^4=O((h_j+1)^4).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Multiply Eqn.~\eqref{quad:bucket-final-support} by this factor and sum.
The two contributions are
\begin{align*}
 q\sum_{j<J_*}(h_j+1)^{-(12-\beta)}&=O(q),\\
 (\log q+3)^3\sum_{j<J_*}(h_j+1)^{\beta+4}
 &\le O((\log q+3)^3(H(q)+1)^{\beta+4})=O(q).
\end{align*}
The first sum is geometric when read backwards and the second
when read forwards. Here $12-\beta>2$, $H(q)\le\log q$, and
$(\log q+3)^{17}=O(q)$. Their constants are absolute. The part
$Z$ has support $O(q)$ and traverses only the last map.
At an unfinished prefix, every processed bucket has traversed
no more maps than in this estimate; an unprocessed bucket has
traversed none. The same bound therefore holds at every prefix.
The estimate also bounds prefixes of the earlier parallel bucket
compression, before the additional factors are applied.

The recursion uses at most $H(q)$ synchronized stages, bucket
compression uses $O(\log(H(q)+1))$, and the accumulator uses
$J_*+1=O(1+H(q))$. The active ranges are respectively at least
$b$, $2b$, and $2b$. The new calls have fixed $L_0$ and size
$2Ab$, so their total construction time is polynomial.
<!-- end proof-88 -->
<!-- lemma-43: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut}
Let $P$ be a size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program on $(X,R)\in\mathsf{F}_2^n\times\mathsf{F}_2^t$, and let $1\le q<n$. There is an equivalent full weakly read-once linear branching program
with a cut $V$ of at most $2s$ markers, each computation crossing exactly
one marker. At each marker $v$, let $W_v$ be its prefix space,
$d_v=\dim W_v$, and let $Q_v$ be the linear map whose coordinate forms are a basis for $W_v$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\rho(W_v)=\dim(W_v\cap E_X)=q$.
\item Reachability is $Q_v(X,R)\in A_v$ for some $A_v\subseteq\mathsf{F}_2^{d_v}$, with probabilities $p_v=|A_v|/2^{d_v}$ summing to one.
\item There are affine sections $\sigma_b:\mathsf{F}_2^{d_v}\to\mathsf{F}_2^{n+t}$, indexed by $b\in\mathsf{F}_2^{n+t-d_v}$, as in \Cref{lem:lbp-future-sections}. Write $\pi_X$ for projection onto the $X$ coordinates. Their projected maps $B_b=\pi_X\sigma_b$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
Q_0B_b(a)=Ja
\label{eq:lbp-common-pure-coordinates}
\end{equation}
for a rank-$q$ map $Q_0:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^q$ and a rank-$q$ map $J:\mathsf{F}_2^{d_v}\to\mathsf{F}_2^q$, independent of $b$.
\item For every fixed $a$ and independent uniform $b,b'$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{Pr}_{b,b'}[B_b(a)=B_{b'}(a)]=2^{-(n-q)}.
\label{eq:lbp-auxiliary-collision}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-43 -->
<!-- proof-89: body_md -->
Put $N=n+t$. Adding one query increases $\rho$ by at most one. Normalize as in \Cref{lem:lbp-full-cut}, and extend each separate short terminal edge by ignored pure-$X$ queries until $\rho\ge q$. This is possible while $\rho<q<n$.

Mark the first transition from $q-1$ to $q$. If an original branching query crosses the threshold, give its two outgoing edges separate markers. If an inserted ignored query crosses, its answers have the same continuation and use one marker. This convention prevents a shared node from being marked on a path that has already crossed the cut. An original vertex contributes at most two markers, either after its own query or on its two outgoing replacement chains. Each chain crosses at most once, so $|V|\le2s$. At each marker, all reaching paths have the same prefix space; its
dimension $d_v$ may depend on the marker.

Reachability and the sections follow by the proofs of \Cref{lem:lbp-full-cut} and \Cref{lem:lbp-future-sections}. Choose the rows of $Q_0$ to be the $q$ independent pure-$X$ forms in $W_v$. They are independent linear combinations of the rows of $Q_v$, giving the rank-$q$ map $J$ and Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-common-pure-coordinates}.

For fixed $a$, a uniform suffix transcript parametrizes the uniform distribution on $Q_v^{-1}(a)$. Its $X$-projection is uniform on an affine space of dimension $n-q$. Indeed, a form $\lambda$ on $\mathsf{F}_2^n$ annihilates $\pi_X\ker Q_v$ if and only if its pure-$X$ extension $(\lambda,0)$ lies in $W_v$. This annihilator has dimension $q$. Two independent uniform points in the projected fiber coincide with probability $2^{-(n-q)}$, proving Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-auxiliary-collision}.
<!-- end proof-89 -->
<!-- theorem-33: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-directional-auxiliary}
Let $X\sim U_n$ and $R\sim U_t$ be independent. Suppose $f:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2$ has directional derivative bias at most $\beta$ at entropy $K$. If $q<n$ and $2q-n\ge K$, every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program on $(X,R)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_{X,R}(-1)^{f(X)+P(X,R)}\right|
\le\sqrt{2s\bigl(\beta+2^{-(n-q)}\bigr)}.
\label{eq:lbp-directional-auxiliary}
\end{equation}
The bound has no dependence on $t$.
<!-- end theorem-33 -->
<!-- proof-90: body_md -->
Use the cut of \Cref{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut} and put $h=(-1)^f$. Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-common-pure-coordinates} shows that every $B_b$ has rank at least $q$, while the displacement $D_{b,b'}=B_b+B_{b'}$ takes values in $\ker Q_0$, of dimension $n-q$. Conditioning on $D_{b,b'}(a)=c$ reduces the rank of $B_b(a)$ by at most $n-q$, leaving dimension at least $2q-n\ge K$. On a nonzero fiber the derivative bound applies; on the zero fiber the sign product is one. Therefore
\[
\left|\mathbf{E}_a h(B_b(a))h(B_{b'}(a))\right|
\le\beta+\mathbf{Pr}_a[B_b(a)=B_{b'}(a)].
\]
For the suffix output sign $g_v(b)$, put $H_v(a)=\mathbf{E}_b g_v(b)h(B_b(a))$. Expanding its second moment and averaging Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-auxiliary-collision} gives
\[
\mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^2\le\beta+2^{-(n-q)}.
\]
The contribution from marker $v$ is $\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a)$. The two Cauchy--Schwarz applications in \Cref{thm:lbp-section-correlation}, using $|V|\le2s$ and $\sum_vp_v=1$, prove the result.
<!-- end proof-90 -->
<!-- lemma-44: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-intersecting-sections}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine extractor, let $u\ne0$, and put $h(x)=(-1)^{\langle u,F(x)\rangle}$. Suppose affine maps $B,B':\mathsf{F}_2^d\to\mathsf{F}_2^n$ satisfy $Q_0B=Q_0B'=J$, where $Q_0$ and $J$ are linear maps of rank $q\ge k+1$. For $c=\mathbf{Pr}_{a\sim U_d}[B(a)=B'(a)]$,
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_a h(B(a))h(B'(a))-c\right|
\le2\varepsilon(1-c).
\label{eq:lbp-intersecting-sections}
\end{equation}
Non-malleability against globally fixed-point-free affine involutions suffices.
<!-- end lemma-44 -->
<!-- proof-91: body_md -->
Choose a linear right inverse $U$ of $J$. Write a uniform parameter as $a=Uz+v$, with $z$ uniform on $\mathsf{F}_2^q$ and $v$ independently uniform on $\ker J$. For each fixed $v$, the maps $\sigma(z)=B(Uz+v)$ and $\tau(z)=B'(Uz+v)$ are sections of the same $Q_0$.

Put $\Delta(z)=\sigma(z)+\tau(z)\in\ker Q_0$. For a binary linear functional $\lambda$, let $E_\lambda=\{z:\lambda(\Delta(z))=1\}$. A nonempty $E_\lambda$ is an affine space of dimension at least $q-1\ge k$. Choose $w\in\ker Q_0$ with $\lambda(w)=1$, which is possible because $E_\lambda$ is nonempty, and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_\lambda(z)&=\Delta(z)+w\bigl(1+\lambda(\Delta(z))\bigr),\\
T_\lambda(x)&=x+\Delta_\lambda(Q_0x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then $Q_0\Delta_\lambda=0$ and $\lambda(\Delta_\lambda)=1$ everywhere. Thus $T_\lambda$ is affine, globally fixed-point-free, and $T_\lambda^2=\operatorname{id}$. On $E_\lambda$ it sends $\sigma(z)$ to $\tau(z)$. If $Z$ is uniform on $E_\lambda$, the source $\sigma(Z)$ has dimension at least $k$, so non-malleability gives
\[
\left|\mathbf{E}_z\mathbf1_{E_\lambda}(z)h(\sigma(z))h(\tau(z))\right|
\le2\varepsilon\mathbf{Pr}[E_\lambda].
\]
This is also true for an empty event. Averaging over uniform $\lambda$, every nonzero displacement is selected with probability $1/2$ and a zero displacement is never selected. Consequently
\[
\left|\mathbf{E}_z\mathbf1_{\{\Delta(z)\ne0\}}h(\sigma(z))h(\tau(z))\right|
\le2\varepsilon\mathbf{Pr}[\Delta(z)\ne0].
\]
On a collision the sign product is one. Add this contribution and average over $v$ to obtain Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-intersecting-sections}.
<!-- end proof-91 -->
<!-- theorem-34: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-affine-auxiliary}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine extractor, where $1\le k\le n-2$ and $0\le\varepsilon\le1/2$. Let $X\sim U_n$ and $R\sim U_t$ be independent. For every nonzero $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^m$ and every size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program $P$ on $(X,R)$,
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_{X,R}(-1)^{\langle u,F(X)\rangle+P(X,R)}\right|
\le\sqrt{2s\left(2\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)2^{-(n-k-1)}\right)}.
\label{eq:lbp-affine-auxiliary}
\end{equation}
Non-malleability against globally fixed-point-free affine involutions suffices. The bound has no dependence on $t$.
<!-- end theorem-34 -->
<!-- proof-92: body_md -->
Use \Cref{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut} with $q=k+1$. For each pair of projected sections, \Cref{lem:lbp-intersecting-sections} gives
\[
\left|\mathbf{E}_a h(B_b(a))h(B_{b'}(a))\right|
\le2\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)\mathbf{Pr}_a[B_b(a)=B_{b'}(a)].
\]
Expanding $\mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^2$ as in the preceding proof and using Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-auxiliary-collision} bounds it by
\[
2\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)2^{-(n-q)}.
\]
The same two Cauchy--Schwarz applications prove Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-affine-auxiliary}. More generally, any $k+1\le q<n$ gives the collision term $2^{-(n-q)}$.
<!-- end proof-92 -->
<!-- theorem-35: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-list-prediction}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine extractor, with $1\le k<n$. Let $P$ be a size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program whose sinks carry lists of at most $J$ distinct elements of $\mathsf{F}_2^m$, where $1\le J<2^m$. Write $p=J/2^m$ and $c=2^{-(n-k)}$, and define
\[
R_0=cp(1-p)+\varepsilon\bigl(c|1-2p|+(1-c)\max\{p,1-p\}\bigr).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{Pr}[F(U_n)\in P(U_n)]\le p+\sqrt{2sR_0}.
\label{eq:lbp-list-prediction}
\end{equation}
For $J\le2^{m-1}$, this implies
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{Pr}[F(U_n)\in P(U_n)]
\le p+\sqrt{2s(1-p)\bigl(\varepsilon+p2^{-(n-k)}\bigr)}.
\label{eq:lbp-small-list-prediction}
\end{equation}
Non-malleability against globally fixed-point-free affine involutions suffices.
<!-- end theorem-35 -->
<!-- proof-93: body_md -->
Pad each list to size exactly $J$, without changing the query structure or decreasing success. Use the cut and sections of \Cref{lem:lbp-full-cut} and \Cref{lem:lbp-future-sections}. The list on suffix $b$ is a fixed set $L_{v,b}$, independent of $a$. Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
Z_{v,b}(a)&=\mathbf1_{\{F(\sigma_b(a))\in L_{v,b}\}}-p,\\
H_v(a)&=\mathbf{E}_bZ_{v,b}(a).
\end{aligned}
\]
The ordinary affine extractor guarantee follows by marginalizing non-malleability against a nonzero translation. Thus the list probability on each section differs from $p$ by at most $\varepsilon$, giving
\[
\mathbf{E}_a Z_{v,b}(a)^2
\le p(1-p)+\varepsilon|1-2p|.
\]
For $b\ne b'$, the involution in \Cref{lem:lbp-nonmalleable-sections} gives the full vector guarantee
\[
(F(\sigma_b(U_k)),F(\sigma_{b'}(U_k)))
\approx_\varepsilon(U_m,F(\sigma_{b'}(U_k))).
\]
The product of the two centered list indicators has ideal expectation zero. Its possible values are $p^2$, $-p(1-p)$, and $(1-p)^2$, with range length $\max\{p,1-p\}$. Therefore
\[
\left|\mathbf{E}_a Z_{v,b}(a)Z_{v,b'}(a)\right|
\le\varepsilon\max\{p,1-p\}.
\]
Since $\mathbf{Pr}[b=b']=c$, expansion gives $\mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^2\le R_0$. The excess success probability is $\sum_v\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a)$, so two applications of Cauchy--Schwarz give Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-list-prediction}. For $p\le1/2$, the coefficient of $\varepsilon$ in $R_0$ is $1-p-cp\le1-p$, proving Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-small-list-prediction}.
<!-- end proof-93 -->
<!-- theorem-36: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-list-auxiliary}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ non-malleable affine
extractor, where $1\le k\le n-2$ and $0\le\varepsilon\le1/2$.
Let $X\sim U_n$ and $R\sim U_t$ be independent. Suppose $P$ is a
size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program on $(X,R)$ whose
sinks carry lists of at most $J$ distinct elements of $\mathsf{F}_2^m$,
where $1\le J<2^m$.
Write $p=J/2^m$ and $c=2^{-(n-k-1)}$, and define
\[
 R_0=cp(1-p)+\varepsilon
 \bigl(c|1-2p|+(1-c)\max\{p,1-p\}\bigr).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{Pr}[F(X)\in P(X,R)]\le p+\sqrt{2sR_0}.
 \label{eq:lbp-list-auxiliary}
\end{equation}
For $J\le2^{m-1}$, this implies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{Pr}[F(X)\in P(X,R)]
 \le p+\sqrt{2s(1-p)
                   \bigl(\varepsilon+p2^{-(n-k-1)}\bigr)}.
 \label{eq:lbp-small-list-auxiliary}
\end{equation}
The bounds do not depend on $t$. Non-malleability against globally
fixed-point-free affine involutions suffices.
<!-- end theorem-36 -->
<!-- proof-94: body_md -->
Pad each list to size exactly $J$. Apply
\Cref{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut} with $q=k+1$.
At a cut marker $v$, let $a$ be the uniform prefix coordinates and
$b$ the uniform suffix answers. Suppress $v$ from the notation.
The projected affine maps satisfy $Q_0B_b(a)=J_0a$, with
$\operatorname{rank}Q_0=\operatorname{rank}J_0=q$.
The output list $L_b$ is independent of $a$. Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 I_b(a)&=\mathbf1_{\{F(B_b(a))\in L_b\}},\\
 Z_b(a)&=I_b(a)-p,\\
 H(a)&=\mathbf{E}_b Z_b(a).
 \end{aligned}
\]
We prove $\mathbf{E}_aH(a)^2\le R_0$.

For fixed $a$, a uniform suffix parametrizes the full input fiber
uniformly. Its $X$-projection is uniform on an affine space of
dimension $n-q$. Hence, for every fixed $a,b$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{Pr}_{b'}[B_{b'}(a)=B_b(a)]=c.
 \label{eq:lbp-list-conditional-collision}
\end{equation}
Let $C$ denote this collision event. By symmetry and
$zz'\le(z^2+z'^2)/2$,
\[
 \mathbf{E}_{a,b,b'}\mathbf1_C Z_bZ_{b'}
 \le\mathbf{E}_{a,b,b'}\mathbf1_C Z_b^2
 =c\,\mathbf{E}_{a,b}Z_b^2.
\]
Each $B_b$ has rank at least $q\ge k$. The ordinary affine extractor guarantee
therefore gives $|\mathbf{E}_a I_b-p|\le\varepsilon$.
Since $Z_b^2=p^2+(1-2p)I_b$, the collision contribution is at most
\begin{equation}
 c\bigl(p(1-p)+\varepsilon|1-2p|\bigr).
 \label{eq:lbp-list-collision-contribution}
\end{equation}
When $p>1/2$, this uses the lower bound $\mathbf{E}_a I_b\ge p-\varepsilon$.

To bound the remaining contribution, fix $b,b'$ and choose a linear
right inverse $U$ of $J_0$. Write $a=Uz+w$, with independent uniform
$z\in\mathsf{F}_2^q$ and $w\in\ker J_0$. For fixed $w$, the maps
\[
 \sigma(z)=B_b(Uz+w),\qquad
 \tau(z)=B_{b'}(Uz+w)
\]
are affine sections of $Q_0$.
For a linear functional $\lambda$, let
$E_\lambda=\{z:\lambda(\sigma(z)+\tau(z))=1\}$.
A nonempty $E_\lambda$ has dimension at least $q-1=k$.
The involution constructed in the proof of
\Cref{lem:lbp-intersecting-sections} maps $\sigma(z)$ to $\tau(z)$
on $E_\lambda$ and is globally fixed-point-free.
Apply non-malleability to the uniform source on $\sigma(E_\lambda)$.
The test
\[
 \phi(y,y')=(\mathbf1_{y\in L_b}-p)
             (\mathbf1_{y'\in L_{b'}}-p)
\]
has ideal expectation zero and range length $M_p=\max\{p,1-p\}$.
Thus
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_z\mathbf1_{E_\lambda}(z)
       \phi(F(\sigma(z)),F(\tau(z)))\right|
 \le\varepsilon M_p\mathbf{Pr}[E_\lambda].
\]
Averaging over uniform $\lambda$ selects each nonzero displacement
with probability $1/2$ and never selects a zero displacement.
The triangle inequality, followed by averaging over $w,b,b'$, gives
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{a,b,b'}\mathbf1_{\neg C}Z_bZ_{b'}\right|
 \le\varepsilon M_p(1-c).
\]
Together with Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-list-collision-contribution}, this
proves $\mathbf{E}_aH(a)^2\le R_0$.

The excess success probability is
$\sum_v\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a)$.
Two applications of Cauchy--Schwarz, using at most $2s$ cut markers
and $\sum_v\mathbf{Pr}[A_v]=1$, bound it by $\sqrt{2sR_0}$.
For $p\le1/2$, the coefficient of $\varepsilon$ in $R_0$ is
$1-p-cp\le1-p$, giving
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-small-list-auxiliary}.
<!-- end proof-94 -->
<!-- theorem-37: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-higher-moment}
Let $F:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^m$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$ $h$-non-malleable affine extractor, where $1\le k<n$.
Let $r\ge1$ be an integer with $2r-1\le h$. For every nonzero output
parity $f_u(x)=\langle u,F(x)\rangle$ and every size-$s$ weakly
read-once linear branching program $P$,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f_u,P)
 \le\left[2s\left(2\varepsilon+(2r-1)!!\,2^{-r(n-k)}\right)\right]^{1/(2r)}.
 \label{eq:lbp-higher-moment}
\end{equation}
It suffices to assume $h$-non-malleability against globally
fixed-point-free affine involutions.
<!-- end theorem-37 -->
<!-- proof-95: body_md -->
Use the cut and sections of
\Cref{lem:lbp-full-cut} and \Cref{lem:lbp-future-sections}. Put $B=2^{n-k}$
and $\chi=(-1)^{f_u}$. Write $g_v(b)=(-1)^{P_v(b)}$ for the suffix output sign and define
\[
 H_v(a)=\mathbf{E}_b g_v(b)\chi(\sigma_b(a)).
\]
First consider $t+1\le2r$ distinct sections
$\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_t$ of the common map $Q_v$. The maps
\[
 T_j(x)=x+\sigma_0(Q_vx)+\sigma_j(Q_vx),\qquad 1\le j\le t,
\]
are globally fixed-point-free affine involutions and satisfy
$T_j\sigma_0=\sigma_j$, as in
\Cref{lem:lbp-nonmalleable-sections}. $h$-non-malleability therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}_a\prod_{j=0}^t\chi(\sigma_j(a))\right|\le2\varepsilon.
 \label{eq:lbp-joint-section-products}
\end{equation}
The first parity is uniform independently of the others in the ideal
distribution, so its product with the other signs has expectation zero.

Expand $\mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^{2r}$ over independent suffix indices
$b_1,\ldots,b_{2r}$. Every index occurring with even multiplicity
cancels. If any indices remain, their number is even and at most $2r$,
so Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-joint-section-products} bounds the absolute
expectation by $2\varepsilon$. Otherwise the product of all the
$g_v$ and $\chi$ signs is one. Let $\alpha_r(B)$ be the probability
that all multiplicities among $2r$ uniform indices from $[B]$ are even.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{E}_a|H_v(a)|^{2r}
 \le\alpha_r(B)+2\varepsilon(1-\alpha_r(B))
 \le2\varepsilon+(2r-1)!!B^{-r}.
 \label{eq:lbp-higher-even-moment}
\end{equation}
For the last inequality, an all-even tuple admits a perfect matching
of its positions in which matched entries agree. There are
$(2r-1)!!$ matchings, and a fixed matching is respected with probability
$B^{-r}$.

More generally, if $\mathbf{E}_a|H_v(a)|^{2r}\le M_r$ at every cut node,
H\"older's inequality gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{Corr}(f_u,P)
 &\le\sum_{v\in V}
       \left|\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a)\right|\\
 &\le M_r^{1/(2r)}\sum_{v\in V}p_v^{1-1/(2r)}
 \le(2sM_r)^{1/(2r)}.
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:lbp-moment-cut}
\end{equation}
Here $\sum_vp_v=1$ and $|V|\le2s$. Apply
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-higher-even-moment}.
<!-- end proof-95 -->
<!-- theorem-38: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-list-higher-moment}
Under the extractor hypotheses of \Cref{thm:lbp-higher-moment}, let
$P$ be a size-$s$ weakly read-once linear branching program whose sinks
carry lists of at most $J$ distinct elements of $\mathsf{F}_2^m$, where
$1\le J<2^m$. Set
\begin{itemize}
\item $p=J/2^m$, the success probability of a fixed list on a uniform output;
\item $B=2^{n-k}$, the number of suffix sections;
\item $a_p=\max\{p,1-p\}$, the largest absolute centered indicator value.
\end{itemize}
For independent Bernoulli-$p$ variables
$Y_1,\ldots,Y_B$, define
\[
 \mathcal M_{2r}(B,p)
 =\mathbf{E}\left(\frac1B\sum_{i=1}^B(Y_i-p)\right)^{2r}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{Pr}[F(U_n)\in P(U_n)]
 \le p+\left[2s\left(\mathcal M_{2r}(B,p)
                     +2r\varepsilon a_p^{2r-1}\right)\right]^{1/(2r)}.
 \label{eq:lbp-list-higher-moment}
\end{equation}
There is a constant $C_r$, depending only on $r$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal M_{2r}(B,p)
 \le C_r\left[
       \left(\frac{p(1-p)}B\right)^r
       +\frac{p(1-p)}{B^{2r-1}}\right].
 \label{eq:lbp-list-central-moment}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-38 -->
<!-- proof-96: body_md -->
Pad each list to size exactly $J$ and use the same cut and sections.
At a fixed cut node put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Z_b(a)&=\mathbf1_{\{F(\sigma_b(a))\in L_b\}}-p,\\
 H_v(a)&=\mathbf{E}_bZ_b(a).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consider a tuple in the expansion of $\mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^{2r}$. Suppose its
distinct suffix indices have multiplicities $e_1,\ldots,e_t$.
The $h$-non-malleability guarantee allows us to replace the output on any one
section by a uniform output independent of all the others. This
requires at most $t-1\le2r-1$ tamperings. Write
\[
 \mu_j=p(1-p)^j+(1-p)(-p)^j=\mathbf{E}(Y_1-p)^j.
\]
Successively replacing the section outputs compares the product moment
with $\prod_{i=1}^t\mu_{e_i}$.

A product of powers of centered indicators of total degree $q$ has
range length at most $a_p^{q-1}$. For $p\le1/2$, its positive values
are at most $(1-p)^q$, and any negative value has absolute value at
most $p(1-p)^{q-1}$. The case $p\ge1/2$ follows by complementing the
indicators. Since $|\mu_j|\le a_p^j$, each replacement contributes
error at most $\varepsilon a_p^{2r-1}$. The last replacement uses
the ordinary affine extractor guarantee, which follows by marginalizing non-malleability.
Thus
\[
 \mathbf{E}_aH_v(a)^{2r}
 \le\mathcal M_{2r}(B,p)+2r\varepsilon a_p^{2r-1}.
\]
Apply the H\"older argument of Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-moment-cut} to
the excess success probability
$\sum_v\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a)$.

For Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-list-central-moment}, put $v=p(1-p)$.
The independent moment expansion has no contribution from a suffix
index occurring exactly once, since $\mu_1=0$. A tuple with
$\ell\le r$ distinct indices, each occurring at least twice,
contributes at most $v^\ell$ in absolute value, since
$|\mu_j|\le v$ for $j\ge2$. There are at most
$C_rB^\ell$ such tuples. Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{2r}(B,p)
 \le C_r\sum_{\ell=1}^r v^\ell B^{\ell-2r}.
\]
For fixed $r$, this sum is bounded by a constant depending only on
$r$ times its two endpoint terms, proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-96 -->
<!-- theorem-39: body_md -->
\label{thm:lbp-auxiliary-higher-moment}
Under the extractor hypotheses of \Cref{thm:lbp-higher-moment}, let
$X\sim U_n$ and $R\sim U_t$ be independent. Let $P$ be a size-$s$
weakly read-once linear branching program on $(X,R)$. Put $L=2r$,
and let $D_L$ be the number of partitions of $[L]$ whose blocks all
have size at least two. For every integer $q$ with
$k+\binom L2\le q<n$ and every nonzero $u\in\mathsf{F}_2^m$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}_{X,R}(-1)^{f_u(X)+P(X,R)}\right|
 \le\left[2s\left(D_L2^{-r(n-q)}
                    +2(2^L-1)\varepsilon\right)\right]^{1/(2r)}.
 \label{eq:lbp-auxiliary-higher-moment}
\end{equation}
The bound has no dependence on $t$, and queries may mix the original
and auxiliary variables arbitrarily.
<!-- end theorem-39 -->
<!-- proof-97: body_md -->
Use \Cref{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut} at pure-input rank $q$.
At each marker, the projected sections satisfy $Q_0B_b(a)=Ja$,
where $Q_0,J$ have rank $q$. Put $\chi=(-1)^{f_u}$ and
$H_v(a)=\mathbf{E}_b g_v(b)\chi(B_b(a))$ as before.

Fix a tuple $b_1,\ldots,b_L$, abbreviate $B_i=B_{b_i}$, and let
\[
 U_i=\{a:B_i(a)\ne B_j(a)\text{ for every }j\ne i\}.
\]
We first prove that for every nonempty $I\subseteq[L]$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{\cap_{i\in I}U_i}(a)
                        \prod_{j=1}^L\chi(B_j(a))\right|
 \le2\varepsilon\mathbf{Pr}_a\left[\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i\right].
 \label{eq:lbp-unique-section-intersection}
\end{equation}
Choose a linear right inverse $U$ of $J$ and write $a=Uz+w$,
with independent uniform $z\in\mathsf{F}_2^q$ and $w\in\ker J$.
For fixed $w$, the maps $\sigma_i(z)=B_i(Uz+w)$ are affine
sections of $Q_0$.

Let $\mathcal E_I$ be the undirected pairs of indices having at
least one endpoint in $I$. For each $e=\{i,j\}\in\mathcal E_I$,
put $\Delta_e(z)=\sigma_i(z)+\sigma_j(z)$ and choose an independent
uniform linear functional $\lambda_e$ on $\mathsf{F}_2^n$. Consider
\[
 E_{\boldsymbol\lambda}
 =\{z:\lambda_e(\Delta_e(z))=1\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E_I\}.
\]
If nonempty, this is an affine space of dimension at least
$q-|\mathcal E_I|\ge q-\binom L2\ge k$.
Moreover, for every $z$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{E}_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\mathbf1_{E_{\boldsymbol\lambda}}(z)
 =2^{-|\mathcal E_I|}
   \mathbf1_{\{\Delta_e(z)\ne0\ \forall e\in\mathcal E_I\}}.
 \label{eq:lbp-random-separation-tests}
\end{equation}

Fix a nonempty $E_{\boldsymbol\lambda}$ and choose $i_0\in I$.
For every $j\ne i_0$, its pair with $i_0$ belongs to $\mathcal E_I$.
Write $\Delta_j=\sigma_{i_0}+\sigma_j$ and
$\lambda_j=\lambda_{\{i_0,j\}}$.
Choose $w_j\in\ker Q_0$ with $\lambda_j(w_j)=1$; such a vector
exists because the corresponding constraint is nonempty. Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_j(z)&=\Delta_j(z)+w_j(1+\lambda_j(\Delta_j(z))),\\
 T_j(x)&=x+D_j(Q_0x).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then $Q_0D_j=0$ and $\lambda_j(D_j)=1$ everywhere. Each $T_j$ is
a globally fixed-point-free affine involution, and
$T_j\sigma_{i_0}(z)=\sigma_j(z)$ on $E_{\boldsymbol\lambda}$.
Apply $h$-non-malleability to the source
$\sigma_{i_0}(U_{E_{\boldsymbol\lambda}})$ and these $L-1\le h$
maps. It bounds the absolute expectation of the sign product on this
source by $2\varepsilon$. Averaging over the functionals in
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-random-separation-tests} cancels the common factor
$2^{-|\mathcal E_I|}$ on both sides. Averaging over $w$ proves
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-unique-section-intersection}.

Let $N(a)$ count the indices whose projected value occurs exactly once
in the fixed tuple. Inclusion--exclusion, followed by
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-unique-section-intersection}, gives
\[
 \left|\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{\{N(a)>0\}}
                      \prod_{j=1}^L\chi(B_j(a))\right|
 \le2\varepsilon\mathbf{E}_a(2^{N(a)}-1).
\]
The product of the suffix signs $g_v(b_j)$ is fixed here and does
not change this bound. On the remaining event the absolute product
is at most one.

For every fixed $a$, independent uniform suffixes give independent
uniform projected inputs in the same affine space of dimension
$n-q$, by the proof of \Cref{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut}. Put
$B=2^{n-q}$. Let $N$ count singleton indices among $L$ independent
uniform draws from $[B]$, and write
$\beta_L(B)=\mathbf{Pr}[N=0]$ and $\gamma_L(B)=\mathbf{E}(2^N-1)$.
Expanding the moment and averaging the preceding bounds yields
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{E}_a|H_v(a)|^{2r}\le\beta_L(B)+2\varepsilon\gamma_L(B).
 \label{eq:lbp-auxiliary-occupancy-moment}
\end{equation}
Every tuple with no singleton has an equality partition with at most
$r$ blocks. A fixed such partition occurs with probability at most
$B^{-r}$, so $\beta_L(B)\le D_LB^{-r}$.
Also $\gamma_L(B)\le2^L-1$.
Apply Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-moment-cut}, whose H\"older argument also
applies when the prefix dimensions vary between markers.
<!-- end proof-97 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-cubic-quotient-count}
Let $F=\mathsf{F}_{2^m}$, and let $U,K\le F^3$ satisfy $U\cap K=\{0\}$ and
$\dim K=d$. Suppose $S\subseteq K$ is an affine space of dimension
$r\le d$ and $\dim(F^3/U)=d+r$. For the quotient map
$\pi:F^3\to F^3/U$, put $a(c)=\dim\pi(Fc)$. Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{E}_{c\sim S}2^{-a(c)}\le\frac32\,2^{-r/2}.
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-quotient-average}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- proof-98: body_md -->
For an integer $j\ge0$, let $T_j=\{c\in S:a(c)\le j\}$.
Choose a maximal $F$-linearly independent subset
$c_1,\ldots,c_h$ of $T_j\setminus\{0\}$, and put
$L=\operatorname{span}_F\{c_1,\ldots,c_h\}$. Thus $T_j\subseteq L$,
$h\le3$, and
\[
\dim\pi(L)=\dim\bigl(\pi(Fc_1)+\cdots+\pi(Fc_h)\bigr)\le hj.
\]
If $3j<d+r$, then $h=3$ is impossible: it would give $L=F^3$
and contradict $\dim\pi(F^3)=d+r$. Hence $h\le2$.
Since $\pi$ is injective on $K$, it is injective on $T_j$, and
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{Pr}_{c\sim S}[a(c)\le j]\le2^{2j-r}
\qquad\text{when }3j<d+r.
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-low-rank-count}
\end{equation}
The argument also covers $T_j=\varnothing$ or $T_j=\{0\}$.

For every nonnegative integer-valued random variable $a$,
\[
\mathbf{E}2^{-a}=\frac12\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\mathbf{Pr}[a\le j].
\]
If $r=2h$, apply Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-low-rank-count}
for $j<h$ and the bound $\mathbf{Pr}[a\le j]\le1$ thereafter. Since $r\le d$,
all these values of $j$ satisfy $3j<d+r$. This gives
\[
\mathbf{E}_{c\sim S}2^{-a(c)}
\le\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}2^{j-2h}
   +\frac12\sum_{j=h}^{\infty}2^{-j}
=\frac32\,2^{-h}-\frac12\,2^{-2h}.
\]
If $r=2h+1$, use Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-low-rank-count}
for $j\le h$, obtaining
\[
\mathbf{E}_{c\sim S}2^{-a(c)}
\le\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{h}2^{j-(2h+1)}
   +\frac12\sum_{j=h+1}^{\infty}2^{-j}
=2^{-h}-2^{-(2h+2)}
\le\sqrt2\,2^{-r/2}.
\]
Both estimates imply Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-quotient-average}.
<!-- end proof-98 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
\label{lem:lbp-cubic-sections}
Let $n=3m$ and $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathsf{F}_{2^m}/\mathsf{F}_2}(xyz)$.
Let $Q:\mathsf{F}_2^n\to\mathsf{F}_2^q$ have rank $q$, put $d=n-q$, and let
$\sigma,\tau:\mathsf{F}_2^q\to\mathsf{F}_2^n$ be affine sections of $Q$.
For $p_0=\mathbf{Pr}_a[\sigma(a)=\tau(a)]$,
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_a(-1)^{f(\sigma(a))+f(\tau(a))}-p_0\right|
\le\frac32\,2^{-(q-2m-d/2)}.
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-section-bound}
\end{equation}
The sections need not be disjoint.
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- proof-99: body_md -->
Write $F=\mathsf{F}_{2^m}$ and identify $\mathsf{F}_2^n$ with $F^3$.
