For $c=(c_1,c_2,c_3)\ne0$, the derivative
$D_cf(w)=f(w+c)+f(w)$ is quadratic. Its polar form is
\[
B_c(u,v)=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(c_1(u_2v_3+u_3v_2)
                   +c_2(u_1v_3+u_3v_1)
                   +c_3(u_1v_2+u_2v_1)\bigr).
\]
The corresponding alternating matrix over $F$ has rank two and
kernel $Fc$. Nondegeneracy of the trace pairing therefore gives
$\operatorname{rad}(B_c)=Fc$.

Let $U\le F^3$ have dimension $t$, and put
$a(c)=\dim\pi(Fc)=m-\dim(U\cap Fc)$, where $\pi$ is the quotient
map modulo $U$. The image of $U$ in the nondegenerate alternating
space $F^3/Fc$ has dimension $t-m+a(c)$. In an alternating space
of dimension $2m$, the restriction to a subspace of dimension $b$
has rank at least $2b-2m$. Consequently
\[
\mathsf{rank}(B_c|_U)\ge2(t-2m+a(c)).
\]
The absolute bias of a quadratic polynomial is at most two to
minus half the rank of its polar form, as follows by squaring the
bias and averaging over differences. Thus, for every translate $w+U$,
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_{z\sim w+U}(-1)^{D_cf(z)}\right|
\le2^{-(t-2m+a(c))}.
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-restricted-bias}
\end{equation}

Now put $K=\ker Q$, $\Delta=\sigma+\tau$, and
$S=\operatorname{Im}\Delta$. Let $\sigma_0$ and $\Delta_0$ denote
the linear parts of $\sigma$ and $\Delta$. Then $S$ is an affine
subspace of $K$ of dimension $r=\mathsf{rank}\Delta_0\le d$.
Every nonempty displacement fiber under $\sigma$ is a translate of
\[
U=\sigma_0(\ker\Delta_0).
\]
Since $Q\sigma_0=\operatorname{id}$, we have $\dim U=q-r$ and
$U\cap K=\{0\}$. In particular, $\dim(F^3/U)=d+r$, so
\Cref{lem:lbp-cubic-quotient-count} applies.
Conditional on $\Delta(a)=c$, the point $\sigma(a)$ is uniform
on a translate of $U$. The displacement is uniform on $S$.
Its zero value contributes exactly $p_0$. Applying
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-restricted-bias} only to nonzero displacements,
we obtain
\begin{align*}
\left|\mathbf{E}_a(-1)^{f(\sigma(a))+f(\tau(a))}-p_0\right|
&\le2^{-(q-r-2m)}\mathbf{E}_{c\sim S}
       \mathbf1_{\{c\ne0\}}2^{-a(c)}\\
&\le\frac32\,2^{-(q-2m-r/2)}
\le\frac32\,2^{-(q-2m-d/2)}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-99 -->
<!-- proof-100: body_md -->
We prove a bound for every $n=3m$ and any number $t$ of independent
uniform auxiliary bits. Let $1\le q<n$, put $d=n-q$, and apply
\Cref{lem:lbp-pure-input-cut} to $P(X,R)$, where $X\sim U_n$ and
$R\sim U_t$ are independent. At a cut marker $v$, the projected maps
$B_b:\mathsf{F}_2^{d_v}\to\mathsf{F}_2^n$ satisfy $Q_0B_b=J$, where both
$Q_0$ and $J$ have rank $q$.
Choose a linear right inverse $L$ of $J$ and write a uniform parameter
as $a=Lz+u$, where $z\sim U_q$ and $u$ is independently uniform
on $\ker J$. For each fixed $u$, the maps
\[
z\longmapsto B_b(Lz+u),\qquad
z\longmapsto B_{b'}(Lz+u)
\]
are sections of $Q_0$. Applying \Cref{lem:lbp-cubic-sections} and
averaging over $u$ gives, for $h=(-1)^f$,
\[
\left|\mathbf{E}_a h(B_b(a))h(B_{b'}(a))\right|
\le\mathbf{Pr}_a[B_b(a)=B_{b'}(a)]+\frac32\,2^{-(q-2m-d/2)}.
\]
Let $g_v(b)$ be the suffix output sign and put
$H_v(a)=\mathbf{E}_b g_v(b)h(B_b(a))$.
Expanding its second moment and using
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-auxiliary-collision}, we obtain
\[
\mathbf{E}_a H_v(a)^2\le2^{-d}+\frac32\,2^{-(q-2m-d/2)}.
\]
As in \Cref{thm:lbp-section-correlation}, the contribution from marker
$v$ is $\mathbf{E}_a\mathbf1_{A_v}(a)H_v(a)$. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds its
absolute value by $\sqrt{p_v\mathbf{E}_a H_v(a)^2}$.
Summing over the at most $2s$ markers and using $\sum_vp_v=1$ gives
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbf{E}_{X,R}(-1)^{f(X)+P(X,R)}\right|^2
\le2s\left(2^{-d}+\frac32\,2^{-(m-3d/2)}\right).
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-general}
\end{equation}
There is no dependence on $t$.

For $m\ge3$, take $d=\lfloor2m/5\rfloor$. Then
$m-3d/2\ge d$, so Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-general} is at most
$5s\,2^{-d}$. When $15\mid n$, we have $d=2n/15$, proving
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-trace}. Exact computation has correlation
one, and the stated average-case bound follows by substituting the
size of the program.

For an arbitrary input length $N\ge9$, put $m=\lfloor N/3\rfloor$
and apply the cubic trace function to three $m$-bit blocks, ignoring
the remaining at most two bits. Treating these bits as auxiliary inputs
gives
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Corr}(f_N,P)
\le\sqrt{5s}\,2^{-\frac12\lfloor2\lfloor N/3\rfloor/5\rfloor}.
\label{eq:lbp-cubic-all-lengths}
\end{equation}
In particular, exact computation requires size at least
$2^{\lfloor2\lfloor N/3\rfloor/5\rfloor}/5
=2^{2N/15-O(1)}$.
<!-- end proof-100 -->
<!-- proof-101: body_md -->
Use the cubic trace function extended to all input lengths as above.
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-cubic-all-lengths} gives
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(f_n,P)\le\sqrt{5s}\,2^{-n/15+O(1)}.
\]
For $s\le2^{n/36}$ and sufficiently large $n$, this is at most
$2^{-n/36}$. Agreement advantage is half the correlation, proving
the assertion with $c_1=c_2=1/36$.

Alternatively, fix $0<\rho<1$ and use a nonzero output parity of the directional affine extractor of Li and Zhong~\cite[Theorem 8]{LZdir}. Its entropy threshold is $K=\lceil\rho n\rceil$ and its error is at most $2^{-a_\rho n}$ for some $a_\rho>0$. Put $\lambda=\min\{a_\rho,(1-\rho)/2\}>0$. For sufficiently large $n$,
\[
2\varepsilon+2^{-\lfloor(n-K)/2\rfloor}\le6\cdot2^{-\lambda n}.
\]
For $s\le2^{\lambda n/4}$, \Cref{thm:lbp-directional-hardness} bounds the correlation by $\sqrt{12}\,2^{-3\lambda n/8}$, and hence by $2^{-\lambda n/4}$ for sufficiently large $n$.

One may also use the non-malleable affine extractor of Li~\cite[Theorem 1.12]{Li23}, with constants $\gamma,c>0$, entropy threshold $K=\lceil(1-\gamma)n\rceil$, linear output length, and error at most $2^{-cn}$. For $\lambda'=\min\{\gamma,c\}>0$,
\[
2\varepsilon+2^{-(n-K)}\le4\cdot2^{-\lambda'n},
\]
and Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lbp-affine-hardness} gives the same qualitative conclusion. Finally, \Cref{thm:affine-linear} supplies a non-malleable affine extractor at every fixed positive entropy rate, to which the same reduction applies. \Cref{thm:lbp-affine-auxiliary} permits independent uniform auxiliary inputs in these affine instantiations as well.
<!-- end proof-101 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{def:lossless-certificate}
A certificate with parameters $(M,H,q,k,k')$ consists of a partition
\[
 [N]=\Gamma_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}\Gamma_M
       \mathbin{\dot\cup}C_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots
       \mathbin{\dot\cup}C_q
\]
and indices $i_j\in\Gamma_j$, where $1\le|\Gamma_j|\le H$, such that
\begin{align}
 r\left(U_{i_j}\mid U_{\bigcup_{v\ne j}\Gamma_v}\right)&\ge k
       &&(j\in[M]),\label{eq:lossless-private}\\
 r\left(\sum_{j\in T}U_{i_j}\mid U_{C_c}\right)&\ge k'|T|
       &&(T\subseteq[M],\ c\in[q]).\label{eq:lossless-joint}
\end{align}
The sets $C_1,\ldots,C_q$ are the \emph{outside classes}; they partition
the blocks outside the selected clusters $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_M$.
We call $X_{i_j}$ the \emph{honest block} of $\Gamma_j$: its tagged
input serves as the original source in the non-malleability guarantee.
The left-hand side of Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-private} is its
\emph{private rank}. It equals the entropy remaining in $X_{i_j}$
after any feasible fixing of all blocks in the other clusters
$\Gamma_v$, $v\ne j$. Neither its own cluster nor the outside classes
$C_c$ are included in this fixing.
Empty outside classes are allowed. The private threshold $k$ is a
positive integer and the joint threshold $k'>0$ may be real; the second
condition is vacuous when $q=0$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- theorem-40: body_md -->
\label{thm:lossless-cluster-phase}
Suppose the jointly affine input blocks $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ have a
certificate with parameters $(M,H,q,k,k')$. If $\mathsf{anmExt}$ satisfies
\Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple} with entropy threshold $k$ for the original
source, against at most $H2^q-1$ comparisons, and with error
$\varepsilon\le1/2$, then
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbf{E}\prod_{i=1}^N(-1)^{g_i(X_i)}\right|
 \le\left(2\varepsilon+(2^q-1)2^{-k'}\right)^{M/2^q}.
 \label{eq:lossless-product}
\end{equation}
The comparison maps may be singular and may coincide with one another.
<!-- end theorem-40 -->
<!-- proof-102: body_md -->
Write $\Lambda=\mathbf{E}\prod_{i=1}^N(-1)^{g_i(X_i)}$ for the expectation
to be bounded.
For each outside class $C_c$, set
$K_c=\bigcap_{i\in C_c}\ker A_i$. The product of the factors indexed
by $C_c$ is invariant under translation by $K_c$. Successive applications of Cauchy--Schwarz over
cosets of $K_1,\ldots,K_q$ give
\begin{equation}
 |\Lambda|^{2^q}\le
 \mathbf{E}_{h_c\sim U_{K_c}}\mathbf{E}_Z
 \prod_{j=1}^M\prod_{i\in\Gamma_j}
 \prod_{\omega\in\mathsf{F}_2^q}
 (-1)^{g_i(X_i+A_i\sum_c\omega_ch_c)}.
 \label{eq:lossless-cube}
\end{equation}
Here the directions are independent. At each step, retain the earlier
directions, apply Jensen before Cauchy--Schwarz on the next quotient,
and use translation invariance to remove the factors in that outside class. Each step replaces
each remaining gadget factor by two shifted copies, proving the
displayed inequality by induction.

By Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-private}, there is a $k$-dimensional space
$V_j\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in\bigcup_{v\ne j}\Gamma_v}\ker A_i$
on which $A_{i_j}$ is injective. The $V_j$ have a direct sum: applying
$A_{i_j}$ to a relation among them isolates its $j$th summand. Choose
a complement $V_0$. After fixing the coordinate in $V_0$ and all directions in
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-cube}, the cluster products depend on independent
uniform coordinates in $V_1,\ldots,V_M$.

In cluster $j$, the distinguished input $X_{i_j}$ at $\omega=0$ is an
injective affine function of the uniform vector in $V_j$, and hence has
entropy $k$. Its tagged version serves as the original source in the
non-malleability guarantee. Each of the other at most $H2^q-1$ tagged
inputs is an affine function of this source on its support. Different
block indices have different tags. For $i=i_j$, an input with
$\omega\ne0$ can equal the original input only if
\begin{equation}
 A_{i_j}\sum_c\omega_ch_c=0
 \quad\text{for some }0\ne\omega\in\mathsf{F}_2^q.
 \label{eq:lossless-collision}
\end{equation}
Call this event bad. On a good cluster, non-malleability bounds the
absolute phase mean by $2\varepsilon$; on a bad cluster use one. The tagged inputs form
a jointly affine tuple, so \Cref{thm:joint-affine-tuple} applies directly.

For every $T\subseteq[M]$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{Pr}[\text{all }j\in T\text{ are bad}]
 \le\bigl((2^q-1)2^{-k'}\bigr)^{|T|}.
 \label{eq:lossless-joint-collisions}
\end{equation}
Indeed, choose a nonzero witness $\omega_j$ for each bad event and
group the indices by the last nonzero coordinate $c$ of $\omega_j$.
After fixing the earlier directions, the equations in group $T_c$
prescribe the joint image of $h_c$. Their conditional probability is
at most $2^{-k'|T_c|}$ by Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-joint}. Multiply over
$c$ and sum over the $(2^q-1)^{|T|}$ witness choices.

Set $a=2\varepsilon$ and $b=(2^q-1)2^{-k'}$. Expanding a nonnegative product
and applying Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-joint-collisions}, we obtain
\[
 \mathbf{E} a^{\#\mathrm{good}}
 =\mathbf{E}\prod_j\left(a+(1-a)\mathbf1_{\{j\text{ bad}\}}\right)
 \le(a+(1-a)b)^M\le(a+b)^M.
\]
Together with Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lossless-cube}, this proves the theorem.
<!-- end proof-102 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{lem:lossless-two-capacity}
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ have dimension at most $\ell$, let $C_0,C_1$
be two subspaces, and let $w\ge1$ be an integer.
For $T\subseteq[m]$, put $A_T=\sum_{i\in T}A_i$, and define
\[
 R=\min_{T_*\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_1=[m]}
 \left(w|T_*|+r(A_{T_0}\mid C_0)+r(A_{T_1}\mid C_1)\right).
\]
There are integers $0\le x_i\le w$ with $\sum_i x_i=R$ and
$\sum_{i\in T}x_i\le r(A_T\mid C_c)$ for every $T$ and $c$.
If the $A_i$ are independent, $W=\bigoplus_jB_j$, and
$C_0=B_b,C_1=B_{b^c}$, then, for $w=\ell$,
\begin{equation}
 R=\min_a\mathsf{rank}\bigl(P(b)J-JQ(a)\bigr).
 \label{eq:lossless-projector-capacity}
\end{equation}
Here $J:\bigoplus_iA_i\hookrightarrow W$, and $P,Q$ are the
coordinate projections in the two decompositions.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-103: body_md -->
Give each index $i$ a set of $w$ interchangeable slots. For
$c\in\{0,1\}$, a set of slots is independent if one can assign to
each slot of index $i$ a vector from $A_i$ so that their images
modulo $C_c$ are linearly independent. These sets form the linear
transversal matroid of the spaces $A_i$ modulo $C_c$.
On a slot set $E$, its rank is
\[
 r_c(E)=\min_{T\subseteq[m]}
 \left(r(A_T\mid C_c)+|E\setminus E_T|\right),
\]
where $E_T$ contains all slots of $T$~\cite{Rado42}. Matroid
intersection~\cite{Edmonds70} gives
the largest common independent set as
$\min_E(r_0(E)+r_1(E_{[m]}\setminus E))$.
If $z_i=|E\cap E_{\{i\}}|$, each rank is a minimum of affine
functions of $z$, hence is concave on $[0,w]^m$. Rounding each
$z_i$ to $0$ or $w$ does not increase the sum. Expanding the two
ranks at such a corner gives exactly the partition minimum $R$.
The slot counts of a maximum common set give the $x_i$.

For the last assertion, each index in $T_*$ can be moved to $T_0$ or
$T_1$ without increasing the expression, since $\dim A_i\le\ell=w$.
The kernel of $P(b)J-JQ(a)$ is the direct sum of
$A_{\mathsf{Supp}(a)}\cap B_{\mathsf{Supp}(b)}$ and
$A_{\mathsf{Supp}(a)^c}\cap B_{\mathsf{Supp}(b)^c}$. Subtract its dimension from
$\dim\bigoplus_iA_i$ and minimize over $a$.
<!-- end proof-103 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{lem:lossless-boolean-rounding}
Suppose $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ are independent nonzero spaces, $W=\bigoplus_{j=1}^nB_j$,
and $J:\bigoplus_iA_i\hookrightarrow W$. If
\[
 \max_b\min_a\mathsf{rank}(P(b)J-JQ(a))\le d,
\]
then there is a map $\pi:[m]\to[n]\cup\{0\}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf{rank}\bigl(P(b)J-JQ(b\circ\pi)\bigr)\le72d
 \quad\text{for every }b.
 \label{eq:lossless-label-rounding}
\end{equation}
Here $(b\circ\pi)_i=b_{\pi(i)}$ when $\pi(i)\ne0$, and it is zero
when $\pi(i)=0$. Thus the label zero denotes the zero coordinate function.
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-104: body_md -->
Choose witnesses $a(b)$ and put $a_i^*=\dim A_i$.
Products $xy$ of Boolean vectors in this proof are coordinatewise.
Injectivity of $J$ gives
$\mathsf{rank} JQ(v)=\sum_i a_i^*v_i$. Additivity of $P,Q$ bounds the
expected weighted number of coordinates where $a(x+y)\ne a(x)+a(y)$
by $3d$ for independent uniform $x,y$, with coordinate $i$ weighted
by $a_i^*$. For its $i$th coordinate,
let $\epsilon_i=\mathbf{Pr}[a_i(x+y)\ne a_i(x)+a_i(y)]$ and
$f_i(b)=(-1)^{a_i(b)}$. Fourier expansion gives
\[
 1-2\epsilon_i=\sum_\xi\widehat f_i(\xi)^3
 \le\max_\xi\widehat f_i(\xi).
\]
Thus there is a homogeneous linear form $L_i$ with
$\mathbf{Pr}[a_i(b)\ne L_i(b)]\le\epsilon_i$. It follows that the
additive matrix map $E(b)=P(b)J-JQ(L(b))$ has mean rank at most
$4d$. Since $E(z)=E(x)+E(x+z)$, its rank is at most $8d$ everywhere.

The projection identities imply
\[
 J\bigl(Q(L(xy))-Q(L(x))Q(L(y))\bigr)
 =-E(xy)+P(x)E(y)+E(x)Q(L(y)).
\]
Hence the expected weighted number of coordinates where
$L(xy)\ne L(x)L(y)$ is at most $24d$. A parity
on at least two coordinates fails multiplication on at least $3/8$
of uniform pairs $(x,y)$: its defect has bilinear matrix $I+\mathbf1
\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}$, of rank at least two. The total weight of
these coordinates is therefore at most $64d$. Replace them by zero.
Each remaining coordinate is zero or one input bit, and the resulting
label map has error at most $8d+64d$.
<!-- end proof-104 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
\label{lem:lossless-block-completion}
Partition the rows and columns of a matrix $M$ into the same set of
block labels, allowing unequal or empty groups. Put
$t=\max_S\mathsf{rank} M[S,S^c]$. There is a block-diagonal matrix $D$
with $\mathsf{rank}(M-D)\le5t$.
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-105: body_md -->
Choose a cut $(I,J)$ locally maximizing $r=\mathsf{rank} M[I,J]$ under
one-block moves and reversal. Choose $r$ pivot rows $R$ in $I$ and
pivot columns $C$ in $J$, with invertible pivot matrix $P$. Set
$L=M[:,C]P^{-1}M[R,:]$ and $E=M-L$, taking $L=0$ if $r=0$.
Then $\mathsf{rank} L=r$, $E[I,J]=0$, and $E$ vanishes on all pivot
rows and columns. Let $D$ be the diagonal blocks of $E$.

For $i\in I$, let $r_i$ be the number of pivot rows in that block.
The columns of $E[I\setminus\{i\},i]$ lie in the column space of
$M[I\setminus\{i\},C\cup i]$, of dimension at most $r$ by local
optimality. Evaluation on the remaining pivot rows has rank at least
$r-r_i$. Since the residual columns vanish there, their rank is at
most $r_i$. Summing over $i$ gives $\mathsf{rank}(E-D)[I,I]\le r$.
The transposed argument gives $\mathsf{rank}(E-D)[J,J]\le r$.
Reversal and $\mathsf{rank} L=r$ give
$\mathsf{rank}(E-D)[J,I]\le2r$. The fourth rectangle is zero.
Consequently $\mathsf{rank}(M-D)\le r+r+r+2r\le5t$.
<!-- end proof-105 -->
<!-- theorem-41: body_md -->
\label{thm:universal-certificate}
For every $0<\eta\le1$, there are constants $\alpha,\beta>0$ and
integers $H,Q,\ell_0\ge1$ with the following property.
Let $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ be binary row spaces of dimension at most
$\ell\ge\ell_0$, and put $U_I=\sum_{i\in I}U_i$ for $I\subseteq[N]$.
If
\begin{equation}
 \dim U_I\ge\eta\ell|I|\quad\text{for every }I\subseteq[N],
 \label{univ:eq:spread}
\end{equation}
then the arrangement has a rank certificate with at least $\alpha N$ honest blocks,
cluster size at most $H$, at most $Q$ outside classes, and both
thresholds at least $\beta\ell$. The constants also apply to every
nonempty subset of the blocks.
<!-- end theorem-41 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{univ:lem:normalization}
Suppose Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:spread} holds, and let $\chi,q\ge1$ be
integers. There are an actual source restriction $X_0$ and an
extension $X'\supseteq X_0$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
 \item Both arrangements have intersection density at most $\chi$.
 For $0<\sigma<\eta$, at least $N-N/[\chi(\eta-\sigma)]$ blocks
 have rank at least $\sigma\ell$ in $X_0$.
 \item $X'$ has the same individual block images as $X_0$, and its
 blocks partition into $q$ internally independent families: the row
 spaces of the blocks within each family have a direct sum.
 \item For $f(S)=\dim\operatorname{proj}_S X_0$ and
 $p(S)=\dim\operatorname{proj}_S X'$, the difference $d=p-f$ is
 nonnegative and monotone, and there are integers $w_i\ge0$ such that the weights
 $w(S)=\sum_{i\in S}w_i$ and total weight $W=\sum_iw_i$ satisfy
 \begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 d(S)&\le w(S),\\
 W&=\dim X'-\dim X_0\le\frac{(\chi-1)N\ell}{2q}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{univ:eq:coordinate-defect}
 \end{equation}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- proof-106: body_md -->
Choose $Z$ maximizing $\Phi(Z)=\sum_i\dim(U_i\cap Z)-\chi\dim Z$.
Then $\dim Z\le N\ell/\chi$. The quotient spaces
$\overline U_i=(U_i+Z)/Z$ have density at most $\chi$: if
$\widetilde Y$ is the inverse image of a quotient space $Y$, maximality gives
\[
 \sum_i\dim(\overline U_i\cap Y)
 =\sum_i\bigl(\dim(U_i\cap\widetilde Y)-\dim(U_i\cap Z)\bigr)
 \le\chi\dim Y.
\]
For $B=\{i:\dim\overline U_i<\sigma\ell\}$, rank spread gives
$\eta\ell|B|\le\dim U_B\le N\ell/\chi+\sigma\ell|B|$.
The quotient is realized by restricting latent directions to
$\operatorname{Ann}(Z)$; call this source $X_0$.

Put $L=\sum_i\dim\overline U_i$ and
$F(t)=\mathbf{E}\dim\overline U_{S_t}$, where each index belongs to $S_t$
independently with probability $t$. Define
\[
 D(t)=\sum_i\mathbf{E}\dim(\overline U_i\cap\overline U_{S_t\setminus\{i\}}).
\]
Differentiating the displayed expectation $F(t)$ and applying density
to $\overline U_{S_t}$ give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F'(t)&=L-D(t),\\
 tL+(1-t)D(t)&\le\chi F(t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Solving $F'(t)\ge(L-\chi F(t))/(1-t)$, with $F(0)=0$, yields
\begin{equation}
 F(t)\ge\frac L\chi\bigl(1-(1-t)^\chi\bigr).
 \label{univ:eq:color-rank}
\end{equation}
Assign each block independently and uniformly to one of $q$ classes.
There is therefore a partition $C_1,\ldots,C_q$ with
\[
 D:=L-\sum_c\dim\overline U_{C_c}
 \le L\left[1-\frac q\chi\bigl(1-(1-1/q)^\chi\bigr)\right]
 \le\frac{\chi-1}{2q}L.
\]
The last inequality is the two-term inclusion--exclusion bound.

Represent $X_0$ in $E=\bigoplus_iE_i$, with $E_i$ its individual block
image. For $F_c=\operatorname{proj}_{C_c}X_0$, choose a complement
$N_c$ spanned by coordinate axes of $E_{C_c}$, and set
$N_* =\bigoplus_cN_c$, $X'=X_0+N_*$. If $n\in N_*\cap X_0$,
its projection onto each class $C_c$ belongs to $N_c\cap F_c=0$.
Thus $\dim X'-\dim X_0=D$, the projection onto each class is all of $E_{C_c}$,
and the individual images stay unchanged.

Let $w_i$ count the chosen axes in block $i$. Then $d(S)\le w(S)$.
If $\pi:(X')^*\to X_0^*$ is restriction, $d(S)$ is the dimension
of the block row span on $S$ intersected with $\ker\pi$, so it
is monotone. The map $\pi$ is injective on each individual row space
$U_i'$. Consequently
\[
 \sum_i\dim(U_i'\cap Y)
 \le\sum_i\dim(\overline U_i\cap\pi Y)
 \le\chi\dim\pi Y\le\chi\dim Y.
\]
This proves all assertions.
<!-- end proof-106 -->
<!-- lemma-51: body_md -->
\label{univ:lem:repair}
Let $p,f$ give the dimensions of the spans of block row spaces in
two arrangements on the same original block indices. Write
$f(T\mid C)=f(T\cup C)-f(C)$, and similarly for $p$.
Suppose $d=p-f$ is
nonnegative and monotone, and $d(S)\le w(S)$ for nonnegative block
weights of total mass $W$. If $p$ has a certificate with $m$ honest
blocks, cluster bound $H$, $Q$ outside classes, and integer threshold
$k$, then for every integer $1\le\lambda<k$, $f$ has a certificate
using surviving original clusters, threshold $\lambda$, at most
$Q+2$ outside classes, and at least
\begin{equation}
 m-\frac{W}{k-\lambda+1}-\frac{W}{k-\lambda}
 \label{univ:eq:repair-count}
\end{equation}
honest blocks.
<!-- end lemma-51 -->
<!-- proof-107: body_md -->
Delete a cluster $\Gamma$ if its honest block $i$ has $f$-rank below
$\lambda$ conditioned on the other surviving clusters $E\setminus\Gamma$.
The private-rank inequality for the certificate in $p$ gives
\[
 d(i\cup(E\setminus\Gamma))-d(E\setminus\Gamma)\ge k-\lambda+1.
\]
By monotonicity, deleting $\Gamma$ decreases $d(E)$ by at least this
amount. There are at most $W/(k-\lambda+1)$ deletions; let $B$ be their
union. The remaining clusters have private threshold $\lambda$ in $f$
and joint threshold $k$ against $B$ in $p$, by expanding rank in a chain.

Process the original outside classes and $B$ one set at a time.
For each such set $C$, repeatedly delete a nonempty set $T$ of current
honest blocks with $f(T\mid C)<\lambda|T|$. Let $R_C$ be all blocks
deleted in this step. Conditional subadditivity and the joint-rank
inequality for $p$ give, when $R_C\ne\varnothing$,
\[
 (k-\lambda)|R_C|<d(R_C\cup C)-d(C)\le w(R_C)+w(C).
\]
All processed sets $C$ and all sets $R_C$ are pairwise disjoint.
Thus these deletions cost fewer than $W/(k-\lambda)$ targets.
Put their whole clusters in one further outside class. The private
inequalities established after the first step give joint threshold
$\lambda$ against this class by a rank chain. Deleting targets only
improves the other inequalities.
<!-- end proof-107 -->
<!-- lemma-52: body_md -->
\label{univ:lem:alignment}
Let $A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m A_i$ be independent nonzero cores of dimension
at most $\ell$, with inclusion $J:A\hookrightarrow W$, and let
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ be an internally independent family of nonzero
original block spaces, $n\ge1$. Put
\begin{equation}
 g=\max_{S\subseteq[n]}\min_{I_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_1=[m]}
 \bigl(r(A_{I_0}\mid B_S)+r(A_{I_1}\mid B_{S^c})\bigr).
 \label{univ:eq:real-capacity}
\end{equation}
There are labels $\pi(i)\in[n]$ and a map $F:A\to B_{[n]}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 F(A_i)&\subseteq B_{\pi(i)},\\
 \mathsf{rank}(J-F)&\le361g.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{univ:eq:alignment}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-52 -->
<!-- proof-108: body_md -->
Write $W=B\oplus C$, where $B=\bigoplus_jB_j$, and let
$h=\mathsf{rank}(J\bmod B)\le g$, using the empty cut. Here $J\bmod B$
is $J$ followed by the quotient map from $W$ to $W/B$.
Complete the family by a decomposition of $C$. Its cut capacity is
at most $g$, since additional conditioning only decreases ranks.
The projector identity and Boolean rounding
(\Cref{lem:lossless-two-capacity} and \Cref{lem:lossless-boolean-rounding})
therefore give original, auxiliary, or zero labels satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf{rank}\bigl(P(x)J-JQ(x\circ\pi)\bigr)\le72g\qquad\text{for every }x.
 \label{univ:eq:rounded-family}
\end{equation}
Let $P_B$ project onto $B$. Group the columns of $P_BJ$ by original
labels, collecting auxiliary- and zero-labeled columns into a group
$0$ with no rows. Every off-diagonal cut of this rectangular matrix
has rank at most $72g$: in Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:rounded-family}, select
the original labels on the row side and restrict to the complementary
column groups. If the row side contains $0$, omit that empty row
group and further restrict the columns.
By \Cref{lem:lossless-block-completion}, a block-diagonal map $F$
satisfies $\mathsf{rank}(P_BJ-F)\le360g$. Its group-$0$ columns vanish,
so assign them any original label. Finally
$\mathsf{rank}(J-F)\le h+360g\le361g$.
<!-- end proof-108 -->
<!-- lemma-53: body_md -->
\label{univ:lem:selection}
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ be independent cores of dimension at least $b$.
Suppose proposed clusters $\Delta_i$ contain their respective core
blocks, have at most $B$ blocks of rank at most $\ell$, and each
intersects at most $\Delta$ other proposed clusters. For an integer
$1\le k\le b$, put $a=b-k+1$. There are at least
\begin{equation}
 \frac{m}{4(\Delta+B\ell/a)}
 \label{univ:eq:selection}
\end{equation}
pairwise disjoint proposed clusters with honest private rank at least
$k$ against the other selected clusters.
<!-- end lemma-53 -->
<!-- proof-109: body_md -->
Independence and conditional subadditivity give
\begin{equation}
 a\,|\{i:r(A_i\mid Y)<k\}|\le\dim Y.
 \label{univ:eq:bad-cores}
\end{equation}
Indeed, for these indices $I$, $b|I|\le\dim A_I\le\dim Y+(k-1)|I|$.
Sample clusters independently with probability $u$. Remove each
sampled cluster meeting another sampled cluster or having core rank
below $k$ against the others. Intersections cost at most
$u^2\Delta m$ in expectation. Each private-rank test depends only on the
other sampling coins; its failure probability is at most the failure probability
against the full sampled span $Y_S$. By Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:bad-cores},
the expected number of sampled clusters failing the private-rank bound
is at most $u\mathbf{E}\dim Y_S/a\le u^2B\ell m/a$.
Taking $u=1/[2(\Delta+B\ell/a)]$ proves the bound.
<!-- end proof-109 -->
<!-- lemma-54: body_md -->
\label{univ:lem:assembly}
Suppose an old arrangement has a certificate with $m$ honest blocks,
cluster bound $H$, $Q_0$ outside classes, and common integer threshold
$\kappa$. Suppose its honest spaces contain independent cores of
ranks between $\lceil\rho\ell\rceil$ and $\ell$, where $0<\rho\le1$.
Add $q\ge1$ fresh, mutually disjoint families of original blocks, each internally
independent. Suppose their ranks are at most $\ell$ and their combined
intersection density is at most $\chi\ge1$. Set
\begin{itemize}
 \item $d_* =\lceil12\chi/\rho\rceil$, $D_*=H+2d_*$;
 \item $\delta=\rho^3/(2^{20}\chi D_*)$;
 \item $R=\lceil(2/\delta)\ln(4q)\rceil$.
\end{itemize}
For $\ell\ge8(R+1)/\delta$, the enlarged arrangement has a certificate
with honest blocks among the original ones and
\begin{align}
 M&\ge\frac{\rho m}{64D_*},
 &H_{\rm new}&\le H+d_*,\label{univ:eq:assembly-count}\\
 Q_{\rm new}&\le Q_0+q2^R+1,
 &k_{\rm new},k'_{\rm new}&\ge
 \min\{\kappa,\delta\ell/[8(R+1)]\}.
 \label{univ:eq:assembly-rank}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-54 -->
<!-- proof-110: body_md -->
Put $b=\lceil\rho\ell\rceil$.
Write $B_{t,1},\ldots,B_{t,n_t}$ for the block spaces in fresh family
$t$, and let $J$ be the inclusion of the direct sum of the cores
into the ambient row space. For a set $S$ of indices in family $t$,
write $B_{t,S}=\sum_{j\in S}B_{t,j}$.

\paragraph{Peeling.}
For each fresh family $t$, start with all core indices $I=[m]$.
Compute its capacity $G_t(I)$ from Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:real-capacity},
always cutting the entire original family. If $G_t(I)\le\delta\ell|I|$,
stop and call $L_t=I$ the \emph{low-capacity remainder}. The alignment
lemma gives a map $F_t:A_{L_t}\to B_{t,[n_t]}$.
Writing $p_t=\mathsf{rank}(J-F_t)$, its guarantees are
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 F_t(A_i)&\subseteq B_{t,\pi_t(i)},\\
 p_t&\le361\delta\ell|L_t|.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{univ:eq:low-maps}
\end{equation}
In the high-capacity case $G_t(I)>\delta\ell|I|$, a maximizing cut
and \Cref{lem:lossless-two-capacity}, with
cap $\ell$, give weights $0\le x_i\le\ell$ of total $G_t(I)$ whose
sum on every subset is bounded by its joint rank against either side.
Allowing the part $T_*$ in that lemma does not lower the two-part
minimum for the chosen cut: each index in $T_*$ can be moved to
either of the other parts without increasing the expression,
since $\dim A_i\le\ell$. Remove those indices with
$x_i\ge\lceil G_t(I)/(2|I|)\rceil$ and call the removed set a
\emph{high group}, meaning a group removed by the high-capacity case.
The other weights sum to less
than $G_t(I)/2$, so at least $\delta|I|/2$ indices are removed.
Every subset of this group has rank greater than $\delta\ell/2$
per index against both sides of the recorded cut.

If the process has not stopped in the low-capacity case after $R$
removals, discard its remaining at most $m/(4q)$ indices and set
$L_t=\varnothing$. Zero-rank family blocks are irrelevant; a wholly
zero family always falls in the high-capacity case on nonempty $I$.
Use the zero map when $L_t=\varnothing$.
Delete all discarded remainders globally, leaving $I_*$ of size
$m_*\ge3m/4$. Restrict the maps and high groups to $I_*$; all rank
inequalities persist. For each family, $I_*$ partitions into the
surviving part of $L_t$ and at most $R$ high groups.

\paragraph{Total rank discrepancy.}
Initially use the low-capacity remainders before global deletion.
Let $S=\sum_t|L_t|$ count their indices with multiplicity, and let
\[
 P=\sum_t p_t=\sum_t\mathsf{rank}(J|_{A_{L_t}}-F_t)
\]
be the total rank discrepancy between the inclusion maps and the maps $F_t$. Also put $A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m A_i$ and
$Z_*=\sum_t\operatorname{im}(J|_{A_{L_t}}-F_t)$.
The grouped images of each $F_t$ lie in individual family blocks and
in $A+Z_*$. Internal independence and intersection density imply
\begin{align}
 bS-P&\le\sum_t\mathsf{rank} F_t(A_{L_t})
 \le\chi(\dim A+\dim Z_*)\le\chi(m\ell+P),
 \label{univ:eq:self-bound}\\
 P&\le361\delta\ell S.
 \label{univ:eq:map-error-sum}
\end{align}
Since $361\delta(\chi+1)\le\rho/2$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 S&\le2\chi m/\rho,\\
 P&\le(722\chi\delta/\rho)m\ell
 <\frac{\rho^2m\ell}{1024D_*}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{univ:eq:absorbed-error}
\end{equation}
Thus the bound on the total rank discrepancy $P$ is independent of $q$. Restricting the maps to
$I_*$ only decreases $P$.

\paragraph{Disjoint private clusters.}
Let $d_i$ count the low-capacity remainders containing $i\in I_*$. The same density
argument gives
$b\sum_i d_i\le\chi m_*\ell+(\chi+1)P$.
Since $P\le m_*\ell$, deleting indices with $d_i>d_*$ costs at most
$m_*/4$ indices. Within each family $t$, group the cores indexed by
$L_t$ according to their labels $\pi_t(i)$.
The sum of these groups' kernel dimensions is at most $p_t$.
A group of $s>2\ell/b$ cores has kernel dimension at least
$bs-\ell>bs/2$, so deleting such groups costs fewer than $2p_t/b$
indices. Deleting individual cores indexed by $L_t$ whose image rank
is below $b/2$
costs fewer than another $2p_t/b$ indices. Here the individual kernel
spaces are independent and lie in $\ker F_t$.

Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:absorbed-error}, together with $m_*\ge3m/4$, gives
\begin{equation}
 P\le\frac{\rho^2m_*\ell}{128D_*}.
 \label{univ:eq:selection-budget}
\end{equation}
Hence at least $m_*/2$ candidates remain. Propose
$\Delta_i=\Gamma_i\cup\{B_{t,\pi_t(i)}:i\in L_t\}$.
Each has at most $H+d_*$ blocks and conflicts with at most
$2d_*\ell/b$ others. For $k=\lfloor b/2\rfloor$, the coefficients
in the two deletion bounds from the proof of \Cref{univ:lem:selection}
sum to at most
\[
 \frac{2d_*\ell}{b}+\frac{(H+d_*)\ell}{b-k+1}
 \le\frac{2D_*\ell}{b}.
\]
Sampling with $u=b/(4D_*\ell)$ therefore retains disjoint clusters
with private rank $k$ and at least
\begin{equation}
 M_s\ge\frac{\rho m_*}{16D_*}
 \label{univ:eq:selected-count}
\end{equation}
honest blocks. For each family $t$, the labels $\pi_t(i)$ assigned to
the selected indices $i\in L_t$ are distinct.

\paragraph{Joint rank against unassigned blocks.}
Fix a family $t$ and restrict latent directions to
$\operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{im}(J-F_t))$, of codimension $p_t$.
On this restriction, each core indexed by $L_t$ agrees with its image
under $F_t$.
Taking a complement to its individual kernel gives a matched space
$E_{t,i}\subseteq B_{t,\pi_t(i)}$ of dimension at least $b/2$.
Write $f_t$ for the restricted family rank function and
$e_j=\dim B_{t,j}$ before restriction. Set
\[
 \varphi_t(S)=\sum_{j\in S}e_j-f_t([n_t])+f_t([n_t]\setminus S).
\]
This is nonnegative and monotone, with $\varphi_t([n_t])\le p_t$,
because the original family is independent.

Let $I_{\rm sel}$ be the set of currently selected indices, and put
\[
 S_t=\{\pi_t(i):i\in I_{\rm sel}\cap L_t\}.
\]
Thus $S_t$ consists of the labels assigned to selected indices in the
low-capacity remainder $L_t$. Call blocks $B_{t,j}$ with $j\notin S_t$
\emph{unassigned} in family $t$. Set $\lambda=\lfloor b/4\rfloor$.
Whenever a nonempty $T\subseteq I_{\rm sel}\cap L_t$ has restricted
joint core rank below $\lambda|T|$ against the unassigned blocks,
delete $T$ from $I_{\rm sel}$ and update the assigned-label sets in
every family. Let $S_t$ denote the set before this deletion and put
$J=\pi_t(T)$. Then
\begin{align*}
 \varphi_t(S_t)-\varphi_t(S_t\setminus J)
 &=\sum_{j\in J}e_j-r_t(B_{t,J}\mid B_{t,[n_t]\setminus S_t})\\
 &\ge\sum_{i\in T}\dim E_{t,i}
       -r_t(E_{t,T}\mid B_{t,[n_t]\setminus S_t})
 >\frac b4|T|.
\end{align*}
For the middle inequality, restrict the kernel of the conditional
observation map to the smaller sum of matched spaces. Their restricted
rank is at most that of the failing full cores. A global deletion only
removes labels assigned to the deleted indices in other families, so
none of their potentials
increases. The sum of potentials, initially at most $P$, thus pays for
all deletions. Fewer than $4P/b$ selected indices are lost, leaving at least
\[
 \frac{\rho m_*}{16D_*}-\frac{4P}{b}
 \ge\frac{\rho m_*}{32D_*}\ge\frac{\rho m}{64D_*}.
\]
For each family $t$, every $T\subseteq I_{\rm sel}\cap L_t$ now has
joint core rank at least $\lambda|T|$ against that family's unassigned
blocks, on its fixed restriction. These inequalities hold on the
original source as well: for latent spaces $L\subseteq V$,
\begin{equation}
 r_L(A\mid C)=\dim A(L\cap\ker C)\le\dim A(V\cap\ker C)=r_V(A\mid C).
 \label{univ:eq:restriction-monotonicity}
\end{equation}
The family restrictions need not coincide.

\paragraph{Outside classes.}
Partition the blocks of each family by membership in its at most
$R$ recorded cuts, and restrict this partition to the unassigned blocks.
This gives at most $2^R$ classes, each lying on one side of every cut.
Because the cuts were taken in the complete original family, this
classification also applies to blocks that became unassigned when
selected clusters were discarded.
For one such class $C$, a set $T$ of surviving selected indices splits
into its part in $L_t$ and its parts in at most $R$ high groups. With $h=\lfloor\delta\ell/2\rfloor$,
\[
 r(U_T\mid U_C)\ge\max_j r(U_{T_j}\mid U_C)
 \ge\frac{\min\{\lambda,h\}}{R+1}|T|.
\]
Keep old outside classes, and put all discarded old clusters in one
additional class. The original certificate's private-rank inequalities
give joint threshold $\kappa$ against that class by a rank chain.
Unassigned fresh blocks stay in their family classes, so this is a partition of all original blocks.
The private-rank bounds remain valid after the deletions. Since $\ell\ge8(R+1)/\delta$,
$\lambda\ge h\ge2(R+1)$; the common integer threshold
$\min\{\kappa,\lfloor\min\{\lambda,h\}/(R+1)\rfloor\}$ is at least
$\min\{\kappa,\delta\ell/[8(R+1)]\}$.
<!-- end proof-110 -->
<!-- proof-111: body_md -->
Choose the constants in the following order; logarithms here are natural.
\begin{itemize}
 \item For normalization and the core ranks, set
 $\chi=\lceil4/\eta\rceil$ and $\rho=\eta/(4\chi)$.
 \item For cluster selection, set $d_*=\lceil12\chi/\rho\rceil$
 and $D_*=1+2d_*$. For assembly, then set
 \[
 \delta=\frac{\rho^3}{2^{20}\chi D_*},\qquad
 \alpha_p=\frac{\rho^2}{1024D_*}.
 \]
 \item Choose the number of independent families using
 $M_0=128(\chi-1)/(\alpha_p\delta^2)$ and $q=\lceil M_0^2\rceil$.
 The number of peeling rounds and the rank threshold before repair are
 \[
 R=\left\lceil\frac{2}{\delta}\ln(4q)\right\rceil,\qquad
 \beta_p=\frac{\delta^2}{32\ln(4q)}.
 \]
 \item For the final certificate, set $\alpha=\alpha_p/2$ and
 $\beta=\beta_p/4$. Its bounds on cluster size and the number of outside classes are
 $H=1+d_*$ and $Q=q2^R+3$. Choose the minimum block length so that
 \[
 \ell_0\ge\max\{4/\rho,8(R+1)/\delta,2/\beta_p\}.
 \]
\end{itemize}
Apply normalization with $\sigma=\eta/2$. At least $N/2$ blocks of
$X_0$ and $X'$ have rank at least $\eta\ell/2$. For every set $I$ of
these blocks, density implies
\[
 \dim U_I'\ge\chi^{-1}\sum_{i\in I}\dim U_i'
 \ge2\rho\ell|I|.
\]
Put $b=\lceil\rho\ell\rceil\le2\rho\ell$.
By Rado's theorem on linearly independent representatives~\cite{Rado42},
applied to $b$ copies of each $U_i'$, we may choose a $b$-dimensional
subspace of each $U_i'$ such that their sum is direct.
Apply selection to singleton clusters with $B=1$, $\Delta=0$, and
$k_0=\lfloor b/2\rfloor$. It retains at least $\rho N/16$ honest
singletons, with private threshold $k_0\ge\rho\ell/4$.
Treat these singletons as the old arrangement, with no outside classes,
and the remaining blocks as the fresh families. Removing the old
singletons from the $q$ families preserves their independence.

Assembly gives at least $\alpha_pN$ honest blocks, cluster bound
$1+d_*$, and at most $q2^R+1$ outside classes. Since
$R+1\le(4/\delta)\ln(4q)$, both thresholds are at least
$\beta_p\ell$, hence at least the integer $k=\lceil\beta_p\ell\rceil$.
Our choice $M_0\ge16$ ensures
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac q{\ln(4q)}&\ge M_0=\frac{128(\chi-1)}{\alpha_p\delta^2},\\
 W&\le\frac{(\chi-1)N\ell}{2q}
 \le\frac{\alpha_p\beta_pN\ell}{8}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed $M_0\ge\ln(4M_0^2)$ and $x/\ln(4x)$ is increasing in this
range. Repair with $\lambda=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ loses at most
$4W/k\le\alpha_pN/2$ targets, preserves the cluster bound, adds at
most two classes, and leaves threshold at least $\beta_p\ell/4$.
This gives the certificate in $X_0$. Transfer it to the original source
using Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:restriction-monotonicity}.
Finally, Eqn.~\eqref{univ:eq:spread} is hereditary under deleting
blocks, so the same proof and constants apply to every nonempty support.
<!-- end proof-111 -->
<!-- lemma-55: body_md -->
\label{formula:sparse-base}
For every fixed $0<\delta<1/4$ and sufficiently large $r$, one can
deterministically construct, in time $r^{O_\delta(1)}$, a system
$Ez=b$ over a field $\mathsf{F}_Q$ of characteristic two such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item $E$ has $r+1$ rows, $r$ columns, and row weight at most $s$, where
$Q$ and $s$ depend only on $\delta$;
\item for integers $\alpha,\beta=\Theta_\delta(r)$ with
$2\le\alpha$ and $2\alpha-2\le\beta$, every set of at most $\beta$
rows is independent;
\item $\operatorname{wt}(E^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\ge(1-\delta)r$ whenever
$\alpha\le\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)\le\beta$;
\item $Ez=b$ is inconsistent.
\end{itemize}
Here $\operatorname{wt}$ counts nonzero coordinates.
<!-- end lemma-55 -->
<!-- proof-112: body_md -->
The lossless-expander theorem of Capalbo, Reingold, Vadhan, and
Wigderson~\cite[Theorem~7.1]{CRVW02} supplies the following graphs.
For any fixed power of two $R$ and sufficiently large power of two $n'$,
there is a deterministically constructible left-$D_0$-regular graph
with $Rn'$ left vertices and $n'$ right vertices satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{formula:lossless-expansion}
 |\Gamma(S)|\ge\tfrac78D_0|S|\quad\text{for }|S|\le c n'/D_0.
\end{equation}
The constant $c>0$ is independent of $R$, and $D_0$ depends only on $R$.
Fix $0<\rho\le c/16$ and choose constants in this order:
\begin{itemize}
\item a regular graph of degree $d$ whose normalized adjacency operator
has norm at most $\theta$ on vectors orthogonal to the constants,
with $\theta^2\le\rho\delta/8$;
\item a power of two $B\ge d$ with $(d-1)/B\le\delta/8$, and $Q=B$;
\item a power of two $R\ge4B$, and the corresponding degree $D_0$.
\end{itemize}
For the spectral graph, a fixed power of the lazy
Margulis--Gabber--Galil graph gives exactly $u^2$ vertices for every
integer $u$, with a uniform spectral gap~\cite[Construction~8.1 and
Theorem~8.2]{HLW06}. Neighbor lists may repeat vertices and include
the vertex itself, so loops and parallel edges are allowed.

Choose the graph sizes in order as follows:
\begin{equation}\label{formula:base-sizes}
 \begin{aligned}
 u&=\lfloor\sqrt{r/B}\rfloor,\\
 n&=u^2,\\
 r_0&=Bn.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Let $n'$ be the largest power of two at most $n$, and set
$K=\lfloor c n'/D_0\rfloor$. Thus $n/2<n'\le n$
and $r-r_0=O_\delta(\sqrt r)$. Let
$H:\mathsf{F}_Q^{Rn'}\to\mathsf{F}_Q^n$ be the incidence map of the
lossless graph, padded with zero rows. Each column corresponds to a
left vertex, and its entry at a right vertex counts their incident
edges in $\mathsf{F}_Q$. If $0<|S|\le K$, at least
$2|\Gamma(S)|-D_0|S|\ge3D_0|S|/4$ right vertices receive exactly one
edge from $S$. Each gives a nonzero image coordinate, even in
characteristic two. Therefore every $\lambda$ with
$0<\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)\le K$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{formula:incidence-weight}
 \operatorname{wt}(H\lambda)\ge\tfrac34D_0\operatorname{wt}(\lambda).
\end{equation}
Take $\beta=K$ and $\alpha=\lfloor K/2\rfloor+1$. Since
$D_0K\ge c n'/2$ eventually, this gives
\begin{equation}\label{formula:constant-density}
 \alpha\le\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)\le\beta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{wt}(H\lambda)\ge3cn/32\ge\rho n.
\end{equation}

At each vertex of the spectral graph, regard its ordered $d$-neighbor
tuple as coefficients of a polynomial of degree at most $d-1$ and
evaluate at all $B$ field elements. This defines
$T:\mathsf{F}_Q^n\to\mathsf{F}_Q^{Bn}$. A nonzero tuple gives at least
$B-d+1$ nonzero evaluations. Since $B\ge d$ and every input coordinate
occurs in a neighbor tuple, $T$ is injective; its columns have weight
at most $dB$.
For $S=\mathsf{Supp}(y)$ of density $p\ge\rho$, the normalized adjacency
operator $P$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{formula:spectral-variance}
 \mathbf{E}_v(P\mathbf1_S(v)-p)^2\le\theta^2p(1-p).
\end{equation}
Thus at most a $\theta^2(1-p)/p\le\delta/8$ fraction of vertices have
no neighbor in $S$, and
\begin{equation}\label{formula:amplified-weight}
 \operatorname{wt}(Ty)\ge(1-\delta/8)(B-d+1)n\ge(1-\delta/4)r_0.
\end{equation}

Keep any $r+1$ columns of $TH$ and append $r-r_0$ zero rows, obtaining
$A\in\mathsf{F}_Q^{r\times(r+1)}$. There are enough columns because
$Rn'>2r_0$ and $r_0/r\to1$. Every column has weight at most
$s=D_0dB$, every set of at most $K$ columns is independent, and
Eqn.~\eqref{formula:constant-density} and
Eqn.~\eqref{formula:amplified-weight} give the required medium-weight
bound, since $(1-\delta/4)r_0\ge(1-\delta)r$ eventually.
Set $E=A^{\mathsf T}$. Find a nonzero $\lambda_*\in\ker A$, choose
$j$ with $\lambda_{*,j}\ne0$, and set
$b=\lambda_{*,j}^{-1}e_j$, where $e_j$ is the $j$th standard basis
vector. Then $\lambda_*^{\mathsf T}b=1$, proving
inconsistency. All graph parameters and auxiliary searches are constant
for fixed $\delta$; generation and Gaussian elimination take polynomial
time in $r$.
<!-- end proof-112 -->
<!-- lemma-56: body_md -->
\label{formula:legal-sets}
Let $E\in\mathsf{F}_Q^{m\times r}$, and fix parameters
$\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item $2\le\alpha$ and $2\alpha-2\le\beta$;
\item every subsystem of at most $\beta$ rows of $Ez=b$ is consistent;
\item $\operatorname{wt}(E^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\ge\gamma$ whenever
$\alpha\le\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)\le\beta$.
\end{itemize}
For $|D|<\gamma$, define
\begin{align}
 K_D&=\{\lambda\in\mathsf{F}_Q^m:\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)<\alpha,\quad
       \mathsf{Supp}(E^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\subseteq D\},
       \label{formula:multiplier-space}\\
 H_D&=\{z_D:(E^{\mathsf T}\lambda)_D\cdot z_D=\lambda\cdot b
                 \text{ for all }\lambda\in K_D\}.
       \label{formula:legal-assignment-set}
\end{align}
Then $K_D$ is linear, $H_D$ is a nonempty affine subspace, and
\begin{equation}\label{formula:projection-identity}
 \begin{aligned}
 \pi_C(H_D)&=H_C&&\text{for every }C\subseteq D,\\
 \operatorname{codim}H_D&=\dim K_D-\dim K_\varnothing.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Every member of $H_D$ satisfies every original equation supported on $D$.
<!-- end lemma-56 -->
<!-- proof-113: body_md -->
The sum of two members of $K_D$ has weight at most $2\alpha-2\le\beta$
and image supported on $D$. Since $|D|<\gamma$, its weight is below
$\alpha$. Scalar closure is immediate. An inconsistency in the equations
for $H_D$ would give $\lambda\in K_D$ with
$E^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0$ and $\lambda\cdot b\ne0$, contradicting
consistency of the fewer than $\alpha$ rows in its support. The kernel
of the coefficient map on $K_D$ is $K_\varnothing$, proving the
codimension formula. Eliminating $D\setminus C$ retains precisely
those combinations in $K_D$ whose coefficient images are supported on
$C$, namely $K_C$, with their original right sides. This proves the
projection identity. Finally, the unit multiplier of each row supported
on $D$ belongs to $K_D$.
<!-- end proof-113 -->
<!-- lemma-57: body_md -->
\label{formula:closure}
This maximizer is unique; $F[\overline{C(F)}]$ is safe; and
$k|C(F)|<\dim F$ if $C(F)\ne\varnothing$.
If $F\subseteq F'$, then $C(F)\subseteq C(F')$.
For $F'=F+\langle f\rangle$ with $f\notin F$, put $C=C(F)$ and
$C'=C(F')$. If $C'\ne C$, then
\begin{equation}\label{formula:closure-increment}
 \dim F'[\bar C']=\dim F[\bar C]-k|C'\setminus C|.
\end{equation}
Otherwise, the projected rank increases by zero or one.
<!-- end lemma-57 -->
<!-- proof-114: body_md -->
The function $h_F$ is supermodular: $(F\cap V_S)+(F\cap V_T)$ lies in
$F\cap V_{S\cup T}$ and the summands intersect in $F\cap V_{S\cap T}$.
Its maximizers are consequently closed under intersection and union,
giving the unique minimal one $C$. For $T\cap C=\varnothing$,
\[
 \dim(F[\bar C]\cap V_T)
 =\dim(F\cap V_{C\cup T})-\dim(F\cap V_C)\le k|T|.
\]
If $C\ne\varnothing$, then $h_F(C)>0$; otherwise the empty set would
also maximize $h_F$. This proves the first assertions.

For monotonicity it suffices to adjoin one independent form. Then
$a(S)=\dim(F'\cap V_S)-\dim(F\cap V_S)$ is increasing and takes
values in $\{0,1\}$: it is one exactly when the nonzero coset in
$F'/F$ has a representative supported on $S$. For any new maximizer $D$,
\[
 h_F(C\cap D)+h_{F'}(C\cup D)\ge h_F(C)+h_{F'}(D).
\]
Both left terms are bounded by their corresponding maxima, so $C\cap D$
is an old maximizer. Minimality gives $C\subseteq D$.
If $C'\ne C$, necessarily $a(C)=0$ and the maximum increases by one;
otherwise $C$ remains a new maximizer. Therefore
$a(C')=1$ and $h_F(C')=h_F(C)$, whence
$\dim(F'\cap V_{C'})=\dim(F\cap V_C)+k|C'\setminus C|+1$.
Subtract from $\dim F'=\dim F+1$ to obtain
Eqn.~\eqref{formula:closure-increment}.
<!-- end proof-114 -->
<!-- lemma-58: body_md -->
\label{formula:activation}
If the gadgets are surjective on every safe affine system, every viable
$\Phi$ of rank below $kw$ admits a viable answer to every parity query.
<!-- end lemma-58 -->
<!-- proof-115: body_md -->
For a queried form $f$, put $C=C(F)$ and $C'=C(F+\langle f\rangle)$.
Then $C\subseteq C'$ and $|C'|\le w$. Let $x^0$ witness viability.
Extend $G(x^0)_C$ to $z_{C'}\in H_{C'}$ by
Eqn.~\eqref{formula:projection-identity}. Fix the raw coordinates in
$C$ to those of $x^0$, retaining all equations of $\Phi$.
The remaining consistent system has safe row space $F[\bar C]$,
so surjectivity realizes $z_{C'\setminus C}$. The resulting full
solution $x$ realizes $z_{C'}$ and answering $f$ by $f(x)$ is viable.
<!-- end proof-115 -->
<!-- theorem-42: body_md -->
\label{formula:lifting}
Under \Cref{formula:legal-sets}, suppose $w<\gamma$ and the gadgets
are surjective on every safe affine system. Put $K_0=kw$.
Then $\Psi$ has $\operatorname{Res}(\oplus)$ width at least $K_0$,
and every $(K_0,b_0)$-path-free refutation has size at least
\begin{equation}\label{formula:path-free-bound}
 2^{K_0-b_0-(\ell-k)w}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-42 -->
<!-- proof-116: body_md -->
No viable system of rank at most $K_0$ falsifies an initial clause.
Indeed, falsifying a full clause fixes all raw coordinates of its
blocks. Each such block must belong to the closure: adjoining it
otherwise increases $h_F$ by $\ell-k>0$. A viability witness would
then violate a base row supported on its legal domain, contradicting
\Cref{formula:legal-sets}.
Starting at the empty system, \Cref{formula:activation} and weakening
therefore permit a walk through viable labels in any proof of width
below $K_0$. Such a walk must reach a sink, a contradiction. This
proves the width bound.

For size, retain the complete affine query history with row space $F$
until rank $K_0$ is reached, and put $C=C(F)$. Dependent queries are
forced. An independent query is \emph{free} if closure is unchanged
and its projection lies outside $F[\bar C]$. Either answer then
preserves viability: fix the old witness's raw closure coordinates
and solve the remaining affine system with that answer.
At every other independent query, choose a viable answer using
\Cref{formula:activation}, and call the query \emph{paid}.
Fix deterministic choices whenever several answers are possible.

The potential
\begin{equation}\label{formula:query-potential}
 P(F)=k|C(F)|+\dim F[\overline{C(F)}]
\end{equation}
starts at zero and increases by one exactly at free queries. At a paid
query with unchanged closure, the outside rank is unchanged; when
closure grows, Eqn.~\eqref{formula:closure-increment} cancels its
contribution to $P$. Hence every prefix pays at most
\begin{equation}\label{formula:paid-bound}
 \dim F-P(F)=\dim(F\cap V_C)-k|C|
 \le(\ell-k)|C|\le(\ell-k)w
\end{equation}
queries. No sink is reached before the threshold. A uniform raw
assignment gives an unbiased answer to each independent query,
conditional on its complete affine history. It agrees with all paid
answers, and therefore reaches the threshold viably, with probability
at least $2^{-(\ell-k)w}$.

At a successful stopping node $v$, its label is a weakening of the
history and hence viable. Write $d$ for its rank. If $d<K_0-b_0$,
restart the strategy from this label, keeping the new suffix history.
It cannot reach a sink before rank $K_0$, and so yields at least
$K_0-d>b_0$ independent forms modulo the starting label. The suffix
has at least that rank by itself, contradicting path-freeness.
Thus $d\ge K_0-b_0$. A consistent rank-$d$ label is satisfied by
exactly a $2^{-d}$ fraction of assignments. Taking a union bound over
stopping nodes gives
\[
 2^{-(\ell-k)w}\le |\text{refutation}|\,2^{-(K_0-b_0)}.
\]
The full history is used only to count paid queries; the restart begins
from the actual node label. Thus forgetting is permitted throughout,
and every rank and query cost is binary, without a factor of $\log Q$.
